entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; UI craft/accessibility checklist; DESIGN.md states/layers; component-island safeguards
principles: Reuse the project's existing accessible interaction primitives and avoid mixing primitive systems within one focus/keyboard surface; prefer native semantics when native controls solve the task.
Give icon-only actions accessible names, keep paste enabled, associate errors with the affected input/action and give empty states a clear relevant next step.
Account for dynamic viewport height and safe areas where the UI truly fills the viewport or uses fixed controls; avoid clipping normal content into an app-shell layout.
Use named depth layers and stable numeric glyph widths; test heading wrapping and body line endings in the actual font instead of forcing awkward manual breaks.
Keep feedback prompt, pause unnecessary offscreen loops, prefer inexpensive properties and avoid large animated blur/backdrop surfaces.
Use will-change only when profiling shows a benefit around active animation, and keep simple derived React state in rendering logic instead of redundant effects.
conflicts: Reject mandatory Tailwind defaults, cn, motion/react, tw-animate-css and React primitive packages for native HTML sites.
Reject blanket animation opt-in questions, 200ms cap, no custom easing/tracking, no gradients/purple and one-accent aesthetics; DESIGN.md and the authorized brief govern.
Reduced motion cannot remain merely SHOULD when the selected accessibility contract requires it; apply consistent preference handling to CSS and JS.
AlertDialog for every destructive action is overbroad: choose guardrails by actual consequence, reversibility and established platform behavior.
Line clamping and truncation are suitable for bounded dense UI, not a way to remove important service information or SEO copy.

entries.destination: references/design-contract.md: evidence, scope and reconciliation; assets/DESIGN.template.md: evidence-aware fields
principles: Separate repository documentation from public-site reconstruction. Repository evidence can establish governing tokens and ownership; a public page establishes observable behavior and computed values, not undisclosed rationale or internal architecture.

Trace each candidate as role → value → source → scope → recurrence → confidence. Prefer accepted DESIGN.md/guidance, active themes, shared primitives and rendered consumers before page-local literals.
Only inspect sources actually imported or rendered by the selected product. Exclude dormant migrations, examples and similarly named packages from normative token inference.

For a URL study record page, viewport, element role, computed value and matching loaded CSS/custom property. Promote an exact value when declaration and rendering agree or the role recurs across relevant samples; otherwise keep the observation scoped or omit the number.

Do not turn repeated literals or a framework utility scale into an intentional product token system. Preserve actual semantic names and accepted decisions; explicitly distinguish measured implementation from desired direction.
Every rule should change an implementation choice. Remove component inventories, duplicated token prose and generic instructions that add no decision.
Reconcile DESIGN.md against the loaded fonts, executable token definitions, themes and representative consumers. Record accidental drift for correction rather than rewriting intent to legitimize it.

If a project deliberately adopts a machine-readable token/export schema, validate category shapes and actual exported categories, not only a successful command exit. Preserve alternate-theme information and report exporter limitations honestly.
conflicts: Do not replace Web's established DESIGN.md dossier/template with mandatory alpha Google frontmatter, css-tailwind URL export defaults or npx @google/design.md commands.

Reject hiding all drafts until lint/export succeeds and forbidding provenance/conflicts anywhere in the design package. Keep source evidence and deliberate exceptions accessible through Web's linked reference records.

The source's fixed sample limits, exact section order and token naming omissions are its exporter contract, not universal design-document truth. For new design, explicitly chosen semantic tokens may be authored; they must not be mislabeled as observed upstream tokens.

The source is DESIGN.md-only; its prohibition on product edits does not restrict an independently authorized full website build. Conversely document-only work does not authorize implementation or deployment.
entries.reason: Strongest transferable evidence discipline for DESIGN.md in this batch. Keep methodology and reconciliation while preserving the canonical Web schema and source-linked dossier.

source.description: Create or update a DESIGN.md from an existing product repository or public website, with evidence-based design tokens and guidance.

principles: Turn a vague visual request into a brief with goal/audience, format, layout hierarchy, type roles, palette/material, imagery and exact supplied copy.
Lock layout, hierarchy and content before tuning style; vary one selected dimension at a time so the effect of a revision is understandable.
Keep explicit font/style/mode constraints in design records and generation prompts rather than relying on conversational memory.
Maintain a local source-linked reference pack and distinguish actual content references from style references.
Reserve clean text-safe space in generated imagery, then typeset important words as real HTML or a suitable editable design layer rather than accepting gibberish raster text.
Use spacing, contrast and hierarchy as specific review dimensions when improving a candidate.
conflicts: Do not render 'Constraints/FONT/STYLE/MODE' panels or internal prompt notes into visitor-facing UI.
One accent, no logos, six-column grids, named font vibes and fixed aspect ratios are examples or scoped image constraints, not brand-independent rules.
Figma is not a compulsory second-pass text provider; HTML/CSS remains the Web default and the existing GPT Image module owns image generation.
Do not impose a new interview or variant approval gate where the brief already resolves the direction.

entries.destination: Proposed topics for references/ui-skills.md / ui-playbook.md consolidation (parent owner to merge; neither reread nor edited): references/design-contract.md: page-intent contract; references/seo-pages.md; copywriting adapter and DESIGN.md page families.
principles: For a single-offer landing page, record audience, offer, incoming message/traffic source and one primary conversion action. Distinguish this scoped journey from a multi-intent homepage.
Make hero headline, clarifying subheadline, CTA and the most relevant truthful proof answer the visitor's immediate questions; align the promise with the ad/search/email that led there.

Choose structure according to persuasion needs: classic overview, educational long-form, short high-intent action page or evidence-backed comparison. Assign each section a job rather than copying a fixed sequence.
Write benefits as actual outcomes supported by specific product/service evidence; name the next step with a meaningful verb and destination.
Place proof beside its claim and move important objection handling earlier for a high-friction offer. Include genuine terms/trial/cancellation assurances only when the business actually offers them.
Iterate in bounded sections while keeping the complete journey coherent, then verify CTA consistency and mobile readability.

Make indexability a deliberate page-map decision based on lasting user value, duplication, campaign lifecycle and search intent. Provide appropriate metadata and crawlable internal links for indexable pages; keep useful Q/A readable.
conflicts: No mandatory counts of benefits, how-it-works steps or FAQs; no guarantee that the template converts better.
Reject invented savings, fake proof, default guarantees/free plans or a mandatory risk-reversal offer.
An ad-only page is not automatically noindex; a non-indexed parent/path does not itself noindex its children. Verify the actual directive and crawling behavior.
Plain FAQ text and eligible schema are not AEO/ranking/rich-result guarantees. Apply current truthful schema eligibility rules, not this checklist alone.
Do not substitute a single landing page for all agreed SEO subpages or restrict service content to arbitrary short copy.
entries.reason: Good page-intent, message-match and proof-placement principles when stripped of fixed funnel templates and SEO/conversion claims.

source.description: Use when designing or implementing a landing page with strong hierarchy, conversion flow, and visual pacing.

entries.destination: Web page-family briefs: pricing/offer comparison and enquiry decisions
principles: Design pricing around uncertainty reduction: who each offer fits, the billing/value unit, included limits, upgrade trigger and the next action.
Choose layout by the real pricing model: natural tiers, transparent usage calculator, separate audience paths, or self-serve plus sales-led enterprise.
Keep billing period, total commitment, usage math and annual savings explicit and verifiable; show variable starting prices only when true.
Group comparison rows by meaningful buyer concerns and highlight what actually changes between tiers.
Place truthful proof and clear cancellation/refund/trial/limit answers near the decision where they resolve objections.
Use CTA labels that accurately distinguish trial, purchase and sales contact, with a real destination for every action.
Adapt comparison content for mobile without losing plan relationships or hiding important limits; preserve semantic table structure when it is a true comparison table.
Provide a crawlable pricing/offer route with accurate title, metadata and internal links where such a page belongs to the business.
conflicts: Do not invent three plans, annual billing, a recommended or most-popular label, a free trial, response-time guarantee, discounts, security certification or social proof.
Plan/bullet/FAQ count limits and above-the-fold checklists are heuristics, not requirements that may suppress essential terms.
'High-conversion', emotion and SEO/AEO framing is not performance evidence; FAQ schema eligibility and current search guidance require separate verification.
Do not convert honest bespoke-service pricing into fake self-service SaaS tiers, or render all comparison data as cards when that obscures cross-plan comparison.
entries.reason: Useful optional page-family guidance when an offer actually has prices, packages or procurement decisions.

source.description: Use when building a pricing page with clear plan comparison, emphasis, and conversion-oriented layout.

principles: When Tailwind is already selected or a real component dependency needs it, check the installed version and source scanning configuration before adapting classes.
Use complete static class-name maps for finite variants and CSS custom properties for truly dynamic values; ensure templates and external/local component paths contribute to the production CSS.
Express hover/focus/active/disabled and responsive states using the existing token vocabulary, preserving actual semantic controls and visible focus rather than copying a visual CTA recipe blindly.
Extract repeated UI by semantic component/partial responsibility and use @apply sparingly; do not assume the order of class names determines the CSS winner.
Validate the production build's appearance and state coverage, especially when a dev environment appears to contain the needed classes by accident.
conflicts: Tailwind is not the default replacement for custom CSS, nor a justification for whole-site React.
Do not paste v3 content/safelist configuration into v4 without checking current syntax; zero-runtime utility generation does not mean zero CSS or dependency cost.
Sample indigo colors, rounded hero cards and English promotional copy are demonstrations, not a design direction.
Accessibility is a baseline design obligation, not an optional answer to a setup questionnaire.
entries.reason: Small but useful library/styling integration checklist, conditional to the selected tooling.

source.description: Use when you are implementing UI with Tailwind and want reusable, practical utility-first patterns.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md motion tokens and choreography; preserved Scrollcraft integration
principles: Define reusable motion primitives for fade/rise, scale/fade, sliding and shared-element changes, with purpose, duration, easing, offset, stagger and fallback recorded as one coherent system.
Use visual hierarchy to choreograph a sequence instead of animating all elements independently; choose a principal moment and quieter supporting motion when the brief calls for a narrative.
Treat micro 120–200ms, state 180–260ms, section 400–800ms and hero 800–1600ms as example tiers to tune, not a uniform duration for every surface.
For occasional scroll reveals, trigger meaningfully within the viewport and avoid repeated replay from tiny scroll changes; reduce stagger on narrow/mobile layouts when necessary.

Keep important content visible under reduced motion, disable nonessential pin/scrub behavior, avoid per-frame layout measurement and bound heavy canvas pixel ratio/effect areas according to measured devices.
conflicts: Stripe/Linear/Apple/Vercel are reference families, not mandatory brand aesthetics. No universal hero-first/headline-next/CTA-last sequence or field motion; primary actions must remain promptly usable.
Do not ask whether basic reduced-motion support is wanted. It belongs with the implementation.

Its exit ease-in suggestion conflicts with Emil's never-ease-in rule; select by direction, continuity and perceived responsiveness, and document the chosen token. DPR limits and timing numbers are contextual.
entries.reason: A concise motion-system vocabulary complements individual recipes without replacing existing Scrollcraft.

source.description: Use when building a coherent animation system instead of one-off motion tweaks.

entries.destination: Vorhandenes Motion-/Scrollcraft-Modul: einfacher progressiv verbesserter IntersectionObserver-Reveal
principles: Für einfache Sichtbarkeits-Reveals einen gemeinsamen IntersectionObserver und CSS-Klassen nutzen; threshold und rootMargin passend zur Elementgrösse und gewünschten Wahrnehmung wählen.
Einmalige Reveals nach erfolgreichem Eintritt unobserve; dynamisch hinzugefügte relevante Elemente bewusst registrieren und den Observer beim Ende des zugehörigen UI-Lebenszyklus bereinigen.
Animation-Keyframes, Dauer, Verzögerung und Transformation als normale benannte CSS-Regeln ausdrücken. Das Pattern benötigt weder Tailwind noch React noch ein neues Motion-Paket.

Der Grundzustand muss lesbarer HTML-Inhalt sein. Verbergen/pausieren erst nach erfolgreicher Motion-Initialisierung aktivieren; bei fehlendem JS, fehlender Observer-Unterstützung und reduced motion Inhalt sichtbar halten.

Replays mit tatsächlich zurückgesetztem Zustand implementieren und testen; zusätzlich direkte Sprunglinks, grosse Abschnitte, initial sichtbare Elemente, nachträgliches Mounten und schnelle Scrollrichtungswechsel prüfen.
Screenshot-Readiness darf nicht lediglich DOMContentLoaded bedeuten: den tatsächlich sichtbaren Endzustand oder einen deterministisch gesetzten Prüfzustand samt Motion-Präferenz erfassen.
conflicts: Die Quelle behauptet, once=false erlaube Replays. Ihr Observer entfernt die animate-Klasse aber nie und startet die Animation nicht neu; das Beispiel erfüllt diese Aussage nicht.
Opacity 0 plus animation-fill-mode:both und pausierter Animation kann Inhalt bei Initialisierungsproblemen dauerhaft verbergen. Kein unveränderter Codeimport.
DOMContentLoaded-Listener allein verpasst Initialisierung nach bereits geladenem Dokument; readyState oder Framework-Lifecycle berücksichtigen.
Bereits sichtbare Elemente sind nicht grundsätzlich ein IntersectionObserver-Problem: observe liefert regulär eine initiale Zustandsmeldung. Die Pitfall-Behauptung ist zu pauschal.
0.8 Sekunden, 30px Translation, 8px Blur und globale window-Namen sind keine Standards. Hohe threshold-Werte können bei sehr grossen Elementen nie erreicht werden.
entries.reason: Ein kleiner Vanilla-/CSS-Baustein passt zur Architektur, jedoch nur mit den ausdrücklich benannten Funktions- und Accessibility-Korrekturen. Kein zweites Scroll-System neben Scrollcraft einführen.

source.description: Use when you need scroll-driven motion that feels intentional instead of noisy or overdone.

entries.destination: GSAP integration notes within existing Scrollcraft module
principles: Use timelines with labels/relative overlap to coordinate multi-element motion rather than disconnected tweens; centralize defaults and intentional stagger.
For ScrollTrigger failures inspect trigger presence/height, nested scroller and overflow context before changing animation values.
Initialize after required font/image geometry is stable and refresh when late content actually changes layout.
Scope GSAP contexts and teardown to the owning component/route; prefer transform/opacity and measure before adding compositor hints.
Treat pin, scrub and snap as optional storytelling mechanisms with explicit small-screen/reduced-motion behavior.
conflicts: The global ScrollTrigger.getAll().forEach(kill) example can destroy other modules, including Scrollcraft. Kill only owned triggers.
No universal will-change or GSAP/React requirement. The source's snippets omit complete accessibility and failure fallbacks and are not production-ready simply because they run.
Fixed +=800 pin distances and transform percentages require content/breakpoint verification.
entries.reason: Operational GSAP concepts are useful only where the existing module and site brief need timeline/scroll complexity.

source.description: Use when implementing motion with GSAP and you want practical animation structure and sequencing guidance.

entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; existing references/scrollcraft.md choreography extension; DESIGN.md motion scenes
principles: Use a scroll story only when successive product states or workflow steps make the offer easier to understand; give each scene an explicit narrative job and timeline label.
Coordinate copy, images, overlays and UI states on one main scrubbed timeline instead of unrelated scroll handlers; reserve large transitions for meaningful scene handoffs.
Choose direct scrub for precise explanatory relationships and smoothing only when it helps the intended feel; set pin length according to actual content, not theatrical duration.
Prefer transform/opacity and measured quickSetter/quickTo updates; add will-change only where an observed problem warrants it.
Refresh trigger geometry when fonts, images or async content change layout; use scoped setup/cleanup so route transitions do not leave duplicate triggers.
Simplify desktop pinning for small screens and reduced motion, preserving a readable, ordered static narrative, usable links and visible CTAs.
Verify content visibility, contrast, scroll escape, image readiness and cleanup in both the enhanced story and the existing Scrollcraft still fallback.
conflicts: GSAP is the source's selected choreography tool, not a required replacement for vanilla CSS/JS or the existing Scrollcraft module.
Cinematic blur, depth, masking and pinning can undermine readability and performance; only use them with reference fit and measured evidence.
The source lacks explicit reduced-motion and no-JS handling; add these from the host architecture rather than claiming the source already supplies them.
Do not conceal indexable copy or require completing a long pinned animation to reach the enquiry action.
entries.reason: A focused optional choreography extension to existing motion infrastructure; avoids creating another media/scroll stack.

source.description: Use when building scroll-based storytelling sections with GSAP ScrollTrigger.

entries.destination: Optional Three.js technical appendix for justified 3D
principles: Use Three.js for actual 3D needs such as a product viewer or meaningful spatial visualisation, not merely because a hero needs decoration.
Keep a clear scene/camera/renderer/resource ownership model; update time-based animation and controls before rendering. Respect CSS canvas dimensions and update camera aspect/projection on resize.
Tune pixel ratio against target devices, use compressed models/textures and reduce lights/shadows or bake lighting where it preserves the intended result.
Tear down RAF, event listeners, geometries, materials, textures and renderer when the scene is no longer needed; account for shared resource ownership before disposal.

Render a deliberate still for reduced motion where appropriate and supply indexable HTML description/controls outside decorative canvas. Verify actual device interaction and loaded/failed asset states.
conflicts: No automatic whole React/R3F stack, continuous spinner hero, default cube palette or universal DPR=2 performance guarantee.
The sample RAF does not store a cancellation handle and is not a complete production lifecycle. Do not claim the minimal cube includes the prose cleanup/reduced-motion requirements.
No unrequested shader or 3D work; module complements rather than duplicates GPT Image/Scrollcraft. The inline source is not a substitute for installed-version API checks.
entries.reason: Small conditional technical reference for real 3D; its readable setup and teardown principles transfer cleanly to vanilla websites.

source.description: Use when building 3D scenes, interactions, or WebGL-backed interface moments in Three.js.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md: optional location globe; references/dependencies.md: Cobe version checks
principles: Use a small dedicated globe library when a globe and truthful location markers materially support the service/business story; a full 3D engine is unnecessary for that bounded requirement.

Coordinate CSS canvas size, drawing-buffer dimensions and the library's devicePixelRatio semantics. Recompute from the actual container on resize and verify crispness versus fill cost on target devices.

Separate ambient rotation from drag interaction, preserve phi/theta intentionally and destroy old instances on replacement/unmount. Check the installed version before relying on onRender, toggle or other lifecycle APIs.

Use actual latitude/longitude and brand-compatible marker colors, and provide equivalent location information outside the canvas. Add a still/fallback, reduced-motion behavior and offscreen/hidden pause using the stronger WebGL contract from this batch.
conflicts: The sample rotates continuously, recreates on every window resize and does not show final listener cleanup, reduced motion, no-GPU fallback or keyboard alternatives. It is not a ready production recipe.
DPR 1–2, map sample count and fixed angular increment are examples; verify library version and elapsed-time behavior rather than copying frame-rate-dependent rotation.
A globe does not require React/Next or a whole-app migration. The source contains no linked authoritative API docs; its API/version claims remain unverified in this extraction.
Do not ask placement/marker questions already answered by the brief or fabricate a global business footprint.
entries.reason: Narrow useful optional visualization, enriched by the batch's WebGL lifecycle/fallback lessons. Not a default hero asset or a replacement for Scrollcraft/GPT Image.

source.description: Use when building lightweight animated globe or orb visuals with Cobe.

entries.destination: Optional physics interaction appendix; motion lifecycle QA
principles: Use Matter.js only when 2D physical behaviour serves the experience. Decide engine/world ownership and debug versus custom renderer in the existing HTML/canvas/React context.
Use Composite to add bodies and constraints; choose either the supplied Runner or an owned Engine.update loop so timing has one owner.
Add mouse/touch constraints only for a real requested interaction; preserve page scrolling, text selection and equivalent non-drag/keyboard actions through the Web accessibility contract.
Plan responsive canvas/bounds, pause or still fallback when offscreen/reduced-motion, and teardown of runner, render loop, event handlers, canvas and world resources.
Inspect behaviour at actual viewport sizes and after repeated mount/unmount rather than considering the fixed 800×600 starter a finished responsive scene.
conflicts: No physics engine for routine button/motion polish, no automatic framework choice or perpetual offscreen simulation.

The source cleanup list stops Runner but omits Render.stop although the sample starts Render.run; stopping physics alone does not stop the render RAF. Mouse/listener cleanup also needs actual API verification.
The source minimal setup lacks full resize/accessibility/reduced-motion handling; do not present those as tested features of the sample.
Optional physics must not hijack normal page scrolling or displace existing Scrollcraft responsibilities.
entries.reason: Narrow physics option with useful lifecycle concepts; needs additional integration checks if ever selected.

source.description: Use when building physics-driven interactions and layout behaviors with Matter.js.

entries.destination: Optionale CSS-Effekte im Motion-/UI-Craft-Modul
principles: Progressive Randunschärfe mit überlappenden Masken und gestuften backdrop-filter-Ebenen aufbauen; Richtung, Ausdehnung und Intensitätsverlauf als zusammenhängenden Effekt abstimmen.
Das Overlay dekorativ und nicht interaktiv halten: pointer-events:none sowie eine bewusste Stacking-Ebene unter Modals und über dem vorgesehenen Hintergrund.
Den echten Hintergrund prüfen: backdrop-filter verändert dahinter liegende Darstellung; auf einer gleichmässigen Fläche entsteht kein sinnvoller sichtbarer Unschärfeverlauf.

Fläche, Anzahl der Layer und Blur-Stärke als Kostentreiber behandeln und auf Zielgeräten prüfen. Bei ungeeigneter Unterstützung oder Darstellung eine einfache Fläche/Transparenz ohne Filter verwenden.
Fokusindikatoren, Text, feststehende Navigation und Scrollziele im Randbereich bei mobilen und hohen Zoomstufen prüfen; der Effekt darf wichtige Inhalte nicht unlesbar machen.
conflicts: Die Beispielwerte bis 64px Blur und insbesondere 65 Prozent Höhe beim Bottom-Overlay sind keine sicheren Defaults; sie können einen grossen Teil der Seite unlesbar machen.
Top-DOM-Position und z-index:5 sind keine universelle Stacking-Lösung. CSS-Kontexte und vorhandene Dialog-/Header-Ebenen entscheiden.
Kein Pflichtfragebogen zu Position und Performance; DESIGN.md und vorhandene Komponenten liefern Routineentscheidungen.
Acht Layer sind kein Qualitätsziel. Pointer-Passthrough garantiert weder Lesbarkeit noch Accessibility.
entries.reason: Klarer, frameworkfreier Spezialeffekt, der nur bei gewählter visueller Richtung und nach Leistungs-/Lesbarkeitsprüfung passt.

source.description: Use when applying blur transitions or layered depth effects that need to feel smooth and controlled.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — optional CSS elevation recipes, mapped to DESIGN.md tokens
principles: Use distinct depth roles: compact controls receive a tight contact/ring shadow, cards/popovers a graduated ambient stack, and a rare large media/modal surface stronger lift.

The small recipe combines 0 2px 3px -1px black/0.1, a nearly invisible 1px contact layer and a 1px low-alpha ring; the medium recipe combines a ring with doubling blur/offset steps and negative spread. Preserve the layered mechanism when translating to custom CSS.
Tokenize one chosen shadow stack per state rather than stacking competing shadow utilities at call sites. Pair the stack with an intentional fill and radius.
Test the shadow at the actual component size and background; strong long-range elevation belongs to a large focal surface, not a dense list or tiny control.
conflicts: Exact Tailwind arbitrary utility classes are not a requirement. Translate the recipe into ordinary box-shadow tokens within the current custom CSS system.
Neutral shadows, exact strengths and the large 100px/80px final layer are optional treatments, not universal premium aesthetics. Consider clipping, dark mode, forced colors and render cost.
Shadows do not replace required control boundaries or focus indicators, and multiple supplied shadow sets are not a reason to add elevation everywhere.
entries.reason: A small, concrete recipe library useful only when the chosen design calls for layered elevation. No support documents are delegated.

source.description: Use when a UI needs better depth, elevation, and shadow treatment without looking muddy.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md-Logo-/Trust-Komponentenvertrag und bestehendes Assetregister

Authentische Wortmarken und Logos können unterschiedliche Formen besitzen; visuelle Kohärenz darf sie weder verfälschen noch zu einer erfundenen Einheitlichkeit zwingen.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md: structural container guides
principles: For a deliberately technical or editorial direction, reveal the main content bounds using subtle 1px guides and small corner/intersection marks rather than framing every nested component.
Use the same max-width and responsive inline-padding tokens for content and guide positions so marks sit on real container edges at every width.
Keep decorative layers noninteractive and within an isolated, intentional stacking context; ensure the guides sit above the background and below meaningful content.

Verify line-to-content spacing on mobile, corner alignment and contrast on actual backgrounds. Use physical corner geometry deliberately while retaining logical content layout where localization matters.
conflicts: The 1120px container, opacity values and 4–8px corner squares are sample style values, not Web defaults or a requirement for all service pages.
Viewport-based 100vw line positioning must be checked against the actual containing block and scrollbar behavior; shared tokens alone do not prove alignment.
Lines that merely add decoration or distract from offers should be omitted. Decorative spans can be avoided with CSS and must not create accessibility noise.
entries.reason: A concrete custom-CSS composition tactic, kept conditional on the chosen brand direction.

entries.destination: Optional short-heading motion recipe within Scrollcraft
principles: For a justified short heading reveal, use word masks with overflow clipping and a restrained word stagger; keep spaces intact and avoid splitting links, controls or meaningful inline markup.
Use reveal-once behavior and tune the source's top-82%, 0.7–0.9s, 25–45ms word stagger and 110% offset against the real font, line height and viewport.
Preserve full text for assistive technology without duplicate word announcements, and validate the resulting accessibility tree/reading behavior.

principles: The assigned file is only a loader: its substantive command.md was fetched and read. Extract current rule content with URL/date instead of attributing details to an unread link.

Prefer native action buttons and navigation anchors, explicit labels, decorative alt/hiding, appropriate landmarks/headings and skip links; provide keyboard operation and meaningful asynchronous status feedback.
Preserve visible focus and ensure sticky UI does not obscure it; use scroll offsets for anchor destinations and maintain focus styling across states.

Use correct field type/name/inputmode/autocomplete, clickable labels and paste support; associate errors with fields and show recovery guidance. Test request loading and failure rather than disabling completion pre-emptively.
Handle empty and long content, localisation expansion and flex min-width constraints without clipping essential text. Use Intl formatting and stable numeral widths for comparable values.

Reserve image dimensions, use responsive sources and lazy-load below-fold media; prioritise actual critical media and preload only necessary fonts/resources. Replace heavy decorative GIFs when a supported video/still approach is better.
Keep motion interruptible, respect reduced motion and provide pause/stop/hide for applicable continuing autoplay; supply meaningful media alternatives and gesture alternatives.
Make meaningful filters/pagination state linkable where useful, retain real link opening behaviour and protect destructive actions with a suitable confirmation or undo.
Record findings by source location plus observable issue and relevant route/state evidence; code lint and visual/interaction review complement one another.
conflicts: Command.md rules are heuristics, not WCAG or legal compliance certification. Native controls generally do not need redundant explicit keydown/up handlers; async semantics depend on message urgency and context.

Reject blanket autocomplete=off, title case/second-person/ampersand mandates, ellipsis requirements, every-state-in-URL and >50-items-must-virtualise rules. Preserve project language and actual product behaviour.
Do not solve overflow by hiding essential content or applying overflow-x:hidden indiscriminately. Do not treat truncation as the default answer for SEO text.
Transform/opacity and SVG wrapper claims need browser profiling; video in picture is platform-specific and needs a verified still fallback.

No mandatory fresh network fetch for every unchanged review, no unavailable WebFetch prerequisite, no forced library (nuqs/virtua) or automatic publishing. Current installed tool prerequisites still apply.

principles: Activate migration recipes only in an existing compatible Next.js App Router project with an explicit cache-adoption need. Resolve next.config and the real app directory first; inspect the installed version and runtime. The feature starts at Next 16, while this skill's instant-validation/codemod workflow assumes 16.3+; static export and Edge runtime are not equivalent deployment targets.

Preserve cache semantics when replacing dynamic/revalidate/fetchCache: record what varies per request or user, lifetime, invalidation and persistence. use cache's default per-instance memory and deployment-scoped keys differ from the previous fetch/unstable_cache stores; adding a directive alone is not a behavior-preserving migration.

Choose a data-level cache for shared computed/fetched data and a UI-level cache when the component result is the reusable unit. Set cacheLife deliberately; serialized arguments and captured values participate in the cache key. Read request APIs outside ordinary cached scopes and pass the needed values, not unresolved request-data promises.

Keep useful static content visible by placing Suspense near the actual request-time consumer. Forward params/searchParams promises into that child instead of awaiting them at the layout top. A partial-prerender glyph can still conceal an effectively empty shell.

Compare initial shell, fallback and resolved content in the browser, including direct load and client navigation; reserve realistic dimensions for fallbacks and keep the LCP element outside unnecessary boundaries. Recheck sibling routes when a shared layout changes.

Use dev overlay/log diagnostics together with the build: dev errors may accompany HTTP 200, and runtime API access inside a cached helper may pass build but fail under production serving. Read the exact version-matched error page instead of applying a generic Suspense recipe.

Document intentional instant=false exceptions rather than counting their presence as adoption; remove temporary opt-outs top-down and verify complete route paths. Explicitly test back-navigation behavior because Activity can preserve form inputs, modal state and scroll position.

Verify meaningful status codes, metadata and response content separately from pixels: headers cannot change after streaming starts. Check relevant browser and crawler user agents on the real serving stack; cache prerequisites must also be available at request time for paths that rerender for bots.
conflicts: Reject automatic next-dev-loop installation, bundler changes, upgrades, mandatory per-feature permission menus, commits/PRs and provider choices as global Web workflow.
Do not relocate authentication or authorization merely to clear prerender errors. Preserve the established protection contract; a cache key containing a user identifier is not authorization.
The migration guide states Next 16 for the feature; the assigned skill requires 16.3 for its newer workflow. Do not merge those into a universal minimum without the installed API check.

Official fetched pages are internally inconsistent about bots: caching broadly says bots get a complete dynamic document; streaming distinguishes HTML-limited bots and DOM-capable crawlers, and its demo prose again says full buffering. Preserve that uncertainty and verify actual responses.
Reject claims that a static shell, HTTP 200, successful build or Suspense adoption proves SEO, accessibility or field Web Vitals. No React or Next migration for service pages.

principles: Keep useful static content and layout stable while deferring only genuinely request-dependent leaves. If markup appears in both a loading fallback and the resolved tree, hoist the shared structure to avoid replacement, focus loss and skeleton drift.

Test hard navigation and real link-driven soft navigation separately; shared layouts and parallel slots mean they can expose different shells. Put dynamic boundaries below the relevant shared-layout divergence and in each affected server slot.

Reuse colocated loading components inside the same responsive layout as resolved content. Test both meaningful shell content and loaded output at desktop and mobile widths; a blank null fallback can pass a guard without helping visitors.

On a verified compatible Cache Components project, prove that the instant() test lock actually engages on a production-like test build. Check shell presence and gated dynamic absence; establish an unlocked baseline for the same account, route, role, flags and navigation type.

Use a failing-then-passing differential to establish that the refactor changes shell availability rather than merely the selector or environment. Assert the deployed revision when testing remote artifacts and verify post-load content, redirects, errors, state and focus parity.
Choose cache freshness per data source. Cache shareable stable data only when freshness semantics are known; keep request-specific fresh reads deferred rather than guessing cacheLife.

If useful content is inherently URL-specific, stop trying to manufacture a shared shell. In an already compatible Partial Prefetching setup, weigh targeted full prefetch for selected canonical links against added server work; do not blanket-prefetch every link.

Deferring an auth redirect into a sibling while rendering children unconditionally is unsafe as a general recipe. Authorization must still protect every data read, action and sensitive rendered subtree; successful eventual redirect is not proof that no data leaked.
instant() is a structural shell test, not elapsed latency, Core Web Vitals, crawlability or SEO proof. A heading is not automatically the page LCP element.
The sample cookies-to-UserMenu rewrite does not preserve a body-wide theme by itself. Review semantic parity rather than treating every before/after example as mechanically equivalent.

entries.destination: React-island performance checklist in component-islands/stack adapters
principles: Apply React-specific guidance only where actual React components exist; a useful shadcn component can be statically rendered or hydrated as a bounded Astro island without converting the whole website.

Prioritise avoidable data waterfalls and initial bundle weight before micro-optimisations. Start truly independent work together, defer awaits to branches that need them and preserve authentication/side-effect ordering.

Use explicit statically analyzable imports for optional heavy features; defer noncritical dependencies and consider intent-based preload when it benefits a real action. Use only supported typed package subpaths and inspect the built bundle.

Minimise props crossing server/client or island boundaries to fields actually needed. Keep request-specific state local to the request; shared caches need correct identity keys, invalidation and privacy boundaries.

Place submit/click side effects in their event handlers rather than a state-triggered effect that can rerun. Use narrow effect dependencies and clean up event listeners; keep transient pointer values in refs/direct transforms instead of rendering on every pointer event.
Use lazy initialisation for expensive initial state and memoise only measured expensive work; account for the installed React Compiler and supported APIs rather than adding manual memo everywhere.

Keep input updates urgent and defer expensive derived rendering where useful, exposing stale results honestly. Do not use a transition as a substitute for reducing unnecessary per-frame state updates.

Consider content-visibility with intrinsic placeholder size for long content; inspect search/find, focus, layout stability and real performance before virtualising. Preserve crawlable static content and accessible list/table semantics.
Batch layout reads/writes and prefer classes for shared states. Test hydration consistency, loaded fonts/images and theme changes rather than suppressing warnings as the default solution.
conflicts: No React/Next.js default, SWR/zustand/better-all mandate, automatic package install or app-wide migration. Next-specific RSC/Suspense/after/dynamic APIs do not transfer directly to Astro/vanilla.
Performance percentages, universal waterfall rankings, GPU claims and fixed list thresholds are source claims, not measured results for Raphael projects.
Generic typeof-window guards do not alone prove a module is excluded from server bundles. Verify bundler output and supported client boundaries; ssr:false examples need correct framework context.
Do not move filtering to the client when it increases data disclosure or payload. Do not ship private data for a low-level serialization optimisation.
Random IDs/dates are generally hydration bugs to resolve, not automatically expected differences; suppression or DOM mutation before hydration requires an explicit compatible case.
The compiled guide was fetched in full but only decision-relevant sections were read; remaining server/cache and micro-optimisation recipes are not extracted as verified implementation instructions.

Choose SSR or explicit static pre-rendered routes for public content needing initial HTML; enumerate dynamic paths when pre-rendering. An SPA fallback is not completed indexable content for every agreed service route.

principles: Record exact routes, states, public/authenticated context and device conditions; localize source inspection from actual rendered failures and separate measured defects from source-only hypotheses.

principles: Use AnimationClip for keyframe data, AnimationMixer for the animated root and AnimationAction for playback, looping and blending; update the mixer from one coherent time delta per frame.
Select numeric/vector/quaternion/color tracks by the property being animated. Use NumberKeyframeTrack for numeric morph influences and QuaternionKeyframeTrack for orientation.

Load and inspect GLTF clip names before binding actions. Crossfade actions with deliberate weights; additive layers need an appropriate reference pose, and LoopOnce plus clampWhenFinished can hold an intended final pose.
Keep procedural motion and clip-driven bone motion in an explicit update order so they do not accidentally overwrite each other. Cache bone/clip lookups outside a hot loop.

Share immutable clips across mixers where suitable, optimize redundant keyframes, limit active mixers and update offscreen content only when needed; use simpler distant rigs when complexity warrants it.
Isolate a justified 3D experience from the semantic page, pause it when hidden, offer a static/reduced-motion alternative and dispose resources when the section is removed.
conflicts: Three.js is optional and does not require React or a full application. Avoid adding real-time 3D where existing Scrollcraft pre-rendered media or ordinary imagery satisfies the brief.

The source contains illustrative defects: StringKeyframeTrack with string morph weights, resetDuration described as resetting the first frame, repeated Clock reads that alter the delta, and per-render callbacks that do not reliably detect future offscreen visibility.

The smoothDamp sample allocates several cloned vectors per frame and the simple Euler spring lacks a large-delta safeguard. Profile and harden actual adopted code rather than claiming these recipes guarantee smooth motion.
Examples use a global window.mixer and lack complete cancellation/disposal, reduced-motion and semantic fallbacks. These must be supplied by the Web adapter.

Kontrast am tatsächlichen Farb-/Hintergrundpaar messen und relevante Information zusätzlich zur Farbe vermitteln. W3C bestätigt 4.5:1 für normalen Text, 3:1 für grosse Schrift mit Ausnahmen; keine abgeschnitten gerundeten Werte als Pass ausgeben.
Automatische Befunde und incomplete-Ergebnisse getrennt behalten; Dialogfokus, Tastaturbedienung, sinnvolle Fehlertexte, Medienalternativen und tatsächliche AT-Ausgabe manuell ergänzen.

Bei Medien genau zwischen Audio-only, Video-only und synchronisierten Aufnahmen unterscheiden. SC 1.2.3 erlaubt Audio Description oder vollständige Medienalternative; AA 1.2.5 ist eine zusätzliche Anforderung, sofern die nötige visuelle Information nicht bereits im Audiotrack vermittelt wird.

Kontinuierliche automatische Bewegung mit wirksamem Pause/Stop/Hide-Verhalten und statischem Reduced-Motion-Zustand planen. Flashing separat nach den tatsächlichen allgemeinen/roten Flash-Schwellen beurteilen.
conflicts: Legal baseline, Most regulations, ADA/Section508 und 'VPAT compliance' sind keine tragfähigen Rechts- oder Konformitätszusagen. Ein Skill oder automatischer Scan zertifiziert keinen Rechtsstatus.
30–50 Prozent automatisch erkennbare Probleme sind keine universelle Abdeckungsquote und wurden hier nicht als gemessene Zahl übernommen.

Der Detailkatalog verkürzt SC 1.2.3 auf Pflicht-Audiodeskription, vermischt Textresize/Reflow und fordert für 2.4.4 uneingeschränkt isolierte Linkverständlichkeit. Korrekte Kriterien und Ausnahmen separat konsultieren.
'Flashing kleiner als 25 Prozent Viewport' ist kein korrekter allgemeiner Schwellenwert. Der gelesene W3C-Text definiert Schwellen im relevanten Sichtfeld, Frequenz, Luminanz und Rotanteil.
Die Contrast-Fix-Skizze nennt #767676 ohne Hintergrund fälschlich 2.5:1. Kontrast hat immer zwei Farben; ihre Werte nicht als geprüfte Resultate kopieren.

div-role-button/-checkbox und der Custom-Combobox-Schnipsel implementieren keinen vollständigen zugänglichen Interaktionsvertrag. Native Controls oder tatsächlich geprüfte Bibliothekskomponenten verwenden.

entries.destination: Web dependencies / inherited Vue and Pinia state-management adapter
principles: Apply to viable inherited Vue projects that use Pinia, or to an explicitly selected Vue/Pinia stack. Inspect existing store IDs, Option versus Setup Store conventions and installed versions; preserve the viable architecture instead of converting it to Astro/React.
Use storeToRefs(store) when destructuring reactive state or getters; ordinary destructuring loses their reactive connection. Actions are bound and can be destructured directly.

In Setup Stores, use ref for state, computed for getters and functions for actions, and return all state properties needed for Pinia tracking, SSR and tooling. Preserve existing Option Stores unless the task gives a concrete reason to change their form.

Use $patch for coherent grouped updates. Option Stores provide $reset; Setup Stores require an explicit reset implementation when the UI needs reset behavior. Define the intended reset state rather than assuming both store forms behave identically.

A getter returning a function does not cache each parameterized result. Where repeated filtering is costly, compute the stable filtered set in the getter and perform the parameter lookup against that set; verify actual usage before adding optimization.

For SSR, create a fresh Pinia instance per request to avoid cross-request state pollution. Pass the correct instance when using stores outside setup, such as navigation guards; resolve dependent stores before awaiting asynchronous work rather than relying on ambient context after await.

Hydrate the client Pinia state before the first dependent useStore call, and align server-prefetch/loading behavior with the inherited framework so the initial client UI reflects the rendered server state.

Pair server serialization with the matching client deserializer for the installed library version and actual output format. The source juxtaposes a devalue example with JSON.parse without establishing compatibility; verify the pair, safe HTML embedding and round-trip state reconstruction instead of copying it as a working security recipe.

Keep $subscribe and $onAction lifecycle ownership explicit. Retain and invoke unsubscribe handles where needed; detached subscriptions deliberately survive component unmount and require an owner. Persistence examples do not justify storing every state field or exposing sensitive state in browser storage.
conflicts: The HTML/custom-CSS/vanilla default is a default for suitable new work, not an exclusion of viable inherited Vue projects. Conditional Pinia guidance does not authorize framework migration, adding Pinia to unrelated projects or rewriting every store into Setup form.

The SSR example combines a devalue serialization example with JSON.parse hydration without establishing compatible formats/version imports. Its safety and runtime behavior were not tested; confirm serializer/deserializer compatibility and safe HTML embedding before implementation.

The snapshot targets Pinia v3.0.4. Core stores and SSR references were fully read; plugins, composables, Nuxt, testing, HMR and external serializer references remain ancillary_not_read. Do not claim those extensions or current runtime compatibility were verified.

Do not import mandatory HMR, @pinia/testing installation, blanket persistence or store scaffolding. Reuse the inherited project conventions and actual installed framework/tool prerequisites; add mechanisms only for the requested behavior.
entries.reason: Conditional integration for viable inherited Vue/Pinia projects: the fully read core and SSR references supply concrete reactivity, reset, subscription, request-isolation and hydration mechanisms. entries.destination: Existing Vue application compatibility appendix; never the routing default for HTML service pages
principles: When an existing Vue route reuses a component with a new parameter, watch the relevant parameter or use an update guard; initial mounted hooks and per-route beforeEnter do not cover every param/query/hash navigation.
Await or return asynchronous guard work and provide explicit pending/error outcomes. Use return-based guards for simple decisions; if next is used it must resolve exactly once per path.
beforeRouteEnter cannot access an instance before creation; the supported next(vm => ...) callback can access it after confirmation. Update/leave guards operate on the reused/live component.
Exclude public/error/redirect destinations from circular guard logic and verify direct entry, param change, refresh, back/forward and cancellation.
Keep cleanup symmetrical for hash/listener-based routing and guard browser globals in SSR; avoid old requests overwriting new-route state when asynchronous loads race.
Treat client guards as navigation UX, with authorization enforced by the server. A network/auth timeout must not silently grant access.
Use the official router's actual versioned API and hosting history fallback when maintaining an application; preserve initial HTML, real page URLs and search requirements for public Web routes.
conflicts: All eight delegated guides were read, and several contain errors. Official navigation-guards documentation confirms next remains supported, async guards may return undefined to allow navigation, beforeEach precedes beforeRouteUpdate and errors may be thrown to trigger router.onError.

Reject the guide's remove-all-next mandate because beforeRouteEnter's instance callback is valid. Its valid awaited-return example is incorrectly marked wrong, and its param-update execution-order table is incorrect.
Reject timeout/network-error examples that allow protected navigation, and the claim that client guards prevent security issues by themselves.

The production recipe advertises a bare loader field as Vue Router 4.2+ data loading and gives an empty view-transition setup; these claims are unverified by the fetched official guard document and must not be used without versioned API evidence.

The redirect-depth sample adds 1 to a query value without parsing it; async watcher examples omit cancellation/race control, and window access in setup is not SSR-safe. Do not copy the sketches wholesale.
Do not introduce Vue/SPA routing into a static site or claim history URLs require Vue Router. Framework/library selection must follow actual application complexity.

principles: Test through the public interface: meaningful props/slots, visible text, role/name queries, actual user actions and observable outcomes; avoid private component state as the main assertion.
Use focused structural snapshots only as supplementary regression evidence. Read changes instead of blindly accepting updated snapshots and add behavioral checks for actual controls.
Run style/layout/focus/drag/viewport-sensitive checks in a real browser; a simulated DOM or a class-presence assertion cannot prove the pixels or native interaction.
In Vue tests await trigger/setValue and the appropriate reactive update; distinguish nextTick from external promise completion and use observable readiness/polling where needed.
Choose tests by the behavior at risk and existing project tools; keep logic tests, browser component checks and complete user journeys as complementary evidence.

The browser-vs-node source overstates lack of all cookie/computed-style support in simulated DOMs; the material distinction is absence of a real layout/rendering/native platform, not that every API always returns empty.

principles: In einem bereits gewählten Vue-/Nuxt-Projekt Anforderungen zuerst einer passenden Composable zuordnen und deren konkrete Referenz sowie installierte Version prüfen; der lange Katalog ist ein Suchindex, keine pauschale Importliste.

Die gelesene useEventListener-Referenz liefert automatische Abmeldung beim Unmount, eine manuelle Cleanup-Funktion und Ab-/Neuanmeldung bei wechselnden reaktiven Targets. Diese Lebenszyklusgarantien bei Bibliotheksauswahl und eigener Vanilla-Implementierung ausdrücklich prüfen.
Direkte document-/window-Zugriffe erst im Client ausführen; useEventListener mit bereits ausgewertetem document ist trotz Composable nicht automatisch SSR-sicher. Die Referenz zeigt dafür onMounted.

usePreferredReducedMotion liefert 'reduce' oder 'no-preference', keinen Boolean. Bewegung anhand des tatsächlichen Werts reduzieren und den statischen Zustand bereits beim Rendering sinnvoll festlegen.
useIntersectionObserver bietet Support-, Pause- und Stop-Steuerung sowie root, rootMargin und threshold. Offscreen-Medien und Reveals gezielt steuern und Observer beim Ende ihres Nutzens stoppen.

useFocusTrap ist eine Integration mit eigenständiger focus-trap-Abhängigkeit. Bei v-if den DOM-Aufbau mit nextTick abwarten; alternativ mountgebundenen Wrapper verwenden. Aktivierung, Deaktivierung und Fokus-Rückgabe müssen im realen Dialog geprüft werden.

Preserve native button/link semantics, real href navigation and modifier-click behavior; ensure focus stays visible and unobscured by sticky chrome, with skip navigation and anchor scroll margins.

Provide pointer/tap and keyboard alternatives to drag/swipe/path gestures, preserve safe areas and native scrolling, and guard autoplay with reduced-motion behavior and applicable pause controls.

Localize dates, times, numbers and currency with Intl and real locale context. Keep server/client initial content deterministic and isolate intentional client-only differences instead of broadly suppressing hydration warnings.

Virtualizing every list over 50 items or every large map is arbitrary and can harm accessibility, find-in-page and indexable content. Measure first; content-visibility is not DOM virtualization.

entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; DESIGN.md motion language; motion critique checklist
principles: Define duration/easing tokens for related interactions so similar operations feel consistent, with timing chosen by task frequency, distance and total perceived delay.
Give immediate activation feedback and use an entrance that settles promptly; keep exits purposeful and avoid slowing high-frequency menus or repeated controls.
Use one dominant animated focal point at a time; subordinate surrounding movement and backdrop emphasis to the primary task.
When physical overshoot genuinely communicates the interaction, use a tunable spring and restrained deformation; verify interruption and the reduced-motion equivalent.
Limit cumulative stagger across long lists rather than checking per-item delay alone; make content usable before decorative staging finishes.
Coordinate animated surfaces with the existing stacking model and accessible dialog behavior; record exact file/state defects instead of declaring a style preference a runtime failure.
conflicts: The title overstates coverage: the source is a selected web-rule checklist, not a complete treatment of all twelve Disney principles.
Reject universal 300ms/50ms caps, identical timings for all similar elements, scale on every pressed control, no context-menu entrances and fixed ease-in/ease-out rules.
Linear motion is appropriate for direct scrub/constant-speed processes; its ban conflicts with scroll-driven motion and must be contextual.
A hardcoded z-index:50 is not a stacking solution; prefer existing tokens and primitive/top-layer behavior.

entries.destination: references/design-contract.md: bounded design comparisons; references/ui-playbook.md: interaction stress tests
principles: Use an exploratory comparison only when a real hierarchy, layout, density, interaction or expressive-direction decision remains open. Keep the same realistic fixture content across alternatives so the comparison measures design rather than content completeness.

Read existing tokens, representative buttons/cards/forms, package conventions and prior design decisions before sketching. Put inferred visual language, tasks, pain points and must-keep constraints in the brief without repeating questions already answered.

Each alternative needs a distinct question and tradeoff: reorganized importance, list versus table versus split pane, compact versus spacious density, or inline edit versus dialog/drawer. Avoid merely swapping color or radius.

Record feedback against a variant and identifiable element, with selector plus human description where useful. Read overall direction first, then synthesize explicitly chosen traits and preserve the rationale in DESIGN.md.

The delegated DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md adds a concrete robustness matrix: rapid repeated activation, rapid typing and resize, interrupted opening/closing, navigation during transitions, slow/offline/timeout requests, state combinations and observer/listener cleanup.

For gesture-heavy controls, distinguish press, drag and click using a movement threshold and pointer capture; update continuous position without a full component rerender per frame; settle on release. Provide non-gesture alternatives and preserve native scrolling where possible.
Use optimistic feedback only for recoverable operations with explicit saving, rollback and retry states; retain actual server confirmation as the success authority.

Use content-driven layout and intrinsic grid stacking when overlaid elements must contribute to parent height. min-width:0 resolves flex text shrinkage; distinguish overflow:clip from a scroll container and preserve access to clipped content.

Track temporary preview ownership explicitly and remove only owned temporary routes when appropriate. Save the selected design and implementation decisions before cleanup so a successful exploration remains reproducible.

Next App Router __design_lab is a private-folder-style name and needs routing verification; do not promise a URL without testing it. Cleanup instructions also conflict over route ownership and DESIGN_KEEP_LAB.

The delegated reference contradicts itself on sentence/title case and entrance/exit easing. Treat its 8px grid, navigation counts, one-primary-action rule, exact spring parameters, 50-row virtualization threshold and 44px target wording as contextual heuristics.

Do not copy hover-only table actions, a whole-card click handler with nested controls, the native img priority attribute, universal clip-path GPU claims, blanket touch-action:none or every-state-on-every-component boilerplate.
The reference's named-company attributions and claims that single-column forms outperform alternatives are not accompanied by empirical citations. No conversion or compliance claim follows from them.

principles: For closely nested rounded surfaces, relate outer radius to inner radius plus intervening padding; for well-separated surfaces choose independently. Inspect actual corner shape rather than applying the equation to every nested container.
Correct optical imbalance in icon/text controls and play triangles; treat 1–2px adjustments and icon-side padding as starting hypotheses checked at render size.

Use shadows for elevation where appropriate while preserving borders that communicate structure, input boundaries, selection or keyboard focus. An inset image outline can separate a photo without changing layout dimensions when it fits the design.

Use balance for short headings and pretty for suitable short/medium copy; verify browser support and actual wrapping. Use tabular figures for updating numbers and numeric columns, and inspect the chosen font's numeral appearance.

Prefer retargetable transitions for interactive state changes and one-shot keyframes for staged sequences. Test rapid reversal; frequent interactions need immediate or minimal feedback, and every animated state also needs a static cue.

Cross-fade contextual icons in a stable-size wrapper without a new dependency; only use Motion APIs when the installed package/import path matches. Decide first-render animation separately from subsequent state transitions.
Specify exact transition properties and add will-change only for a measured first-frame problem, accounting for layer memory and the browser's real compositor behavior.

Make small controls easy to target without overlapping neighboring hit areas; the source's 44px touch/40px dense-desktop sizes are design preferences to evaluate alongside actual accessibility criteria.

Use coherent icon geometry/strokes, currentColor for monochrome state tinting, accessible names on icon-only controls and hidden decorative icons. Test the smallest rendered size and flip only reading-direction glyphs in RTL, preserving logos and media controls.

Inspect all relevant states and replay motion at 10% speed to diagnose timing/exit defects, then judge it again at normal speed. Report location, evidence, severity, actionable change and user impact, explicitly marking uninspected areas.

entries.destination: Web DESIGN.md semantic color tokens and contrast/gamut QA
principles: Use OKLCH when it improves palette editing: define lightness, chroma, hue and alpha independently and inspect the resulting rendered colors.
Generate scales with hue-aware gamut checks at every lightness level; reduce chroma where necessary rather than allowing unexpected gamut clipping.
Keep an sRGB-compatible base and use wide-gamut enhancement conditionally; provide a syntax fallback where supported browsers require it.
Measure actual foreground/background pairs, including opacity compositing and image/gradient backgrounds, after every contrast or gamut adjustment.

Use WCAG 2.x contrast for a WCAG 2.x claim: normal text 4.5:1 AA and large text 3:1 AA, with large text defined as 18pt (24 CSS px) or 14pt bold (about 18.67 CSS px), subject to the criterion's details.
Use APCA only as additional perceptual guidance with its correct polarity and typography context; it does not replace the selected WCAG conformance criterion.
When converting syntax, preserve CSS behavior and alpha, leave currentColor/transparent/inherit and third-party hex-only API inputs intact, and report the actual changed tokens.
Map light/dark themes by semantic role and verify each relevant state; reversing a numeric ramp is only a candidate, not proof of readable dark mode.
conflicts: Supporting contrast table incorrectly uses 18px/14px instead of points, and reverses APCA polarity: positive is dark text on light, negative is light on dark.
Reject L>0.6 and lightness-gap thresholds as proof, and 'contrast controlled by L alone/chroma never matters' as an absolute; conversion, gamut and actual luminance still require calculation.
Equal OKLCH steps/relative chroma do not guarantee identical perceived readability or vividness across all contexts; do not claim perfect uniformity or stable hues without limits.
Do not mandate converting every valid existing color, ban intentional hue drift, require Tailwind v4, or present APCA thresholds as generic legal compliance.
The palette reference calls nine steps a Tailwind default despite its own eleven-step @theme example; choose the project's real token scale.

principles: Inspect motion at normal speed and deliberately slowed playback to locate timing, alignment and removal defects; preserve the existing component library, density and motion vocabulary.

Use concentric radius math for visibly close surfaces with an even inset, not for independent/asymmetric containers. Correct icon/text alignment optically after rendering, preferably in the SVG geometry when the same defect repeats.

Separate depth from structure: a layered transparent shadow can express lift while input outlines, dividers, focus and selected boundaries retain their functional role. Tokenize the chosen treatment and verify dark/forced-color states.

Use interruptible CSS transitions for frequent state changes. Keep both icons in a stable layout for a dependency-free crossfade; use the already-installed Motion import path only when that library is genuinely present.
Reserve stagger for infrequent semantic entrances and keep exits softer when they add spatial context. Suppress unwanted initial icon animation without disabling intentional page motion.

Avoid whole-page color smearing during theme changes by applying a short-lived transition suppression around the actual theme update, then restoring it after style commit; respect the project’s existing theme implementation.

Choose one coherent icon family, use currentColor for state color, compare stroke weight with adjacent text and inspect icons at their smallest render size. Mirror only icons whose meaning is direction-dependent.
Every animated state change needs a persistent static cue. Give high-frequency interactions immediate feedback or minimal transitions, and add will-change only for a demonstrated first-frame issue.

Not every button/image needs motion or an outline. Preserve transparent assets, meaningful borders, native affordances and reduced motion rather than applying a global polish transform.
CSS keyframes/WAAPI can be controlled and interrupted with explicit logic; the source’s transitions-versus-keyframes table is a useful default, not a technical impossibility claim.
Box-shadow/filter animations in its own recipes can incur paint cost. Favor small measured effects or opacity layers instead of treating will-change as guaranteed GPU acceleration.

The icon demo buttons omit accessible names/state and the paired icons need decorative semantics to avoid duplicate announcements. A slowed visual pass does not replace keyboard/screen-reader verification.

entries.destination: Colour systems, semantic tokens and contrast evidence in DESIGN.md/UI playbook
principles: Keep an established colour notation consistent. For a new system, perceptual OKLCH/OKLab tooling can generate ramps while emitting the project's desired notation; format migration must be deliberate.
Define neutral/accent/status ramps according to roles that actually render. Preserve exact fixed brand colours and build suitable action/text steps around them instead of quietly darkening the brand.

Separate hue primitives from semantic roles; add component-level tokens only for meaningful scoped divergence. Text, separators and control boundaries remain distinct even when values currently match.
Treat Radix steps as role-based and Tailwind steps as lightness-based; map roles explicitly across themes rather than pretending the numbering systems are interchangeable.
Generate ramps with perceptual lightness, controlled hue/chroma and gamut checks; reduce chroma where needed and verify adjacent steps remain distinguishable after rendering.
Use one coherent theme-switch mechanism respecting a user's override; light-dark() follows color-scheme, so a manual theme control must update the same source of truth.
Measure foreground against its actual surface, accounting for alpha, imagery, filters and every relevant state/theme; report exact computed/observed pairs and identify checks not performed.

Choose gradient interpolation deliberately: rectangular OKLab versus polar OKLCH gives different hue paths, and shorter/longer hue selection matters. Inspect worst-case text contrast across the gradient.
Check load-bearing semantic colours against audience conventions, including locale-dependent financial gain/loss colours; add text/shape cues so colour is never the only meaning carrier.
conflicts: Reject automatic one-accent/one-filled-action mandates, a universal 15-degree hue-equivalence threshold, compulsory two themes and bans on pure neutrals. Preserve established brand and component hierarchy.
APCA can supplement typographic judgement; its simplified thresholds are not WCAG 2 conformance or automatic legal compliance. Correct 14pt bold to about 18.67px, not 18.5px.

The palette-generation reference says contrast is asymmetric without distinguishing algorithms. WCAG 2 ratios are symmetric for the same two opaque colours; APCA is polarity-aware and changed theme pairs still need separate checks.

P3 without an explicit fallback does not universally fail to render; gamut mapping/clipping depends on browser/support. Similarly, derived colour expressions can be evaluated when all inputs are known, although real composition still needs browser verification.
Do not merge by popularity or near-value alone: preserve semantic roles and scoped/theme behaviour, applying token-consolidation's stronger dependency checks.
Reject report-only/change-only-on-separate-request rules when contrast repair is already authorized. No arbitrary blocking/approval ritual replaces the current task.

The Tailwind example maps --color-text-secondary but claims text-secondary; verify the actual generated namespace (normally text-text-secondary for that token). Do not reproduce example class names blindly.

Serve appropriate licensed WOFF2 files. Compare static versus variable transfer size for the actual used weights; a variable file is not automatically smaller when only one or two faces are needed.

Test headings, labels, captions and long prose at real text lengths. Body leading around 1.5–1.6 and a roughly 60–75-character measure are useful starting points; multiline descriptions need more leading than short display text.
Use balance for suitable short headings and pretty for suitable short descriptions; protect layout from long URLs/IDs, and use nowrap only where content still fits at narrow widths and larger text.

entries.destination: Accessibility QA ledger and browser checks in screenshots/ui-playbook
principles: Recognise the actual source identity: this compatibility ID resolves to accessibility-inspect, a hands-on interaction assessment rather than only colour contrast.

Report impact severity separately from evidence basis. Attach selector, state, interaction and observed DOM/a11y-tree fact for reproducible findings; mark interpretive judgments and actual AT experience separately.
Close each scoped criterion as verified, flagged, engine-owned, not applicable or not exercised/undetermined. Do not convert skipped features or a clean scan into a sitewide accessibility pass.

Use a settled page snapshot to map landmarks, names, states and feature triggers. After interaction inspect the affected widget and use real Tab/Escape/Enter/Space/arrows to verify traversal, dismissal and operation.

Use DOM focus/box measurements as candidate evidence, not proof of actual keyboard traversal or screen-reader announcements; inspect focus visibility and sticky-overlay obstruction in rendered states.
Exercise 320 CSS-pixel reflow, text-spacing overrides, zoom, reduced motion and meaningful contrast across hover/focus/background-image states; label CSS zoom approximations honestly.
Submit invalid forms, verify error associations and recovery, check label-in-name/state changes, and test pointer/keyboard alternatives for dragging and composite widgets.
Deduplicate current automated findings while retaining manual interaction checks; for untested AT behaviour provide a precise flow and AT check rather than simulate a screen-reader user.
conflicts: Reject hard one-screenshot/zero-driving evidence budgets and any cap that prevents resolving a concrete issue. Existing valid evidence can be reused without a quality ceiling.
A scripted focus() sequence cannot establish real Tab order, operability or lack of traps. Geometry alone also cannot certify complete target-size conformance.
Checkpoint one-h1/no-skip rules are useful structure heuristics, not universal WCAG pass/fail laws. Account for target-size exceptions and criterion levels; 2.3.3 is not an AA-only rule.
Reject universal automated defect-catch percentages and site conformance claims from a single page or partial sample. A11y-tree presence does not prove actual announcements.
No automatic browser/CLI installation, mandatory AccessLint tool chain, source-only TODO for labels, or refusal to fix already-authorised issues. Preserve actual installed browser prerequisites.

entries.destination: Accessibility QA evidence model and state coverage
principles: Treat this source by its actual contents: accessibility-inspect, a manual browser tier, not a link-purpose-only rule.

Report user-impact severity separately from evidence confidence. Attach selector, interaction and observed DOM/accessibility-tree fact to reproducible findings; distinguish interpretive review and untested assistive-technology behavior.
Maintain coverage states for applicable criteria: verified, flagged, not exercised, N/A and engine-owned. Never convert an omitted check or an empty scanner result into a pass.

Use a page snapshot to identify landmarks, custom widgets and relevant checks; after state changes inspect the changed subtree. Use scripted focus/geometry to find suspects, then real keyboard input to validate operation and traps.

Exercise forms with invalid input, associated errors and recovery; inspect custom control name/role/state changes, sticky-overlay focus obstruction, small targets, drag alternatives, media controls and reduced motion where present.
Evaluate narrow reflow, text resizing, text-spacing overrides and orientation; explicitly label CSS zoom as an approximation rather than actual browser zoom.

For site-wide assessments, define scope and sample distinct routes, templates and states; prepare concrete AT follow-up flows for announcement and real-user behavior that browser DOM inspection cannot establish.
conflicts: Reject fixed one-selector/one-screenshot evidence caps and zero-driving rules when further evidence would improve the assigned outcome; retain calibrated uncertainty without artificial limits.
Do not import the ~57%/~80% coverage claims as project evidence or compliance guarantees. An accessibility tree is not screen-reader output; ARIA presence alone is not a passing announcement test.

The detailed checkpoints oversimplify normative rules: one h1/no skipped headings is a heuristic, SC 2.4.4 allows link purpose in programmatic context, 24px targets have exceptions/spacing cases, and SC 2.3.3 is AAA. Verify criterion applicability rather than labeling all these AA failures.
Programmatic focus does not establish true sequential keyboard reachability or every composite-widget contract. Do not require each roving-tabindex child to be a separate Tab stop.
Use available browser tools; no forced Chrome MCP installer. A one-page manual review remains a valid scoped review even though it is not a full site-wide conformance assessment.

entries.destination: Web screenshot/accessibility QA evidence contract
principles: Record impact severity separately from evidence basis: reproducible DOM/interaction fact, visually informed judgment, or a task requiring real assistive-technology testing.
Give each in-scope check an explicit outcome: verified pass/fail, flagged, engine-owned, not applicable, or not exercised/undetermined. Missing coverage is never a pass.
Ground each finding in route/state, selector, real interaction and observed result; associate screenshot evidence with the affected state and only cite source locations actually established.

Use automated scans and manual interaction as complementary evidence. Scripted focus() and computed outlines are diagnostic probes; real Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter/Space/arrows and Escape verify keyboard behavior.
Exercise form error recovery, reflow, text spacing, reduced motion, sticky-overlay focus visibility and gesture alternatives where the page uses those features.
Keep accessibility-tree state distinct from what a screen reader actually announces; specify the browser/AT and exact task for any unperformed announcement check.
Use WCAG 2.5.8's 24×24 CSS-pixel minimum with its spacing, equivalent, inline, user-agent and essential exceptions; 44×44 is a useful larger touch target, not the same conformance threshold.
Preserve all-route Web delivery QA; use representative sampling only for an explicitly bounded audit and report its scope.

Reject one-screenshot evidence caps, zero-driving human-required caps, tool-installation demands and any cost policy that leaves useful authorized checks undone.
Do not turn 'one h1/no skipped headings', bounding-box-only target assessment, or a single main-landmark heuristic into universal WCAG pass/fail rules.
SC 1.4.4 text resize and SC 1.4.10 reflow are distinct; CSS zoom is an approximation and must be labeled. Actual 400% browser zoom is not established by a resize alone.
Do not infer screen-reader experience, percentages of accessibility coverage, or full legal compliance from automated/manual proxies.
