entries.destination: DESIGN.md-Motionvertrag, UI-Craft-Referenz und references/screenshots.md
principles: Vor jeder Bewegung Zweck und Wiederholungsfrequenz nennen. Häufige Arbeitsaktionen dürfen nicht auf dekorative Animation warten; räumliche Orientierung, Statuswechsel und unmittelbares Eingabefeedback sind belastbare Zwecke.

Dauer und Easing als komponentenbezogene Tokens dokumentieren: kleine Controls eher kurz, grosse Flächen entsprechend ihrer Bewegung; die Quellwerte von etwa 100–250 ms sind Startwerte für Erprobung, keine Abnahmeschwellen.

Ankergebundene Popovers vom tatsächlichen Trigger aus skalieren, inklusive veränderter Platzierung; zentrierte Modals behalten einen zentralen Ursprung. Bei gestalterisch passender Skalierung mit kleinem Delta und Opazität statt scale(0) beginnen.

Bei schnell umschaltbaren Zuständen unterbrechbare CSS-Transitions oder gezielt steuerbare WAAPI bevorzugen. Gestenfedern nur einsetzen, wenn ihr Umgang mit Geschwindigkeit und Richtungswechsel einen konkreten Vorteil bringt.

Tooltip-Gruppen können beim ersten Hover verzögert, innerhalb der bereits aktiven Gruppe unmittelbar reagieren. Toast-Timer bei verborgenem Tab pausieren und Hover-Lücken zwischen gestapelten Toasts vermeiden.

Drag-Interaktionen mit Pointer Capture, Schutz vor zusätzlichem Touch-Pointer, passenden Grenzen sowie Distanz und gemessener Geschwindigkeit prüfen. Eine Flick-Schwelle benötigt definierte Einheiten und Geräteprüfung.

Nur die tatsächlich benötigten CSS-Eigenschaften transitionieren. Hochfrequente Werte möglichst am bewegten Element setzen, statt über vererbende Custom Properties unnötig grosse Unterbäume zu invalidieren.

Hover-Bewegung auf geeignete Pointer beschränken und für reduced motion einen eigenständig nutzbaren Zustand vorsehen. Stagger darf Interaktion nicht sperren oder wichtige Inhalte verzögert zugänglich machen.

Animationen normal, verlangsamt und an kritischen Einzelbildern ansehen; Ursprung, doppelte überblendete Texte, Synchronität und schnelle Richtungswechsel prüfen. Bei Gesten echte Touch-Hardware verwenden, wenn verfügbar, und sonst die Testgrenze nennen.

@starting-style als progressive CSS-Verbesserung für Eintritte prüfen; Prozenttranslationen eignen sich für elementgrössenabhängige Drawer. Clip-Path-Reveals und Vergleichsbilder nur mit zugänglicher Bedienung und unverändertem semantischem Inhalt einsetzen.
conflicts: Begrüssungs-/Wartepflicht und vorgeschriebenes Before/After-Tabellenformat sind keine Web-Workflow-Gates.

'Nie Tastaturaktionen animieren', 'nie ease-in', 'immer custom easing', 'nur transform/opacity', 'jede Schaltfläche skalieren' und pauschale 300-ms-Grenzen zu kontextabhängigen Heuristiken abschwächen; die Quelle selbst nutzt abweichende Drawer-/Toast-/Height-Beispiele.

CSS, WAAPI, transform und clip-path sind nicht in jedem Browser und jeder Kombination garantiert compositor-/GPU-beschleunigt. Aussagen über Motion-x/y und transform-Strings sind versions- und pfadabhängig und benötigen Profiling.
Die Spring-Mausbeispielzeile beweist keine vollständige reaktive Verdrahtung. Velocity 0.11 und Blur unter 20 px sind keine universell sicheren Werte.

Duplizierte Tab-Overlays dürfen keine doppelt fokussierbaren/angesagten Controls erzeugen. Hold-to-delete braucht eine zugängliche Alternative; reduzierte Bewegung kann auch vollständigen Verzicht erfordern.
'Am nächsten Tag prüfen' ist eine mögliche Perspektive, keine Pflichtpause. Ein schneller Spinner ist kein Beleg für geringere tatsächliche Ladezeit.
entries.reason: Sehr reichhaltige frameworkunabhängige Craft- und Motion-Quelle. Die technischen und ästhetischen Absolutheiten müssen vor der Konsolidierung von den konkreten Interaktionsprinzipien getrennt werden.

principles: Show press feedback on pointer-down while committing ordinary actions on release/click; support cancel-by-dragging-away rather than triggering destructive actions on pointer-down.

For justified draggable sheets, sliders or carousels, preserve grab offset, use pointer capture and track recent position/time samples for release velocity; retain keyboard and single-pointer alternatives.

Make gesture transitions interruptible from the current on-screen value and carry velocity into the next motion. Test grab-during-close and immediate reversal rather than waiting for transitions to finish.

When spring interaction is appropriate, start with little or no overshoot; reserve bounce for a momentum-bearing gesture. Project a landing point from release velocity, then choose a permitted snap target.

Document motion origin and direction: overlays should grow from their trigger and reverse coherently. Progressive resistance at real boundaries should remain responsive without hijacking native scrolling.

Record separate reduced-motion, reduced-transparency and increased-contrast behavior. Replace large motion with static or short opacity feedback, make translucent surfaces solid when needed, and preserve all actions and information.
Tune tracking, leading, weight and optical sizing by type role and actual font; allow rem/em-based text growth and layouts that reflow with zoom.
Inspect motion at normal speed and with slow/frame inspection where necessary; judge continuity, jump-free reversal, interaction latency and real device behavior in addition to frame rate.
conflicts: Apple visual language, system fonts, glass chrome, rubber-banding, sound and haptics are conditional references, not universal aesthetics or dependencies. The brief and business identity govern selection.
Reject the absolute claim that CSS transitions cannot be redirected and the mandate to use springs for every touchable control; choose the simplest sufficient implementation and measure it.
The source both recommends animating blur and says only transform/opacity are allowed. Profile actual effects; avoid transition-all and needless will-change, and retain static fallbacks.

WWDC claims and exact Apple-shipped values are secondary-source assertions without linked primary material here; do not present them as independently verified measurements. A normalized velocity division needs a zero-distance guard.
Labels are not evidence of weak mapping: required visible/accessible names remain. Native platform close-button placement is not automatically the correct web convention.
entries.reason: Highly relevant interaction principles translate to vanilla JS and optional islands; integrate the behavior and QA guidance while treating Apple styling and numerical recipes as conditional.

source.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

entries.destination: Web references/creator-methods.md + screenshots.md: motion audit and concrete remediation
principles: Inventory motion engines, token definitions, component primitives, gesture paths, product personality and frequency before judging isolated declarations.
Audit eight distinct concerns: purpose/frequency, timing, physical origin, interruption, rendering cost, accessibility, token cohesion and useful missing continuity.
Validate findings in the actual code and rendered behavior; exclude deliberate documented tradeoffs, duplicate symptoms and legitimate centered modal origins.
For reversible state changes use transitions that retarget from current values or suitable springs; gesture motion needs velocity-aware settlement and sensible resistance at boundaries.
Keep popovers anchored to their trigger, frequent interactions responsive and useful state feedback available under reduced motion. Hover-only motion needs appropriate hover/pointer media conditions.
Consolidate near-identical motion values into existing semantic tokens. Separate corrective defects from optional delight/continuity opportunities; no animation is a valid outcome.
A remediation brief should include current revision, real locations and code evidence, desired behavior/values, existing conventions, scope boundaries and reproducible acceptance steps.
Verify by rapidly toggling, interrupting/reversing, checking slowed playback/frame sequences and exercising reduced motion. Mechanical correctness alone cannot establish motion feel.
conflicts: Do not adopt the advisor/executor hierarchy, cheaper-model language, mandatory subagents, top-3–5 cap, plans-only refusal or mandatory user-selection stop as Web workflow.
AUDIT.md says UI stays below 300ms but allows 200–500ms modals and 0.5s springs. Treat values as starting examples, not contradictory release gates.
Universal ease-in failure, pure-fade failure, required press scaling/stagger and all-keyboard-motion bans are stylistic overreach. Prioritize accessible function and actual latency.
Transform/opacity-only, a fixed <20px blur rule, all Motion shorthand acceleration claims and a universal gesture velocity threshold are technically/contextually overbroad.
The reducer must not interpret reduced motion as requiring opacity animation in every case. An immediate state change with clear feedback can be appropriate.
entries.reason: Full SKILL, delegated AUDIT.md and PLAN-TEMPLATE.md read. Adopt its evidence-rich audit categories and concrete verification, replacing fixed values and workflow gates with project-specific decisions.

source.description: Survey a codebase's animation and motion code as a senior motion advisor, then produce prioritized audit and self-contained implementation plans. Read-only on source code - it plans improvements, it does not apply them. Use when the user asks to improve animations, audit motion, make an app feel better, or wants a roadmap of animation fixes rather than a review of a single diff.

entries.destination: Motion decision model and recipes, extending existing Scrollcraft
principles: Choose motion by frequency, purpose and functional impact before choosing a curve: feedback, spatial continuity, state indication, bridging a change or a justified explanatory/celebratory moment.

Reuse project motion tokens. Prefer CSS transitions for state/hover/press, starting-style for progressive entry, CSS keyframes for predetermined sequences and WAAPI for programmatic control; use an existing suitable library when dynamic layout or gesture complexity warrants it.
Prefer transform/opacity for movement, small scale entrances rather than unnecessary scale-from-zero, and an origin at the trigger for anchored surfaces; centered modals are a different spatial case.

Rapidly repeatable state changes should retarget from the current visual state; gesture motion should preserve continuity/velocity through interruption. Pair entry/exit paths with the surface's spatial relationship.
Use timings as tunable starting ranges: press 100–160ms, tooltip/popover 125–200ms, dropdown 150–250ms; tune longer surfaces to distance and function rather than applying one number everywhere.
Ship reduced-motion behavior and fine-pointer/hover capability gating together with motion. Keep functional states perceivable and content usable when movement is reduced or disabled.
Tooltip groups can open subsequent tooltips instantly after the first delay. Synchronize modal/backdrop changes; keep decorative stagger from delaying interaction.

For drag, handle pointer capture, multitouch exclusion, resistance at boundaries and distance/velocity dismissal. Inspect slow playback, intermediate frames and actual gestures when code cannot settle feel.
conflicts: Reject absolute no-animation rules for keyboard actions or 100+/day frequency, exact-table-only curves, forced library picking and universal sub-300ms caps; the source's own toast/drawer recipes exceed the cap.
CSS/WAAPI and transform/opacity are not unconditional off-main-thread/GPU guarantees; the blanket Motion shorthand claim is version/path dependent. Validate the chosen implementation under load.
Do not require a fade under reduced motion; immediate state changes can be appropriate. Do not use blur to conceal incorrect state/timing or accessibility defects.

The hold-to-confirm recipe is only visual feedback, not a complete safe interaction; duplicate-tab overlays need inert/decorative semantics and unique IDs. Native height interpolation support must be checked before blindly importing measured-height recipes.
entries.reason: Useful ordered motion reasoning and concrete recipes; retain existing Scrollcraft and tune to the real site rather than adopting this source's absolute aesthetic gates.

source.description: Build an animation from scratch, making the decisions in the order that determines whether it feels right — should it animate at all, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve and duration, how it interrupts, how it exits. Writes the implementation. Use when asked to animate something, add motion, make a component feel alive, or build a transition. For critiquing existing motion use review-animations; for auditing a whole codebase use improve-animations.

entries.destination: Web motion craft reference: cross-platform interaction principles only; native implementation stays with Expo specialists
principles: Choose whether to animate from purpose and frequency before choosing an engine. Frequent controls need immediate, low-amplitude feedback; rare explanatory moments can support more motion.

Touch interfaces require visible press and positional affordances instead of hover dependence. Start feedback on press-in and commit on a valid release; preserve usable hit areas and cancellation behavior.

For a drag release, preserve velocity and current position, test flick and slow drag separately, and allow interruption/reversal. Consider dismissal by velocity or distance rather than distance alone.
Keep continuous animation updates out of React render state. On the web use the existing suitable CSS/WAAPI/motion mechanism; the transferable rule is avoiding a full application render each frame.
Crossfade a static expensive visual layer instead of continuously recalculating blur or shadow geometry. Check the real rendering cost and layer memory.

Reduced motion and scaled text are part of the initial behavior contract. Avoid fixed expanded heights that break with larger text; evaluate on representative slower real hardware when gesture feel matters.
conflicts: Reanimated 4, worklets, Gesture Handler, Expo Router native sheets/tabs, expo-haptics, Yoga, Babel and iOS configuration are native-only and must not enter the canonical Web implementation instructions.
Transform/opacity are not free, every other property does not necessarily trigger layout, and 100 daily uses is not a defensible universal animation cutoff.
Native 44pt/48dp guidance is not a CSS-pixel WCAG conformance rule. Web targets and interaction semantics require their own actual criteria.
No forced dependency installation, native platform replacement, exact spring-config mandate or refusal to build requested motion solely because a stylistic table says no.
RECIPES.md is unread ancillary native implementation material, not missing required web substance.
entries.reason: Main SKILL fully read. Select only gesture, input-mode and performance principles with explicit web adaptation; do not transplant the native recipe/runtime stack.

source.description: Build animations in React Native and Expo, making the decisions in the order that determines whether they feel right — should it animate, which thread it runs on, which properties, spring or timing, how the gesture hands off, how it degrades. Writes the implementation with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and expo-haptics. Use when animating anything in an Expo app, adding gestures, sheets, screen transitions, press feedback or haptics, or fixing motion that stutters on device. For web animation use animate.

entries.destination: Proposed topics for references/ui-skills.md / ui-playbook.md consolidation (parent owner to merge; neither reread nor edited): references/component-islands.md and references/dependencies.md: Sonner notification adapter; DESIGN.md feedback states.
principles: For actual Sonner reuse, mount one deliberate shared Toaster client boundary and invoke toast from client-side results/events. Avoid one instance per page/island; if multiple regions are intentional, give them ids and target toasterId explicitly.

Model pending/success/error honestly: use toast.promise for a settling promise or update the same stable id when managing state yourself. Do not emit success from a server action without handling its result in the client.
Keep notifications persistent only when needed and provide an accessible dismissal/action path; distinguish timeout onAutoClose from manual onDismiss in behavior and tests.

Wire theme explicitly because the documented default is light, and map tone, typography, spacing and offsets into the existing design system. Use custom/headless rendering only when the desired design warrants its extra ownership.
In Astro/view-transition integrations, test stylesheet retention and explicitly import sonner/dist/styles.css in a persistent layout if injected styles are lost.

Test duplicate effects in React StrictMode, clipping/stacking contexts, modal interactions, narrow-screen offsets, text direction, keyboard access and live-region labeling. Static build-time rendering alone cannot deliver toast interactions.
Use the read API table for exact options such as containerAriaLabel, testId, mobileOffset, toasterId, duration and dismissible, then confirm the installed version's types.
conflicts: Do not introduce whole-site React or Sonner for feedback a native inline status can serve. Interactive Sonner requires hydration, not merely static shadcn rendering.
Do not apply important to every class blindly; inspect actual cascade/layers/version and prefer a coherent wrapper when warranted.
Moving a Toaster to document root or increasing z-index does not guarantee visibility above a native dialog's top layer; verify the actual overlay behavior.
Ephemeral toast alone is not sufficient for critical field errors or proof of submission receipt; keep persistent relevant status and accessible error association.
Package/API details are source evidence, not tested behavior in an installed application during this research.
entries.reason: Especially relevant to real React component islands and Astro stylesheet loss, with the full delegated API reference read.

principles: Scope evidence: the file teaches Swift value semantics, actor isolation, Sendable, structured concurrency, ARC, Swift Testing and Swift 6 migration; none supplies a browser/UI implementation contract for the HTML/CSS/vanilla or Astro-island stack.

entries.destination: Reference research; DESIGN.md; screenshot and interaction QA; optional advanced effect analysis
principles: Distinguish faithful reproduction, visual adaptation, content adaptation and technical teardown before judging success. For MAKE Web default to transferable, source-linked patterns and the client's own content.
Inspect real source or deployed assets when available; label technical conclusions SOURCE, PARTIAL or GUESS and attach the relevant code, runtime observation or captured state.
Inspect representative routes and templates, not only the homepage: use navigation/sitemap/footer links to identify home, listing, detail, search/filter and contact patterns.

Capture comparable desktop/tablet/mobile views and hover, click, scroll, drawer, validation, loading, empty and error states. Record console/network evidence and honestly identify interactions that automation did not exercise.

Translate references into three design layers: measurable tokens/layout, interpreted visual style/composition/voice, and special effects with technology, intensity and fallback. Carry these into DESIGN.md rather than requiring another giant schema.

For exact complex-effect reconstruction, establish a minimal reproducible baseline before refactoring. Inspect pass order, coordinates, timing and resource bindings; do not conceal a wrong model by tuning brightness, speed or noise.

Capture runtime-loaded assets by exercising the page; static URL scraping can miss fonts, binary geometry, WASM and scroll-loaded media. Keep an asset manifest with request status and local provenance.

Compare reference versus implementation by module and state with differences and evidence; keep a content/media/token replacement map and remove unintended original-brand/tracker dependencies from authorized adapted work.

For optional heavy rendering, separate rendering, composition, physics, interaction and audio; stop rendering settled scenes and consider reduced-resolution auxiliary buffers when visually acceptable.
conflicts: Reject personal /Users/jane paths, forced scaffolding/Node versions/provider switches and the assumption that identifying React in a reference requires a React rebuild.
Public deployed assets do not grant reuse rights. Reject wholesale mirroring as the default, blanket license simplifications, and instructions to bypass font domain licensing through self-hosting.
The directive to reuse original images instead of AI generation must not replace Raphael's existing GPT Image module; choose authorized original, supplied, licensed or generated assets by brief.

Complexity-based fidelity percentages and the example's 5/5 score are source claims, not guarantees. Runtime capture is not universally complete and different initial states do not prove correct physics.

Exact-replay gates are useful for an explicitly faithful effect reconstruction, not for ordinary reference-informed design. No blanket requirement to obtain original source before implementing an independently designed page.
entries.reason: Eight supporting references make this a substantial source for traceable design research, multi-route coverage and reproducible effect QA, after removing copying and workflow mandates.

source.description: 网站复刻 / 克隆方法论。Use when the user says to clone, reproduce, or recreate a website or WebGL/Canvas/Three.js effect. Covers source-first reconstruction, repo scaffolding, reverse engineering, implementation paths, and verification for static sites, content sites, and heavy front-end experiences.

entries.destination: Optional interaction-audio appendix; only when sound is selected by the product brief
principles: Reuse an AudioContext and handle its suspended state after an appropriate user gesture; wait for/respect resume failure before relying on playback.
Disconnect finished audio nodes and release sources after playback so repeated interactions do not accumulate a graph.
Set an initial positive gain before an exponential decay, and use a small positive endpoint rather than zero to avoid invalid exponential ramps.
For a short tactile click, start with a brief filtered noise burst; for a tonal confirmation use an oscillator with intentional pitch movement. Tune duration, frequency, Q and gain by listening.
Translate specific feedback into parameters: harshness can suggest lower cutoff/Q, muffling higher cutoff, abrupt ending a different envelope, and excessive prominence lower gain.
Keep sound supplemental to visible/accessible state feedback and expose a way to control or mute it when the feature uses audio.
conflicts: No sound on service sites by default. The source's 5–15ms, 3–6kHz and Q 2–5 ranges are a particular click recipe, not universal correctness requirements.
Gain <=1 does not by itself prevent clipping when signals sum or filters resonate; oscillator/noise and linear/exponential envelope choices are contextual. Inspect output and loudness.
The resume example does not await the promise, and its cleanup example must include all nodes in the actual graph. Adapt rather than copying it as complete lifecycle handling.
Do not require a sound provider, add audio automatically or classify a different sound aesthetic as a runtime defect.
entries.reason: Self-contained procedural Web Audio rules have a narrow optional use; they are not core page design. MDN overview remains ancillary because no recommendation relies on unseen content.

source.description: Audit Web Audio API code for procedural sound synthesis quality, UX decisions, and parameter best practices.

entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; React-island Motion adapter; native CSS presence alternative; motion QA
principles: For an existing Motion React surface, keep AnimatePresence mounted outside the condition removing its child and assign stable data-derived keys to direct children.
Run presence hooks inside descendants; disable exiting interactions and coordinate focus restoration with the accessible primitive rather than leaving a visually departing control actionable.
Choose sync for concurrent entry/exit, wait for an intentional one-child sequence and popLayout when departing list items should free layout space. Budget the combined sequence duration.
Use propagate on the relevant nested presence boundary only when child exits should run when that boundary leaves; coordinate parent/child timing with the intended story.
If removal is manual, ensure safeToRemove runs after completion and has an error/cancellation path; test interrupted transitions and route unmounts.
Official Motion documentation adds popLayout's custom-child ref forwarding and non-static parent positioning requirements; verify these against the actual React/Motion versions.
For native HTML dialogs/popovers, consider CSS @starting-style plus appropriate display/overlay allow-discrete transitions instead of adding Motion/React solely for entry/exit.
For CSS presence, distinguish first-render starting, visible and default exit styles; defer actual DOM removal when needed, preserve reduced-motion behavior and test target-browser support.
conflicts: Exit need not mirror initial: the official documentation itself shows directional slides entering from one side and exiting the other.
sync does not universally cause layout conflicts; popLayout, propagate and a 300ms total are scenario choices, not mandatory fixes for every presence wrapper.
cleanup().then(safeToRemove) leaves removal hanging on rejection. Some examples omit keys despite the key rule and do not supply the ref contract for custom list items.
The native CSS alternative does not automatically delay Element.remove(); the MDN example explicitly delays removal. @starting-style alone is not full presence management.
Do not add a whole React app or an animation package for this audit; bind it to an existing/justified island and keep accessible focus semantics independently verified.
entries.reason: Useful targeted Motion lifecycle checks and a source-backed native CSS alternative; official documentation narrows several overbroad rules.

source.description: Audit Motion and Framer Motion exit/presence patterns with practical fixes for AnimatePresence usage.

entries.destination: Web motion micro-patterns and bounded component islands
principles: For small line-based icons that should morph, normalize them to the same viewBox and a fixed three-line topology.
Represent unused segments as zero-length center lines with opacity zero so interpolation preserves element identity.
Share base geometry for rotational variants; animate rotation within a related family and reset rotation immediately when moving to an unrelated family.
Use rounded line caps and consistent stroke geometry so endpoints remain coherent throughout the morph.
Provide an immediate reduced-motion state update and test repeated/interrupted transitions.
Hide an icon from AT only when the surrounding named control or text already conveys its meaning; update the real control state independently of the animation.
conflicts: 'Any icon can morph into any other' only applies to the deliberately simplified three-line vocabulary, not arbitrary library icons.
The three-line rule, spring rotation, 14×14 viewBox and 400ms easing are optional implementation choices rather than universal icon rules.
Motion/React snippets do not justify a whole React application; use native SVG/JS where sufficient or a justified interactive island.
Do not apply aria-hidden to a meaningful unlabeled standalone image or use motion as the only state signal.
entries.reason: A distinctive and concrete micro-interaction pattern for selected menu/close, plus/minus and arrow transitions.

source.description: Build icon components that morph between SVG shapes with smooth, line-based transformation.

entries.destination: Native CSS craft; progressive View Transitions
principles: Use before/after with content:'' for decorative layers rather than additional semantic DOM; define the containing block and stacking context deliberately so decoration cannot cover labels or capture unintended input.
Expand small hit areas with a pseudo-element only when the enlarged region does not overlap neighboring controls or get clipped; verify the actual pointer target and keyboard focus treatment.
Prefer native dialog/popover backdrop and native placeholder/selection styling when they satisfy the interaction; placeholder styling never replaces a label.

For shared-element View Transitions, assign unique names to actual participating elements, transfer names deliberately between source and target and clear temporary names after completion/cancellation.
Style transition pseudo-elements to match project motion tokens when custom behavior is needed; retain normal navigation/state updates with unsupported APIs or reduced motion.
conflicts: A parent need not always be position:relative; another intentional containing block can be correct. An explicit z-index is not mandatory for every pseudo-element.
View Transitions can use the default root crossfade without individually named targets. Default crossfade and existing JS shared-element libraries are not automatically failures.
The shown name-cleanup example clears the source before the transition but does not perform final target cleanup. Add lifecycle/error handling when using temporary names.
Native ::backdrop does not replicate every custom overlay click-dismiss contract; verify behavior and support rather than replacing on appearance alone.
entries.reason: Useful native CSS techniques after replacing rule-style absolutes with containing-block, lifecycle and capability checks.

source.description: Audit CSS pseudo-elements and View Transitions usage for hover effects, decorative layers, and transitions.

entries.destination: Optionales Audiofeedback in funktionalen UI-Modulen; Accessibility-/Zustands-QA
principles: Audiofeedback ausschliesslich als Zusatz zu verständlicher visueller und gegebenenfalls programmatisch angekündigter Rückmeldung verwenden. Der entscheidende Zustand muss ohne Ton erkennbar bleiben.
Ton eher für seltene wichtige Bestätigungen oder Hinweise erwägen; kein Geräusch bei Tippen, Hover, Scrollen oder routinemässiger Tastaturnavigation.
Eine explizite Soundpräferenz und bei echtem Audioeinsatz unabhängige Lautstärkeregelung vorsehen. Zurückhaltende Lautheit und freundliche Fehlertöne statt strafender Alarme wählen.
Soundgewicht und Dauer an Bedeutung und Dauer der Handlung anpassen; eine kurze Interaktion nicht mit langer Fanfare überlagern.

Benötigte Audiodaten im autorisierten Feature vorladen, wiederverwendete Audioreferenzen verwalten und Wiederholung bewusst steuern. Browser-Autoplay-/play-Promise-Fehler behandeln; Ton darf eine Handlung nicht blockieren.

Erfolgsgeräusche erst nach tatsächlich bestätigtem Abschluss auslösen, zusammen mit einem wahrheitsgemässen sichtbaren Zustand. Das async-Payment-Beispiel illustriert die richtige Reihenfolge besser als mehrere andere Quellbeispiele.
conflicts: prefers-reduced-motion ist keine standardisierte Audio- oder Lautstärkepräferenz. Es kann zusätzlich vorsichtig berücksichtigt werden, ersetzt aber keinen expliziten Soundschalter und darf nicht als WCAG-Soundanforderung behauptet werden.
Die Matrix 'Formular/Fehler/Payment = Yes' ist keine Pflicht zur Vertonung einer Service-Website. Standardmässig keine neue Audiopipeline ohne Nutzen.
Mehrere als Pass markierte Beispiele spielen success vor onClick/completePurchase und zeigen Erfolg ohne bestätigte Wirkung; sie widersprechen wahrheitsgemässer Formular-/Transaktionsrückmeldung.
Globale new Audio()-Initialisierung ist nicht SSR-sicher; fixes volume=0.3 ist kein Lautheitsnachweis. API-Beispiele sind ergänzungsbedürftig.
entries.reason: Schmale optionale Ergänzung für echte Audiofeedback-Aufgaben. Die visuelle Gleichwertigkeit und Ereignisdisziplin übernehmen, kein dekoratives Website-Sounddesign einführen.

entries.destination: Web motion decision matrix within references/creator-methods.md
principles: Choose the timing model from causality: gestures and momentum favor springs; a predictable system state response can use a timed curve; true progress may need linear mapping; frequent input should remain immediate.
Carry release velocity into a gesture settlement and test repeated interruption. Balance damping/stiffness against scale, distance and product character rather than adding bounce automatically.
Use quick visible entrance response and restrained press/hover timings; if a motion feels slow, inspect total duration as well as the curve rather than hiding a long wait with an extreme easing.
For mode/view transitions, keep direction and pacing consistent with navigation meaning; avoid movement that delays keyboard focus or per-keystroke input.
Write actionable review findings with the actual declaration location, timing choice, observable user consequence and a concrete alternative.
Document timing values as per-component/phase tokens and verify that perceived completion and interaction readiness match the intended behavior.
conflicts: This source requires ease-in exits while Emil/Scandinavian sources ban them. Resolve by desired response and phase behavior; do not make either author’s preference a universal rule.
All interruptible motion does not require springs: ordinary CSS transitions can retarget. Use springs when velocity/physical continuity matters, not to justify a React dependency.
Fixed 120–180/180–260ms ranges, a 300ms ceiling, exact spring presets and a universal context-menu entrance ban are heuristics, not compliance rules.
Linear animation cannot assert real progress unless mapped to actual work; neither loading time nor progress is necessarily linear.
Linked Apple/Freya/Motion references are unread ancillary background; no video or library-version verification is claimed.
entries.reason: Main SKILL is self-contained. The causal timing framework is useful after resolving its absolute prescriptions against other motion evidence.

source.description: Audit animation timing choices to decide when springs versus easing curves produce better motion.

entries.destination: Web DESIGN.md/art-direction previews and screenshot QA; separate presentation adapter
principles: Use real brief content and assets in visual direction previews so comparison tests hierarchy, crop, density and brand fit. Keep template names, option labels and internal requirements outside the rendered design.

Record a chosen direction as reusable typography, palette, spacing rhythm, grid logic and component grammar; expand that same system across additional layouts instead of switching styles mid-delivery.
Inventory and inspect supplied imagery before defining the content structure; preserve original assets when preparing cropped or resized derivatives.
Distinguish speaker-led density from reading-first density when producing a deck; split overcrowded slides instead of shrinking text until unreadable.
Verify rendered overlap as well as overflow: scrollHeight alone misses visually overlapping grid panels. Capture meaningful desktop and phone views after content changes.
For an actual fixed-stage deck, scale the stage uniformly, keep controls outside it, isolate inactive-slide visibility/pointer handling, and expose a static print representation.
Use calc(-1 * clamp(...)) or equivalent valid CSS when negating a CSS math function; a leading minus before the function name is invalid.
Verify all relative media and CSS background assets on the final served/exported artifact; a successful HTML upload is not proof that assets travelled.
conflicts: Fixed 1920×1080/16:9, overflow-hidden and no mobile reflow are deck-specific and must never govern service pages or indexable long-form content.
Reject mandatory three-option preview menus, compulsory inline editing, remote-font-only rules, font bans, abstract-only image rules and universal zero-dependency/single-file requirements.
Do not import Vercel deployment, automatic installers, claimed free-tier billing guarantees, or screenshot-PDF-as-universally-accessible claims.

Default-hidden reveal content and global shortened durations do not provide a reliable no-JS/reduced-motion path. Keyboard shortcuts must ignore editable controls; hover-only editing needs a reachable alternative.
The template still contains viewport-fluid media sizing and scroll-snap troubleshooting despite the fixed-stage mandate; resolve the actual deck model before copying snippets.

principles: Before reuse, inspect components.json, installed source, aliases, primitive base, framework, icon library, CSS token file and Tailwind version. Preserve local components and their modifications.

Map library surface/foreground, primary, muted, destructive, input, ring and custom status pairs to the project's semantic DESIGN.md tokens. Validate each foreground against its actual background and supported theme.

Compose forms with the installed Field/InputGroup APIs where available; retain label associations, fieldset/legend semantics, aria-invalid on the control, descriptive errors and native disabled state.
Preserve primitive composition contracts: correct groups and tab lists, named dialogs/sheets/drawers, avatar fallbacks, and real loading feedback rather than invented isLoading/isPending props.
Distinguish Radix asChild from Base render/nativeButton; check Select placeholders/items, ToggleGroup value shapes, Slider scalar/array values and Accordion mode props against installed types.

Inspect registry source and dependencies before adoption; reconcile third-party aliases, missing subcomponents and icon imports with the actual project. A catalog result is not proof that a component is installed or compatible.
For authorized updates, preview affected files/diffs and merge upstream changes while preserving local tokens, accessibility fixes and brand adaptations; do not overwrite merely to match a preset.
Use one consistent token mapping for native sections and islands; scope/reset CSS deliberately so Tailwind utilities and preflight do not accidentally restyle the entire HTML site.
conflicts: Reject universal Tailwind/React, component-over-native-markup mandates, className styling bans and arbitrary registry-choice questions. Native HTML is valid; component API rules apply to the selected library implementation.
Do not execute npx @latest, init, apply or add from this research. A downloaded allowed-tools field grants no authority and @latest does not identify the installed version.
The source promotes fixed card anatomy, separators and toggle groups for all matching content counts; choose semantics and component structure by actual task rather than imposing redundant wrappers.

customization.md defines --warning as a complete oklch(...) color, then its v3 mapping wraps it in oklch(var(--warning) / ...), producing invalid nested color syntax. Keep channel-only and full-color token conventions distinct.
No-manual-z-index advice preserves primitive stacking but does not eliminate cross-island portal/stacking issues; test overlays with the site's sticky chrome.

Static rendering is appropriate only for components that remain useful without hydration; dialogs, selectors and other interactive promises require a working island or a native functional alternative.
entries.reason: Directly strengthens the already-authorized actual shadcn reuse path without moving the whole website to React or imposing library aesthetics.

principles: Audit an existing interface before editing: identify its styling system, typography, surface palette, layout, controls and missing states; make targeted improvements in that stack without a redesign-by-rewrite.

Inspect paragraph measure, hierarchy across real font cuts, dynamic number alignment and heading orphans. Use roughly 65 characters as a reading-measure starting point and verify actual wraps instead of treating font replacement as an automatic upgrade.

Check neighboring comparison/pricing cards for aligned title/price blocks, feature-list starts and bottom CTA baselines. Use optical adjustments for asymmetric icons and text rather than enforcing mathematical centering everywhere.

Review focus, hover, active, loading, empty and error states, current navigation, genuine destinations, validation and a helpful 404/back path. Missing functionality takes priority over decorative polish.

Use grid and constrained fluid containers to avoid fragile percentage math and stretched text; choose mobile viewport units deliberately. Keep nested radii and layering consistent with the design rather than adding texture or overlap by default.
Preserve meaningful semantic regions, functional skip links, image alternatives based on purpose, coherent z-index layers, verified imports, metadata and a branded favicon.
Use the source's catalogue of alternative layouts/surfaces as candidate ideas tied to a specific observed defect and brand reference, then compare full-page and affected-state screenshots.
conflicts: Explicitly reject invented realistic names, metrics, phone numbers, companies and randomized blog dates. Never disguise placeholders as real customer proof.
Reject universal bans on Inter, black, multiple accents, saturated colors, centered layouts, equal cards, dark sections, Lucide, FAQs or specific button patterns; brand intent and user tasks decide.
Reject mandatory noise/photos/gradients, automatic whitespace doubling, font swaps as universally low risk, scroll inertia, smooth scrolling or springs on every interaction.
Do not force all interactions to 200–300ms; honor reduced motion, interruption and frequent-action restraint.
Legal links and consent UI must come from actual business/jurisdiction and tracking requirements. This aesthetic audit cannot certify compliance.
Keep empty alt on decorative imagery; client validation is not a substitute for server-side checks.

Define semantic elevation/layer roles for navigation, dialogs and tooltips, and limit will-change to elements about to animate.

Treat the editorial split, asymmetric grid and layered compositions as a reference menu whose job and mobile fallback must be documented, not as a random generator.

It mandates blur animation while banning properties other than transform/opacity, and uses arbitrary z-index 50 while banning arbitrary z-index. Keep only coherent measured guidance.

Scroll listeners do not inherently cause reflow, and dvh itself changes with mobile browser chrome; choose native scroll/observers and viewport units for the intended behavior rather than repeating absolute performance claims.

conflicts: Reject React/Next.js, Tailwind v4, Motion and fixed icon-family requirements as global defaults. HTML/custom CSS/vanilla remain canonical; real shadcn components may render statically or hydrate in bounded Astro React islands; a whole React app needs application complexity.

Treat transform/opacity preference as performance guidance, not a ban on necessary height or color transitions. A passive/throttled scroll handler is not intrinsically invalid; do not force a library. Different motion libraries may coexist with distinct property ownership.

100dvh follows the dynamic viewport and is not a universal no-jump guarantee; choose content sizing, svh or dvh for the actual mobile behaviour. Inspect reduced-motion content visibility, rather than only changing a dial.

Reject mandatory installs, exact one-question rituals, character bans and the all-checkbox preflight as imported workflow authority. Do not replace the current owner, specialist tool instructions or authorized scope.

principles: Describe adaptation by task context, input method, content priority, screen constraints and connection conditions before changing layout. Reflow the experience without removing essential mobile functionality or changing its information architecture.
Choose breakpoints where real content stops working, use Grid/Flexbox and container queries for local reflow, and use clamp for fluid values with meaningful minimum/maximum sizes.
Detect pointer/hover capabilities instead of inferring input from width; retain keyboard access and touch alternatives on hybrid devices. Keep controls and focus feedback usable when hover is absent.
Account for safe-area insets and viewport-fit when using edge-to-edge layouts or bottom controls; inspect with browser chrome, software keyboard and landscape orientation.
Use srcset with true intrinsic-width descriptors and sizes matching actual CSS layout. Use picture for intentional mobile/desktop crop changes. Hiding an image with CSS does not prevent its download.

Retain core content in initial HTML and use progressive disclosure where it improves comprehension; prefer native details/summary for suitable disclosures and preserve labels/relationships when adapting tables.

Test representative narrow, intermediate and wide widths, touch/keyboard, landscape and slow networks; distinguish emulation from actual-device observations and record unavailable device coverage honestly.
For explicitly requested print adaptation, expand hidden useful content, make chart meaning survive monochrome and place page breaks logically. Email/native adaptations remain separate scopes.

The claim that desktop-first media queries inherently download extra CSS is inaccurate; ordinary media queries do not partition stylesheet downloads.

entries.destination: Web DESIGN.md motion contract and existing Scrollcraft adapter
principles: Distinguish persuade/experience surfaces from operate/read surfaces: expressive motion may carry a selected brand moment, while routine tasks need prompt feedback.
Specify a motion thesis with focal moment, continuity, control feedback and the cost/frequency of expensive effects.
Select material by meaning: transforms/shared elements for continuity, bounded masks or blur for reveal/depth, and minimal state changes for feedback.
Use CSS for declarative states, WAAPI or an existing library for interruption/sequencing, and scroll-linked media only when the scroll relationship explains something.
Use duration ranges as starting points: roughly 100–150ms feedback, 150–300ms state changes, 300–500ms layout/view transitions, and longer entrances only for a deliberate focal moment.
Cap total list stagger delay; do not reinterpret every section as a reveal sequence.
Keep baseline content visible, pause nonessential offscreen/hidden loops and provide an intentional reduced-motion alternative that preserves information and feedback.
Test interruption, repeated use, keyboard access and measured smoothness on target viewports; transform/opacity alone do not prove acceptable performance.

entries.destination: UI-Copy-Referenz, PRODUCT.md-Terminologie und Formular-/Statusvertrag in DESIGN.md; Abstimmung mit copywriting
principles: UI-Texte im vollständigen Handlungspfad prüfen: Vorwissen, emotionale Lage, Konsequenzen, mögliche Wiederherstellung und reale nächste Handlung bestimmen den Text.
Jeden Zustand auf eine jetzt benötigte Tatsache, eine nächste Aktion und entscheidungsrelevanten Kontext reduzieren. Einleitung oder Helper entfernen, wenn sie nur die Überschrift wiederholen.

Actions mit passendem Verb und Objekt benennen; dieselbe Sache im gesamten Produkt gleich nennen. Bei schädigenden Aktionen Gegenstand und Konsequenz ausdrücken, bei sicherer Wiederherstellung Undo erwägen.
Formate und Voraussetzungen vor Absenden erklären; Labels bleiben sichtbar, Placeholder liefern Beispiele. Fehler nennen das Problem und die konkrete Korrektur ohne Schuldzuweisung.

Fehler-, Berechtigungs-, Leer- und Erfolgszustände unterscheiden: keine Ergebnisse durch Filter ist etwas anderes als Erstnutzung, fehlender Zugriff oder Serverfehler. Keine Ursache, Bearbeitungszeit oder Fortschrittszahl erfinden.
Zugängliche Namen mit sichtbaren Labels abstimmen, Fehlermeldungen bei den Feldern verknüpfen und Statusänderungen passend ankündigen; Linktext soll auch ohne Nachbarsatz verständlich sein.
Übersetzbare vollständige Nachrichten statt Satzfragment-Verkettung schreiben. Variablen, Zahlen und Pluralformen so strukturieren, dass Reihenfolge und Expansion möglich bleiben.
Copy bei Zielbreiten, 200 Prozent Zoom, langen Namen und lokalisierten Werten prüfen. Ein kurzes Glossar stabilisiert Produktbegriffe; knappe Texte dürfen Bedeutung oder Recovery nicht verlieren.

Nicht marketingtypisch variieren, wenn ein fester UI-Begriff Wiedererkennung sichern soll. Brand-Voice ergänzt die Klarheitsregeln, darf reale Zustände aber nicht beschönigen.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md: Farbe als Rolle und Art Direction; Farb-/Kontrast-QA
principles: Vor Farbänderungen DESIGN.md, reale Brandassets, Tokens, Themes und repräsentative Zustände lesen; bestätigte Markenfarbe und semantische Konventionen von einer offenen Identitätsentscheidung unterscheiden.

Besuchermodus berücksichtigen: auf Erlebnis-/Überzeugungsseiten darf Farbe grössere atmosphärische Regionen prägen; in Arbeits-/Leseflächen trägt sie vor allem Aktion, Auswahl, Status und Orientierung.

Farbstrategie mit emotionaler Temperatur, dominanter Beziehung, Kontrastumfang und Dosierung beschreiben. Keine starre Prozentregel; jede Farbe erhält eine stabile funktionale oder zur Bildwelt passende Rolle.

Canvas, erhöhte Flächen, primäre/sekundäre Texte, Aktionen, Fokus, Auswahl, Grenzen und Status als semantische Rollen definieren. Die stärkste Aktionsfarbe nicht gleichzeitig beliebig auf Dekoration verteilen.

Bei neuen Paletten OKLCH für kontrollierbare Helligkeits-/Chromaabstufungen erwägen. An sehr hellen/dunklen Enden Chroma reduzieren und reale darstellbare Farben prüfen; bestehende Farbtechnik nicht unnötig migrieren.
Sekundärtexte auf Farbflächen aus dem konkreten Vordergrund-/Flächenpaar ableiten und Alpha-Layer nicht unkontrolliert stapeln. Dark Mode mit eigener Flächentiefe und Kontraststrategie gestalten.

Kontrast an tatsächlich berechneten Vorder-/Hintergrundpaaren in Fokus, Hover, Fehler, Auswahl, Overlay und Bildtext prüfen. Bedeutung zusätzlich durch Label, Icon, Form, Position oder Muster vermitteln.
Die Palette über dichte, ruhige, leere und fehlerhafte Zustände hinweg beurteilen. Änderungen an semantischen Rollen sollen sich konsistent über Seitenfamilien fortsetzen.

Eine fehlende Kontrastanforderung ist keine Empfehlung für unleserliche Disabledzustände. Produktqualität und normativer Mindestnachweis getrennt dokumentieren.

Automatischer Handoff an impeccable polish und live-mode color-amount-Parameter setzen ein bestimmtes Tool-/Variantensystem voraus. Nicht als Pflichtgate oder ungeprüfte CSS-Variable in Web übernehmen.

principles: Judge product specificity before consulting detector output: identify which composition, vocabulary and interaction decisions depend on this business rather than an interchangeable category template.
Combine qualitative inspection with deterministic/browser evidence without concatenating reports; identify agreement, newly discovered issues and false positives separately.
Review actual primary journeys through first-time, interrupted-mobile, accessibility and edge-case perspectives; derive additional audience assumptions only from verified product context.
Separate task complexity from avoidable interface effort: co-locate information needed for a decision, preserve earlier-step context, label unfamiliar actions and expose progressive-disclosure cues.
Report each defect with exact element/location, user consequence, concrete fix and severity based on task obstruction; retain specific strengths so repairs do not erase successful design decisions.
If using Nielsen scores, mark inapplicable heuristics n/a, recompute the denominator and never compare totals across different applicable sets as an improvement trend without qualification.
Attach review evidence to a stable source target and assessed revision/fingerprint; retain a local ignore rationale and distinguish stale findings from the current implementation.
Inspect error recovery, long strings, empty states, refresh/back navigation, keyboard flow, focus, zoom and mobile interruptions alongside visual hierarchy and emotional reassurance.
conflicts: Reject mandatory two-agent orchestration, Codex permission claims, degraded banners, detector execution gates and compulsory post-report questions. The host and current scope govern agents and tools; this research explicitly forbids children. Under the current user override, Unlazy may be selected automatically when useful and absent time/token/agent budgets are not prerequisites.
The <=4 choices/chunks rule and <=5 navigation items overgeneralize working-memory research into visible-choice limits; use observed search/decision difficulty rather than a universal numeric cap.
Scores, rating bands, persona abandonment predictions and the 'support contact implies P1' shortcut are heuristics, not user-study results or release certification.
4.5:1 text and 44x44pt touch guidance are not a complete accessibility standard; distinguish normal/large text, CSS pixels, target exceptions and actual assistive-technology evidence.
Overlay injection, live-server cleanup and snapshot helpers are only meaningful when actually supported and used; do not invent successful overlays or import tool-specific bookkeeping as a Web gate.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — proportionate personality and humane state feedback
principles: Locate a meaningful emotional moment: earned completion, informative waiting, first-use orientation, recovery or mastery. State what the user should feel and why it belongs to the product.
Choose the smallest interaction/copy/asset treatment that carries that feeling; ordinary saves should feel certain, while consequential milestones may support stronger acknowledgment.
Use waiting to communicate actual progress or context without inventing work or delaying completion. Give empty states their useful next action before adding illustration or personality.
Lead error recovery with cause and remedy. Avoid jokes around lost work, money, privacy and blocked access; voice stays consistent while tone follows consequence.
Keep discovery rewards optional and useful, allow repeat use without fatigue, stop hidden loops and verify muted, keyboard, touch and localized paths.
conflicts: Do not require uniqueness so strict that every conventional success state is rejected; reliability itself can be the appropriate personality.
No unsolicited sound/haptics, mandatory celebration or disproportionate dependency follows from a delight request. Existing motion and image specialists retain tool instructions.
The closing polish handoff is advice, not a second controller or repeated review of an unchanged state.

entries.destination: Web UI craft / DESIGN.md component and hierarchy review
principles: Diagnose the actual complexity source: competing actions, repeated information, purposeless visual variations, confusing hierarchy, unnecessary containers or extra interaction steps.
Identify the primary task at the relevant component/section scope and distinguish required information from secondary controls before cutting or hiding anything.
Use spacing and alignment where cards, borders and shadows add no grouping or interaction meaning; consolidate duplicate styles and genuinely redundant variants.
Offer secondary complexity through a clear accessible entry point when useful; inline editing or sensible defaults can reduce an unnecessary modal or step.
Retain labels, necessary choices, domain complexity and decision-relevant information. Document removed complexity, reason and replacement access where one is needed.
Verify completion paths, discoverability and visual hierarchy after simplification; claims of faster completion or less cognitive load require corresponding user evidence.
conflicts: Reject mechanically halving every sentence twice, deleting legalese/hedging without meaning review, maximum fonts/sizes/colors, never-nested-cards and universal full-width/one-goal rules.
Do not reduce the agreed SEO route/content scope or remove a useful sidebar merely to simplify appearance. The source's preserve-functionality rule outranks its aggressive cuts.
Unexpanded template commands and mandatory polish handoffs do not create installed tools or a second workflow.

entries.destination: Web component resilience, form behavior and responsive QA
principles: Exercise long/short/empty content, long translations, emoji and relevant RTL/CJK text in real components instead of validating only ideal English examples.
Use min-width:0 for shrinking flex/grid children, content-driven sizing, logical CSS properties and deliberate wrapping/hyphenation. Essential text must remain available when truncation is used.
Use Intl for dates, numbers and currencies and locale-aware pluralization; test actual supported languages rather than assuming German is always longest.
Preserve form input through validation, network and permission errors; display field-specific corrections and real retry paths.
Distinguish initial load, refresh, empty result, no permission, offline, timeout and server/rate-limit states; a local component error should not unnecessarily block the whole interface.
Prevent duplicate submissions and stale-result races; implement rollback for any optimistic action and cancel obsolete requests/listeners/timers.
Keep client validation helpful but validate at the server boundary; do not rely on the browser as the sole data-integrity or security check.
Use real slow/offline and repeated-action tests for relevant flows, including text resize and forced-colors behavior.
conflicts: Do not add offline service workers, virtualization, global i18n scope or a complete test pyramid to every static service site merely because listed.
Do not blindly truncate SEO or essential explanatory copy, mask layout errors with overflow:hidden, or use ASCII-only input restrictions for names.
The 30–40% translation allowance and 16px input/body guidance are useful design heuristics, not universal WCAG rules; emoji length is not reliably modeled by a byte count.
React examples do not imply a React migration or automatic handoff to another full polishing workflow.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — craft and critique; references/design-contract.md — system/surface separation; references/screenshots.md — evidence; existing GPT Image/Scrollcraft adapters preserved
principles: Choose the visitor mode per surface: Persuade for a decision/action, Operate for task completion, Read for comprehension, Experience for the work itself. A product can need different modes on different routes.

Resolve visual authority from approved assets, coherent code and rendered evidence, not the presence of DESIGN.md alone. A local refinement inherits the surrounding identity; a true redesign may replace visual language while preserving product facts and functions.

Keep durable global tokens/components distinct from page-specific audience, purpose, proof, first viewport and interaction intent. Seed DESIGN.md with resolved intent, then reconcile executable tokens and rendered evidence; do not promote a one-page metaphor into a global prohibition.

Use an explicit component/region job when translating a reference: identify what is real text/control, exact vector geometry, independent raster artwork or media. Preserve indexable text and functional controls; retain provenance and reference roles for generated or sourced assets.

Judge the page with the real content and its expected usage. Inspect grouping, reading order, density, hierarchy, typography and domain fit independently of deterministic detector output; a clean detector cannot prove excellent design.

Classify drift before changing it: missing token, duplicate implementation, conceptual mismatch or local defect. Repair at the narrowest correct level and retest the whole affected path, not just a visually impressive component.

Triage blocked tasks/data loss/misleading state before missing states, structural drift, cosmetic details and cleanup. Explicitly cover long/empty/missing/localized content, timeout/offline/permission failures, racing responses and repeat submissions where applicable.

When evaluating screenshots, establish capture validity first: correct route/revision/viewport/state, settled fonts/images/motion, no blank or wrong region. Compare full-page context plus named region pairs; distinguish missing material, structural contradiction and small metric drift.

Record what a review actually assessed. A fix-list retest supports resolution of that list, not renewed whole-site approval. If new user evidence contradicts a verdict, reassess the affected evidence and scope.

Use craft levers in concert: semantic color roles, measured foreground/background pairs, close grouping with stronger inter-group space, face-specific line-height/measure, container-aware layout, and deliberate depth that preserves control boundaries.

Motion can explain feedback, continuity or one earned focal moment. Keep default content visible, use interruptible state changes, cap accumulated stagger by usability and measure bounded filter/mask/shadow effects on target devices.

Delight belongs at meaningful success, useful waiting, first-use orientation or recovery; do not stage fake progress, block completion, trivialize high-stakes errors or hide required functionality behind discovery.

Preserve the complete enquiry or task journey on small screens; choose breakpoints from content and input capabilities. Test actual target widths, zoom, safe areas, orientation, keyboard and touch; emulation does not prove real-device media behavior.

If using Impeccable-specific DESIGN.md tooling, verify its installed parser and linked format version. Preserve the incumbent canonical color representation and token names; sidecars may carry extensions without creating a second conflicting token authority.

For reference comps, lead prompts with region structure and real subject content, state precisely what a reference contributes, and separate borrowed material character from unrelated content. A comp is not shipped HTML and its spelling, claims and behavior still need validation.
conflicts: Reject fixed QA/repair ceilings, mandatory random concept-seed selection, numerical candidate/comp counts, compulsory decision servers, repeated approval interviews, scripts as universal build gates and fixed agent rosters. Current authorization and available native tools govern; tool errors or silence do not imply user approval.

Reject blanket font blacklists, eyebrow bans, one-accent percentages, universal card radii, exact tracking/display limits, always-one-depth rules, prohibited nested cards and forced browser-chrome styling. Assess brand fit and user function, not detector taste.

New-work bans many SVG illustrations and requires raster plates before page code; craft-floor and visualize partly disagree about diagrams. Preserve Web’s element-by-element HTML/CSS/SVG/raster choice and existing GPT Image module. Do not force paid provider/image switches or flatten useful vector geometry.

The linked DESIGN.md spec is alpha, permits aliases such as Layout & Spacing, preserves unknown sections and accepts unknown component properties with a warning. Impeccable document.md states stricter eight-property/heading prohibitions; treat those as possible consumer constraints, not universal format law.

The source documents tokens both after building and in seed mode and suggests synthetic sidecar primitives despite later forbidding nonexistent components. Preserve approved intent plus explicit provisional values, and distinguish real components from specimens rather than silently recording accidental drift as law.

Accessibility audit scores are heuristic, not WCAG certification. Do not conflate 44px with AA, mandate dark mode where absent, label every missing ARIA attribute a defect, or treat one h1/no-level-skip as automatic conformance failure.

Critique’s four-item working-memory limit is not a universal menu cap; its named personas and abandonment predictions are hypotheses, not observed user research or conversion evidence. Avoid arbitrary health scores as shipping authorization.

Optimize examples incorrectly lazy-load a hero and subset fonts to Basic Latin; do not delay the actual LCP asset or omit German umlauts/required glyphs. Mobile-first CSS does not inherently download less CSS than desktop-first.
Distill’s cut-every-sentence-in-half, remove-sidebars, reduce-options and font-count rules must not remove required content, SEO page value, factual qualifications or functioning features.

No universal tool/controller replacement: installed specialists retain actual tool instructions; Web and Compound retain ownership. The latest user override allows useful automatic Unlazy selection without time/token/agent prerequisites; do not reintroduce earlier budget gates. Do not automatically duplicate Compound project lessons into Second Brain.

Twenty selected supporting documents, including the linked alpha format spec and visualization reference, were read completely. Integrate the design/evidence tactics while rejecting upstream workflow and aesthetic authority.

entries.destination: Layout diagnosis, responsive contracts and screenshot review in UI playbook/DESIGN.md
principles: Distinguish persuasion/experience from operation/reading: disruption and asymmetry can serve an expressive page, while predictable structure is an affordance for repeated tasks.
Before moving boxes, state the primary reading path, grouping relationships, leading/supporting elements, intended density and structural adaptations.
Use the squint test on rendered views to identify primary, secondary and major groups; keep this judgement separate from a mechanical spacing/overflow scan, then synthesize both.
Use proximity before containers and deliberate tight/generous intervals instead of uniform spacing. Repetition should support recognition; vary topology when priority or content changes.
Specify what reorders, wraps, collapses, scrolls or stays fixed at narrow/intermediate/wide widths, zoom, localization and long/empty content; DOM and keyboard order must remain coherent.
Prefer container-aware components and gap for sibling rhythm when suitable; optical corrections require inspecting the rendered result, not just a token value.
Test structural extremes including sticky elements, overlays, safe areas and small visible controls with sufficiently large targets; report actual evidence for each concern.
conflicts: Do not treat templated impeccable CLI placeholders as installed commands or a clean scan as proof of hierarchy. Actual detector/tool instructions stay with the installed specialist.
No mandatory subagents, follow-on polish command, density slider or parameter schema for ordinary layout work. Use useful procedures within current scope and permissions.
The suggested 4-unit scale is not a universal law; preserve the selected system. The native iOS/Android, identity-replacement and live-mode references are ancillary to this HTML-first extraction.

entries.destination: Performance and Core Web Vitals QA
principles: Identify whether initial load, interaction, animation or memory is slow and who experiences it; measure a reproducible baseline and compare after changing the actual bottleneck.
Inspect request waterfall, shipped JS/CSS/media sizes, long tasks, rendering and field/lab metrics. Separate network/server, JavaScript, layout/paint and asset bottlenecks.
Use responsive image sizes and modern formats, eager critical media, reserved image/video/embed geometry and lazy loading below the fold.
Load only required font weights/subsets with an intentional fallback and display policy; preload truly critical fonts/assets and avoid unnecessary third-party scripts.
Batch layout reads before writes; isolate independent regions, use content-visibility or virtualization only when their content/interaction model suits it, and bound expensive effects.
Keep will-change selective and temporary, avoid unnecessary layout animation, defer noncritical code and break up heavy main-thread tasks.
Use LCP 2.5s, INP 200ms and CLS 0.1 as performance reference thresholds with measurement context; verify relevant mobile hardware/network conditions and preserve functionality/accessibility.
conflicts: The hero img example uses loading=lazy despite the source's own prohibition on lazy above-fold content; do not import that example. Basic-Latin-only font ranges would omit German umlauts/ß and other required content.

No blanket memo/useCallback, inline-handler ban, GraphQL adoption, service worker, CDN/provider migration or bundler switch. Optimize React only inside real justified React code and according to profiling/compiler behavior.
Transform/opacity are favorable properties, not unconditional GPU or frame-rate guarantees. A Lighthouse score or one lab run is neither field INP nor an SEO ranking promise.

Fixed image quality and 16ms frame targets are starting assumptions; validate visual quality and actual device refresh rates. Do not force a separate polish workflow after checks already cover the same state.
entries.reason: Strong framework-independent bottleneck-first performance methods; source is a self-contained reference, not a conventional frontmatter skill.

principles: Choose technical ambition by the visitor task: a service hero may benefit from a single expressive transition, while a complex form benefits from instant reliable feedback and a large table from responsiveness.
Use a removal test: if taking the effect away does not diminish comprehension, orientation or the selected identity, reconsider its cost. Avoid several competing signature moments on one screen.

Choose the smallest browser capability that expresses the effect: CSS/starting-style, View Transitions or WAAPI before a heavyweight rendering layer; workers or virtualization when measured data work blocks input.
Feature-detect advanced APIs and ship a good static or simpler fallback. Initialize expensive contexts/WASM near visibility, pause offscreen work and test on representative midrange devices.
Keep state transitions cancellable and responsive to input. Use actual browser iteration and device evidence to tune timing rather than treating successful compilation as visual success.
Treat audio as opt-in and keep device-permission decisions explicit. Do not silently add collaboration, offline support or backend capabilities under the label UI polish.

Browser-support claims for View Transitions, @starting-style, WebGPU and scroll timelines are version-dependent; verify target browsers instead of copying universal labels.
60fps/50fps thresholds are targets to interpret with the effect and device, not evidence of measured performance. Do not add WebGL/WebGPU merely to demonstrate ambition.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — reducing visual intensity inside an approved identity
principles: Diagnose the actual intensity source—saturation, contrast competition, weight, motion, decoration or scale—before reducing everything uniformly.

Uniform spacing and grid conformity are not inherently better; keep meaningful rhythm and approved expressive composition. No compulsory follow-on polish command or new approval round.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md typography contract / UI craft and screenshot stress QA
principles: Choose type behavior by visitor task: expressive responsive display type may suit persuasion, while reading and operating surfaces need predictable role scales and stable scanning.
Before changing type, document authoritative families/weights, semantic roles, intended hierarchy, measure/density and font delivery constraints; improve use within the approved identity.
Audit hierarchy using computed family, size, weight, leading, tracking and space together rather than size alone. Keep repeated roles consistent across routes and states.

Stress long headings, localized expansion, narrow containers, missing font weights, fallback fonts, zoom and user text scaling. Load only used font assets with appropriate metric fallbacks and avoid disruptive reflow.
Use tabular numerals/code features where the data benefits; choose paragraph spacing or indentation deliberately instead of double-marking every boundary.
Keep visual judgment independent of mechanical detector output, then reconcile both with source or rendered evidence. A clean detector does not establish typography quality.
conflicts: Do not mandate an unavailable impeccable CLI, automatic subagents, a second review of an unchanged stand or a mandatory polish handoff; installed prerequisites remain in force if those tools are actually used.
The sentence 'tune line height inversely with measure' contradicts its explanation that wider lines need more leading; follow the explicit reading rationale and rendered testing.

entries.destination: UI playbook: compact CSS/vanilla motion recipes and state-based screenshot QA
principles: Select motion by UI relationship: trigger-origin growth for dropdowns, centered elevation for dialogs, region entry for panels, directional continuity for related views and same-slot crossfade for icons.
Import only needed semantic duration/easing/distance tokens and enumerate animated properties. Keep token ownership local to DESIGN.md rather than copying an entire universal root block.

Separate stable interaction targets from moving decoration: animate a notification dot independently of its trigger; stack replacement icons in one grid cell and keep a stable accessible label on the control.

Model open, closing and closed states distinctly so exit completes before concealment; cancel stale cleanup work on reopening and remove focusability/assistive-technology exposure from inactive content.
For number/text replacement, retain the real semantic value while visual spans animate; reset/restart only the relevant animation and use deterministic settled states for QA.
For a success stroke, normalize the path or measure its actual total length before selecting dash values. Keep success hidden until real completion, including under reduced motion.

Optional neighbour-lift effects can use distance falloff (lift × falloff^distance) and different return easing; apply to a stable hit region and support equivalent keyboard selection without depending on hover.
Keep validation state separate from shake replay. Error text remains until the invalid condition is resolved; a transient wiggle is only supplemental feedback.
If per-segment shake durations change, recompute cumulative percentage stops; the supplied A,A,B,B pattern uses 2A+2B total, not the conflicting A,B,A,B comment.
conflicts: Reject mandatory verbatim copying, global token dumps and permanent will-change. Width/height and blur animation need measurement; component-specific CSS may be adapted to the existing system.

Provided div dialogs/dropdowns lack complete focus, Escape, inert/background and accessible naming behaviour. opacity:0 and pointer-events:none alone do not hide descendants from keyboard or accessibility APIs.
The success-check reduced-motion rule sets opacity:1 without checking data-state, exposing the out state before success. Scope the resting visibility to actual success state.
Reject auto-clearing an unresolved error after 3 seconds or any keystroke. Native validation, aria-invalid/describedby and durable feedback must follow actual validity.

Timer examples parseFloat time tokens as milliseconds, ignoring s units, local overrides and zero values; reduced-motion CSS does not remove JS delays. Use normalized effective timings or lifecycle events with interruption-safe cleanup.

The number recipe documents arbitrary stagger indices but implements only 1 and 2. The page-slider's absolute children need container sizing and inactive-state semantics. These are sketches, not universally drop-in components.
A reduced-motion media query alone does not certify accessibility; force-reflow replay and cosmetic blur/spring values are optional techniques, not system-wide mandates.
entries.reason: All twelve recipes and the root CSS were fetched and fully read. Their portable CSS vocabulary is valuable after repairing state, accessibility and timer assumptions; no framework is necessary.

daisyUI CSS does not by itself implement every accessibility contract. Source modal examples still need accessible naming and appropriate focus/recovery verification; Popover API does not turn a menu into an ARIA composite automatically.
