entries.destination: DESIGN.md-Kompositionsvertrag und UI-Craft; kompakte Seitenfamilie nur bei passendem Seitenzweck
principles: Ein kompaktes Seitenformat über einen klaren Zweck und redigierte Information definieren, nicht über stets dieselbe schmale Breite. Die erste Ansicht sollte ihre Hauptaktion und einen echten Produktbeleg zeigen.

Einen Design-Fingerprint aus Komposition, Lesemass, Farbrollen, Schrift, Geometrie, Oberflächen, Motiv und Motion beschreiben; Komponenten aus einer kohärenten Richtung ableiten statt unabhängig zufällig gestalten.

Ein produktnahes Signature-Element wählen: echte Transformation, nutzbare Vorschau, Prozessbeispiel, Komponentenzustand oder belegtes Vorher/Nachher. Für Service-Websites kann dies ein echter Arbeitsablauf oder Fallbeleg sein.

Dynamische Zustände in einer stabilen Geometrie planen: Icon-Slots, übereinandergelegte Labelvarianten, reservierte Medienformate und angemessene Mindesthöhen. Tabularzahlen verhindern bei Ziffern Breitenwechsel.
Hover und Statuswechsel sollen nicht ungeplant Padding, Borderbreite, Fontgewicht oder Layouttracks ändern. Metric-kompatible Font-Fallbacks und echte Bildabmessungen helfen gegen Layoutsprünge.
Visuell kleine Controls durch nicht überlappende Hitflächen bedienbar halten; Focus-visible, DOM-Lesereihenfolge, reduced motion und Touch-Verhalten gemeinsam prüfen.
Zusammengehörige Radien konzentrisch denken: Aussenradius ungefähr Innenradius plus Padding; Oberflächen nur dort einfassen, wo dies eine Gruppe oder Ebene erklärt.

Kleine Effekte mit CSS oder vorhandenen Abhängigkeiten umsetzen und echte Zustandswechsel vor/während/nach der Interaktion prüfen; ein Zero-Shift-Vorsatz ist erst durch beobachtete Renderzustände belastbar.
conflicts: Kein Pflichtdialog zur Buttongrösse und kein Ausführen des zufälligen Direction-Pickers. Bestehende Brand und Nutzerauftrag beantworten Routineentscheidungen.
Vier Abweichungen von einer alten Rezeptur und Mutation zweier Details sind keine Qualitätskriterien; neue Seiten müssen nicht anders als das letzte Projekt sein.
420–720px Breite, 11–14px Buttonlabels, 40px Hitflächen und exakte Bewegungszahlen bleiben Beispiele, keine universelle Ergonomie- oder Konformitätsregel.
Beschränkte Inhaltsdichte darf vereinbarte Service-/SEO-Seiten nicht verkürzen oder auslassen. Die kompakte Seitenfamilie ist nicht die einzige Websiteform.
Filter ist nicht pauschal billig; absolutes Verbot von Layoutanimationen kann sinnvolle Inhaltsübergänge verhindern. Performance messen und gezielt entscheiden.
entries.reason: HTML-first passt zur Architektur. Besonders stark sind produktbezogene Komposition und stabile dynamische Geometrie; Style-DNA wurde vollständig gelesen und von Rezeptquoten getrennt.

entries.destination: Optional motion-asset adapter; frame/beat QA alongside existing Scrollcraft
principles: Use Lottie only for a justified portable animation asset. Decide transparent overlay versus full-frame background and one-shot/reversible/loop behaviour before authoring.

Design meaningful start/rest frames and a readable state transition: lead subject first, quieter supporting movement, anticipation/action/settle/hold where helpful. A valid JSON render does not establish good motion.

For this specific source runtime, validate in the official Skia Skottie player with the intended scene path; use explicit path/route over whatever /__context says is active and reread an existing scene before overwriting because UI slot edits write back.
Validate ip-inclusive/op-exclusive frame ranges and inspect frame 0, midpoint, op-1 plus semantic beats and loop seam; scrub actual playback for timing, clipping, layer order and readability.

For native text in that player, ship a licensed font, match fFamily to its embedded family, and keep fallback and slot text documents consistent. Paragraph text wraps by sz width; its height does not clip overflow, so test long edited strings.

Expose only useful colour/text/progress slots with matching value types and controls. Shared colour values can reuse one slot; differently styled copies of text may require coordinated separate slots.
Synchronise label, geometry, fill and state. Preserve logo lockups and SVG viewBox/fill behaviour; verify renderer-dependent masks/gradients and bake unsupported expression-like effects when needed.
For Web integration keep meaningful text/state outside the animation, provide a still/reduced-motion state, and verify the actual shipping player in addition to any authoring preview.
conflicts: Do not install the official player or switch renderers/providers merely because this research source says so. The Skottie validation contract applies only if this specific animation workflow is later selected with its real prerequisites.
No replacement of GPT Image or Scrollcraft, no Lottie wrapper for every CSS hover/toggle, and no compulsory new scene layout for unrelated site assets.
Reject universal zero-chrome/one-surface/black-white aesthetics and font bans. Follow DESIGN.md and preserve semantic/accessibility requirements.

Source timing ranges can reach 500–1250ms for functional feedback; they are asset recipes, not universal UI response targets. The source does not supply a complete Web reduced-motion/accessibility contract.
Do not assume rendering equivalence across Skottie, lottie-web and other players; runtime/version-dependent slot and keyframe claims remain to be tested on actual adoption.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md: accessible primitive contracts; references/component-islands.md: headless state-machine reuse
principles: Classify a requested component as presentational, simple interactive, form control, or composite before choosing its implementation. Prefer native HTML; compose an existing tested primitive or headless state machine before writing date, drag, selection, or virtualization logic.

Write the semantic role, accessible name, required states, keyboard map, focus entry/exit, and disabled/read-only behavior as a component contract before styling it. A nav or table does not need a replacement ARIA role merely because it is a component.

Choose the focus strategy by interaction: normal tab order for independent controls and links; one roving tab stop for a true composite; input focus plus aria-activedescendant for a combobox; two-dimensional navigation for an interactive grid.
A virtualized active descendant must refer to an existing, appropriately owned DOM element. Selection, keyboard focus and hover highlight are distinct states; do not silently conflate them.

For modal dialogs, specify initial focus, background inertness, Escape behavior, containment and restoration to the opening control or a sensible surviving successor. Prefer native dialog or a proven primitive over the sample focus trap.

A custom form control must submit the intended name/value pairs, omit disabled values, preserve input on failure, associate the visible label and error, support reset, and expose useful validation focus. Multiple selected values may use repeated names when the receiving contract expects them.

Expose documented state through data attributes and dynamic geometry through CSS custom properties such as anchor width, available height and transform origin. Keep ARIA state semantics independent from presence-based CSS data selectors.

Where reusable React islands need both controlled and uncontrolled use, define value/defaultValue/onValueChange ownership explicitly and test rapid updates, externally changed values and reset. Do not duplicate a fragile state hook in every component.

Design overlay dismissal and animated presence together: topmost-overlay ownership, trigger/outside-pointer handling, cancellation, rapid reopen, transition end filtering, reduced-motion zero-duration behavior and cleanup must all lead to the correct mounted state.

Verify compound widgets with keyboard, disabled/read-only values, empty options, first/last navigation, form submission and interrupted exit. Styling contracts include visible focus, hover capability checks and a meaningful reduced-motion state.
conflicts: The source mandates React, use client even for presentational components, CVA, cn, Tailwind-specific utility names, named exports and no forwardRef. These are Prototyper/React-version conventions, not Web-wide requirements. Static shadcn SSR and bounded interactive Astro React islands remain allowed.

Do not copy the hidden required text input with aria-hidden and tabindex=-1 as validation infrastructure: it can receive browser validation focus while hidden from assistive technology. Hidden value inputs also need disabled/reset handling absent from the example.

The pagination sample can assign tabindex=0 to both the active page and enabled previous button; ordinary page navigation should remain real crawlable links. The generic arrow handler also lacks RTL/grid-specific behavior.

The example focus trap does not establish inertness or handle all hidden, nested or zero-focusable cases. stopPropagation on multiple document listeners does not itself guarantee only the topmost overlay closes.

The animated-presence example relies on transitionend even when transitions are disabled and does not comprehensively handle cancellation/bubbled events. Its claim of an interruptible production recipe is not verified here.
Presence-only boolean data attributes are a CSS selector convention; ARIA false values must not be omitted indiscriminately. A use client directive belongs to an RSC boundary, not ordinary Astro SSR.
entries.reason: Rich, source-specific accessibility and lifecycle contracts transfer directly to HTML-first Web, while its illustrative React implementations need correction and remain specialist material. Main substance is self-contained; named wrapping/animation/token sibling skills are ancillary to the extracted contracts.

entries.destination: Web references/creator-methods.md / motion terminology for DESIGN.md
principles: Name motion by observed behavior so references can become precise briefs: stagger describes offset item starts; orchestration describes coordination; delay differs from duration and fill mode.
Distinguish a crossfade (overlapping opacity states), morph (shape transformation), shared-element transition (identity moving between contexts) and layout animation (geometry continuity).
Distinguish scroll reveal (visibility-triggered entrance), scroll-driven progress (position controls time), parallax (relative layer speeds) and route/view transitions.
Distinguish clip-path with a hard clipping boundary from a mask that can fade edges; specify which is needed instead of saying reveal vaguely.
Record transform origin and whether the animation is origin-aware; a trigger-anchored popover and a centered modal have different spatial contracts.
For physics, describe velocity handoff, damping, stiffness, mass, perceptual settling time, rubber-band resistance and interruption independently of the vague adjective bouncy.
Use tabular numerals for changing numeric displays; separate the numeric content, update motion and stable text geometry.
When a description is ambiguous, state the closest term and the visible distinction that would choose between alternatives; label approximations.
conflicts: The glossary is a naming aid, not an exclusive vocabulary or an obligation to quote definitions verbatim.
Its definition of layout thrashing conflates layout-affecting animation with repeated forced read/write cycles; not every width animation is thrashing.
Hardware acceleration and will-change are conditional browser behaviors, not guarantees. Press feedback need not always be scale-down, and linear motion is valid beyond the narrow listed cases.
entries.reason: Integrate source-specific distinctions to improve reference annotations and motion contracts; do not add a separate controller or wholesale glossary dump.

source.description: Sharpen motion language so animation choices feel deliberate and consistent.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md motion contract; motion QA in ui-playbook and Scrollcraft adapter
principles: Require an animation purpose tied to orientation, feedback, explanation or state continuity; reduce repetitive motion on frequently used controls and keep the underlying action immediately available.

Select easing by behaviour: quick responsive entrance/exit, balanced travel, simple hover colour change and linear constant motion. Store approved durations, distances and curves as tokens rather than choosing each independently.

Use the source duration bands as starting ranges to inspect: press 100–160ms, small popover 125–200ms, dropdown 150–250ms; justify larger modal/explanatory movement rather than enforcing a universal stopwatch.

Anchor popover/tooltip transforms to their trigger and use a modest initial scale such as .95 when appropriate. Test rapid reopen/reverse/gesture interruptions so transitions retarget from current state.

Prefer CSS transitions, supported @starting-style or WAAPI for predetermined UI movement; use a spring or JS only where dynamic gestures or coordination need it. Name transition properties explicitly.

Prefer transform/opacity and profile rendering cost under realistic load. Avoid driving a whole descendant tree through a frequently updated inherited custom property when only one element needs a transform.
Honour reduced motion, gate hover motion to suitable pointers, and keep staggered content operable. Delete, reduce, tune easing/origin, then add polish only if a defect remains.

Review normal playback plus slowed/frame-by-frame transitions for overshoot, origin, drift, clipped content and loop seams; check gestures on relevant devices and attach file/state/evidence to findings.
conflicts: Reject automatic blocking for any keyboard-triggered motion, pure fade, built-in easing or scale(0), and universal sub-300ms rules. The source itself allows 200–500ms modals and 400ms toasts.

Transform/opacity are compositor-friendly candidates, not a universal GPU guarantee. Motion shorthand, SVG wrappers, clip-path and blur performance depends on versions/browser/compositing; measure rather than copy absolute claims.
Reduced motion can mean zero animation when appropriate; the source gentler-not-zero mandate must not force motion on users.
No default-to-flag bias that manufactures defects, fixed output ritual, mandatory overnight pause or general workflow refusal. Review only relevant motion without a competing controller.

entries.destination: Web references/creator-methods.md + screenshots.md: intent-based motion inspection; optional existing Timeline Inspector integration
principles: Infer a transition purpose from component behavior and phase, not the nearest duration number. Distinguish targeted token adjustments from replacement of the entire animation structure.
Model each animated component as phases (open/close/hover) and members (surface/backdrop/items), with property, actual duration, delay and easing per member.

Use observed current-state timings and corresponding state rules to recover both phases. A flat DOM transition list does not establish which members form a component or how the opposite phase behaves.
For a source change, resolve the real declaration using component, selector, phase and previous values. Update the correct member/property/state and preserve existing units and token conventions.
Keep preview changes, accepted source edits and full recipe implementation separate: a replace card that changes duration/easing has not installed keyframes, extra elements or JavaScript hooks.
Return no change when the existing motion already fits. Prefer a lower-overhead fitting pattern (for example an anchored dropdown over a modal) rather than swapping merely for novelty.

Candidate refinements include faster/quieter closes, no close delay, brief hover intent delays and bounded stagger totals, calibrated to the actual interaction rather than applied as fixed universal tokens.
conflicts: Do not import persistent CLI workers, REFINE_AGENT_CMD, poll loops, relay posts or the 10-minute idle policy into Web. Those are optional tool-specific protocols requiring an actual authorized integration.
Zero-file-read and one-recipe limits conflict with substantive investigation; CSSOM rules are useful evidence but do not necessarily expose runtime-generated or JS-driven phase behavior.
The 40/80/150/250/350/400/500ms ladder and mandatory easing snapping would overwrite deliberate project tokens; blur additions are not automatically cheap.

The source alternately says recipes can require one read and no reads, and its suggestion shape omits scale/blur/distance kinds mentioned earlier. Verify a real installed panel contract before integrating.

principles: Build a pass/fail signal for the user's exact symptom using the seam that reaches it: test, HTTP request, fixture CLI, browser assertion, replay or a small harness. Record the invocation and observed failure, not merely that a command ran.

Make the feedback loop deterministic where possible by pinning inputs/time/randomness and isolating environment dependencies; for intermittent failures measure reproduction frequency and preserve the triggering conditions.
Minimize the reproducer one factor at a time while retaining the same failure. Use several falsifiable causal predictions and probes that discriminate among them rather than logs without a question.
For performance regressions, establish a measured baseline and profile the failing scenario before changing code; preserve the original scenario for the after comparison.
Turn the reproducer into a regression test only at a seam that exercises the real failure pattern; a shallow test that cannot fail on the original bug is false confidence.
Use uniquely tagged temporary instrumentation, redact secrets from artifacts and remove or clearly retain debug fixtures deliberately. Rerun the original unminimized scenario after the fix.
conflicts: Reject prohibitions on reading code or forming hypotheses until a seconds-fast red command exists; investigation often builds the reproducer and partial evidence can still advance diagnosis.
No mandatory hypothesis count, minimization perfection, HITL shell script or stop gate for ordinary defects. ce-debug remains the software workflow owner.
No automatic production instrumentation, captured credential publication, git bisect/history operations or commits from this research source; current authorization governs.
The HITL script is ancillary and was not downloaded or executed.

Current-user consolidation boundary, not an assertion about this source: Unlazy may be selected automatically when useful; absent time/token/agent budgets never block work. Capture verified project lessons through the Compound project workflow without automatically duplicating them into Second Brain.
entries.reason: Excellent evidence-loop tactics to supplement difficult UI/runtime defects, but a full hard-bug controller would duplicate the established Compound flow.

source.description: Systematic bug diagnosis through reproduce, minimize, hypothesize, instrument, and fix.

entries.destination: Führender Compound-Implementierungs-/Bugfix-Ablauf: gezielte Verhaltenstests für UI-Logik und Nutzerwege

Erwartungswerte aus Spezifikation, unabhängig durchgerechneten Beispielen oder bekannten Literalen nehmen; die Implementierungsrechnung nicht nochmals im Test ausführen.

Bei einer sinnvollen Test-first-Aufgabe einen real fehlschlagenden Verhaltensfall reproduzieren, minimal erfüllen und erst dann den nächsten Fall aufnehmen. Keine vorweg erfundene komplette Testsammlung.

Interne Zusammenarbeit möglichst real belassen; externe APIs, Zeit oder unkontrollierbare Systemgrenzen bei Bedarf über klare Adapter ersetzen. Fakes müssen den beobachtbaren Vertrag und Fehlerfälle bewahren.
Testnamen an tatsächlicher Produktsprache und vorhandenen Architekturentscheidungen ausrichten. Prüfungen sollen interne Umstrukturierungen überstehen, solange sich das Verhalten nicht ändert.

TDD ist nicht für jede reversible CSS-/Copy-Änderung erforderlich und ersetzt keine Screenshot-, Tastatur- oder Browserprüfung.
Die Quelle verbietet Refactoring innerhalb des Red/Green-Zyklus. Das darf den führenden Compound-Ablauf und sinnvolle lokale Vereinfachung nicht überschreiben.
Nie interne Mocks bzw. genau eine logische Assertion sind Heuristiken, keine universellen Verbote. Ein notwendiger systemischer Regressionstest darf mehrere zusammenhängende Beobachtungen abdecken.

Test an overloaded term against concrete scenarios: customer versus user, inquiry versus confirmed booking, estimate versus invoice, or cancelled request versus partial cancellation.
Cross-check business descriptions with implemented behavior and surface contradictions before labels and routes encode the wrong promise.
Keep the glossary about domain meaning; put implementation choices and scratch notes elsewhere. Use the existing PRODUCT.md/equivalent rather than creating duplicate knowledge.
Record an architectural/contract decision when it is costly to reverse, surprising without context and reflects a real tradeoff. A short context/decision/why paragraph can suffice.

entries.destination: Implementation architecture: bounded interaction modules, adapters and maintainable component interfaces
principles: Keep caller knowledge small relative to useful behaviour: an interface includes ordering, invariants, configuration, errors and performance, not only type signatures.

Localize animation lifecycle, listeners, state transitions and cleanup inside a cohesive interaction module, exposing a small contract to the surrounding HTML/Astro page.
Inject dependencies where behaviour really varies and return explicit outcomes where practical; test observable behaviour through the same interface consumers use.

Choose verification by dependency type: pure computation directly, local substitute for suitable infrastructure, owned remote service through a transport adapter, true third-party service through a controlled test adapter.

Keep internal test seams private when exposing them would burden callers. Compare materially different interfaces by caller effort, change locality and dependency placement when architectural uncertainty warrants it.

entries.destination: Bestehendes Motion-/Scrollcraft-Modul: GSAP-Lebenszyklus und Responsive-/Reduced-Motion-Vertrag
principles: CSS-Transitions für einfache Interaktionen beibehalten; GSAP bei koordinierter Sequenzierung, Seek/Reverse/Interrupt-Steuerung oder dynamischer Geometrie wählen und den konkreten Bedarf benennen.

to liest den aktuellen Startzustand, from verwendet den vorhandenen Zustand als Ziel und fromTo setzt beide Enden explizit. Bei mehreren from/fromTo-Tweens derselben Eigenschaft immediateRender für spätere Tweens bewusst ausschalten.
GSAP-Transform-Aliase wie x, y, xPercent, scale und rotation für kontrollierbare Zusammensetzung verwenden. Nicht gleichzeitig svgOrigin und transformOrigin einsetzen.
Tween-/Timeline-Referenzen für Pause, Reverse, Fortschrittsprüfung und gezieltes Kill speichern; zusammenhängende Abfolgen über Timeline-Positionen statt verstreute Delays steuern.

Mit gsap.matchMedia Responsive- und Reduced-Motion-Bedingungen gemeinsam behandeln; beim Wechsel automatisch revertieren und eigene Listener separat aufräumen. Nur die jeweils verantwortliche Instanz über mm.revert abbauen.

autoAlpha nur dann einsetzen, wenn vollständig ausgeblendete Elemente auch unsichtbar und nicht bedienbar sein sollen. Fokusführung, Accessibility-Zustand und sichtbaren Fallback ausdrücklich mitprüfen.
Inline-Styles nach Animation bewusst an CSS zurückgeben. clearProps an einem Transform-Alias entfernt den gesamten Transform und darf daher nicht unbemerkt fremde Transform-Anteile löschen.
Easing, Dauern und Stagger als projektbezogene Motion-Tokens beschreiben; overwrite:auto nur mit Verständnis der konkurrierenden aktiven Eigenschaften einsetzen.
conflicts: Die universelle Empfehlung GSAP für jede unbestimmte Animationsfrage widerspricht dem HTML/custom-CSS/vanilla-Default und bedarfsgerechter Bibliothekswahl.
Risk level LOW und minimale Security-Surface sind keine eigenständigen Prüfergebnisse. Keine Sicherheits- oder Performancegarantie übernehmen.

autoAlpha ist kein vollständiger Ersatz für die Accessibility- und Fokuslogik eines Dialogs. Das Beispiel mit clearProps:visibility kann den beabsichtigten versteckten Zustand wieder aufheben und muss im Kontext geprüft werden.
ScrollTrigger gehört zum verfügbaren Pluginangebot, benötigt aber bewusste Einbindung/Registrierung; es ist keine automatisch aktive Funktion jedes Core-Imports.
entries.reason: Solide frameworkunabhängige API-Grundlagen und Lifecycle-Regeln; als optionaler Motion-Adapter integrieren, nicht als neue Bibliothekspflicht.

entries.destination: Proposed topics for references/ui-skills.md / ui-playbook.md consolidation (parent owner to merge; neither reread nor edited): references/dependencies.md: GSAP lifecycle adapter; existing Scrollcraft integration notes.
principles: When GSAP is selected in a lifecycle-based component, create animations only after its root DOM exists and scope selectors with gsap.context(callback, root). Two component instances must not animate each other's matching selectors.
Create ScrollTriggers inside the owned context and revert that context on unmount/destroy so animations stop and injected inline styles are restored.
After data, fonts, images or layout changes move trigger positions, refresh ScrollTrigger after the framework has applied DOM updates; validate start/end positions again.
Register only needed plugins at an appropriate shared initialization point, lazy-load rare plugins where beneficial, and use the framework's actual mount/cleanup API.

Exercise mount, unmount, remount and route replacement in the browser to verify no duplicate animation or detached-node work; retain reduced-motion and still-fallback behavior from the existing motion module.

The Nuxt sample declares Plugins twice and uses an any cast despite claiming typed access; it is illustrative source, not a ready-to-copy implementation.
Late-created asynchronous/event-handler animations may need explicit context ownership; a context around initial setup alone is not proof of complete cleanup.
Related gsap-core/react/timeline/scrolltrigger skills and example projects were not executed or read; installed prerequisites apply when those tools are actually used.
entries.reason: The lifecycle/scoping/cleanup triad is directly useful for bounded motion integrations, but the framework-specific recipes stay conditional.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — GSAP-specific performance adapter
principles: Use GSAP x/y/scale for suitable movement rather than top/left layout changes, and batch direct DOM geometry reads before writes when mixing them with library updates.
Use quickTo for a frequently retargeted numeric property such as a pointer follower; reuse the tween instead of creating a new overlapping tween on every event.
Reuse timelines and stagger related items when that matches the intended sequence; animate only needed/visible items and measure large collections before adding virtualization.
Clean up owned tweens/triggers and listeners when a section becomes inactive or unmounts. Pause offscreen work and refresh trigger geometry only after real layout changes.
Apply targeted will-change/force3D only if measurements justify it; compare low-end device performance, layer cost and input responsiveness.
conflicts: GSAP being installed is not a reason to animate more. Library choice remains conditional and existing native/Scrollcraft solutions stay valid.
Pinning does not universally promote a GPU layer, and numeric scrub smoothing does not guarantee reduced work; it can prolong updates. Profile the actual browser and scene.
Stagger is primarily an orchestration mechanism, not proof of lower cost than all separate tweens. No transform property, hint or cleanup checklist guarantees 60fps.
entries.reason: Contains concrete quickTo/reuse guidance absent from generic CSS advice. Keep within a chosen GSAP adapter rather than adding the library to every site.

source.description: Official GSAP performance guidance for compositor-friendly transforms, quickTo, stagger batching, and smooth 60fps animation.

entries.destination: Bestehendes Scrollcraft-/Motion-Modul: bedarfsgerechte GSAP-Plugins; Bibliotheksintegration und QA
principles: Nur benötigte Plugins importieren und vor erster Nutzung registrieren; Paketversion und dokumentierten API-Stand prüfen. GSDevTools bleibt ein Entwicklungswerkzeug.

Layoutwechsel mit Flip.getState → tatsächliche DOM-/Layoutänderung → Flip.from umsetzen. In Frameworks auf den abgeschlossenen Render warten und bei ersetzten DOM-Nodes explizite targets sowie stabile data-flip-id-Werte verwenden.

Flip-Optionen nach offizieller Dokumentation korrigieren: Standardgrössenänderung nutzt width/height; scale:true ist optional. nested:true kompensiert sich aufsummierende Transformationen von Eltern und Kindern; simple:true setzt fehlende Rotation/Skalierung/Skew in Containern voraus.

absolute nur auf passende Flip-Targets anwenden, damit das Entfernen aus dem Dokumentfluss keinen Containerkollaps auslöst. Unterbrechung, Scrollen und Viewportwechsel während einer Flip-Sequenz ausdrücklich prüfen.

SplitText nur für tatsächlich animierte Einheiten verwenden. Nach Font- und Breitenänderungen autoSplit/onSplit einsetzen und die Animation aus onSplit zurückgeben, damit Cleanup und Fortschritt synchron bleiben.

Textsemantik beim Splitten erhalten: automatische aria-label/aria-hidden-Behandlung kann verschachtelte Links oder Hervorhebungen verdecken. Für solche Fälle ein geprüftes semantisches Original bzw. eine passende zugängliche Alternative erhalten und doppelte Ansagen/Fokuspunkte vermeiden.

DrawSVG benötigt einen sichtbaren Stroke und animiert dessen sichtbares Segment, nicht die Füllung. MorphSVG-Punktzuordnung bei Verdrehung gezielt mit shapeIndex untersuchen; precompile adressiert Startkosten, nicht laufendes Rendering.

Draggable mit Bounds und optionalem InertiaPlugin nur für eine echte Drag-Aufgabe verwenden; ScrollSmoother braucht seine dokumentierte Wrapper-Struktur und sinnvoll platzierte Fixed-Elemente. Native Alternativbedienung und Reduced Motion zusätzlich vorsehen.
Plugininstanzen, Textwrapper und Animationen beim Entfernen eines Bereichs gezielt zurücksetzen. Keine globalen Cleanup-Operationen über fremde Islands hinweg.

Die offizielle 3.13-Mitteilung vom 29.04.2025 bestätigt kostenlose Bonusplugins im öffentlichen Paket und das Ende alter privater Registry-/Token-Schritte. Vor tatsächlicher Wiederverwendung gelten dennoch die Paketlizenz und aktuelle Bedingungen.
conflicts: Die Quelltabelle nennt für Flip scale fälschlich true als Default und beschreibt nested/simple unzutreffend. Die vollständig gelesene offizielle Flip-Dokumentation korrigiert diese Punkte.

Die verlinkte Akquisitionsmeldung von Oktober 2024 bestätigt den kostenlosen Pluginwechsel noch nicht; sie nennt damalige Bezahlpläne. Der passende Primärbeleg ist die zusätzlich gelesene 3.13-Mitteilung von April 2025.
MIT im Skill-Frontmatter ist kein Beleg für die Lizenz der GSAP-Bibliothek. Kostenloser kommerzieller Einsatz bedeutet nicht bedingungslose Wiederverwendung oder eine pauschale Lizenzfreigabe.

Seltene Pluginoptionen und neuere MorphSVG-Funktionen sind nicht vollständig primärverifiziert. Vor Implementierung die tatsächlich installierte Version prüfen; keine Installation oder Workflow-Ausführung erfolgte hier.

Text-Kerning abschalten, text-wrap:balance vermeiden oder Smooth Scrolling installieren sind keine universellen Gestaltungsvorgaben. Nur bei einem nachgewiesenen Konflikt bzw. Motion-Bedarf einsetzen.

principles: When a React island already uses GSAP, scope targets to its ref so generic selectors cannot animate another instance.

Choose dependencies and revertOnUpdate deliberately when prop changes must recreate animation state.
Wrap later GSAP-creating callbacks with contextSafe so created animations are tracked, and separately remove native event listeners and cancel pending external work.
Run browser animation setup inside the client lifecycle; keep server rendering free of window-dependent execution and preserve visible initial HTML.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — GSAP adapter; references/scrollcraft.md — layout and seam integration
principles: When ScrollTrigger is chosen, register it once; choose scrub for continuous progress or toggleActions for discrete enter/leave behavior. Put the trigger on a top-level tween or the timeline, not independently on child tweens.
Express start/end as trigger-versus-viewport relationships and use function values when dimensions are dynamic. Refresh after actual geometry changes such as loaded fonts/images or inserted content.

Pin the stable wrapper and animate its child; retain pin spacing unless the layout explicitly provides equivalent space. Create pins/triggers in document order so downstream measurements include upstream pin offsets.

For asynchronous creation, use refresh priorities deliberately: the inspected official sort comparator refreshes higher priorities before lower priorities, contrary to the assigned SKILL.md. Retest actual pin dependencies.

For simulated horizontal travel, animate the inner wrapper by a pixel x distance derived from scrollWidth minus visible width, with ease:none and scrub. Pass that tween as containerAnimation to nested triggers; those nested triggers cannot pin or snap.

batch() groups callbacks while retaining one ScrollTrigger per target. Its callbacks receive both element and trigger arrays; use batching for repeated entrances without mistaking it for virtualization.

Use scrollerProxy only when a chosen custom scroller needs integration; synchronize its update events with ScrollTrigger.update and its geometry with refresh. Avoid adding a smooth-scrolling layer solely because an example has one.
Remove development markers and revert or kill only the instances owned by the affected section/island on teardown.
conflicts: Reject automatic GSAP selection for every scroll effect; CSS, IntersectionObserver or the existing Scrollcraft module may be sufficient.

The horizontal example contains Max.max, incorrectly uses a pixel-derived value as xPercent, computes the wrong sign/clamp for overflowing content, and omits scrub despite describing it. Do not copy it.

The source repeatedly says lower refreshPriority refreshes first; official GSAP source lines 1745-1751 implement higher-first. The official source was retrieved in full but only this relevant portion and search hits were read.

Global ScrollTrigger.getAll().forEach(kill) can destroy other islands. Cleanup must respect ownership. Scroller smoothness, snap and pinning must preserve keyboard, anchors, reduced motion and ordinary page access.

entries.destination: Existing motion/Scrollcraft adapter: sequencing and playback primitives
principles: When several animations truly need coordination, use one timeline with meaningful labels and child sequences instead of chains of unrelated delays.

Use position parameters deliberately: an absolute second, a relative offset from the timeline end, a label offset or < for the recently added animation start. > is the recently added animation end; omitting position appends at the timeline end.
Put shared duration/easing in timeline defaults and organise repeated choreography as nested timelines. Timeline duration is derived from children rather than a tween-style duration setting.
Attach scroll control at the top-level timeline/tween so nested animations do not fight separate ScrollTriggers.

Use pause/play/reverse/restart/time/progress for testing and controlled state changes, and kill/revert appropriate owned animation state on teardown. Provide reduced-motion and visible-content fallbacks through the existing Web motion contract.

The source describes > as default placement, but recently-added end and whole-timeline append are not always equivalent when animations overlap; preserve the distinction.
The minimal timeline source does not establish accessibility, keyboard operation, context cleanup or scroll performance by itself. Those checks remain required in the actual integration.

entries.destination: Existing Web motion / Scrollcraft module, GSAP utility appendix
principles: Use the helpers only when GSAP is already chosen for a real animation need. Construct reusable mapping/clamping functions once outside hot callbacks and scope selectors to the component container.

Normalize input and map progress to output ranges; explicitly clamp progress where bounds matter because normalize/mapRange extrapolate outside the input range. Keep arithmetic values numeric and guard degenerate ranges.
Compose numeric transforms with pipe; use snap for permitted steps and wrap for cyclic indices, noting that wrap's upper bound is exclusive.

Use distribute to express position/grid-based stagger with amount versus each deliberately selected; compare against the real responsive target order and avoid unexplained randomized screenshot states.
Correct unitize usage from upstream source: unitize(func, unit) returns a function that parses the input, applies func, then appends the specified or original unit; it is not unitize(number, unit).

Correct shuffle's mutation semantics: pass a copy when preserving the original order, since upstream shuffle calls Array.sort on its argument. Random's reusable form requires its return-function option.
Reuse these math helpers within existing motion ownership and cleanup, reduced-motion, static-fallback and screenshot contracts; they do not register or supply a complete animation lifecycle.
conflicts: Source incorrectly claims shuffle returns a new array and supplies invalid unitize examples; both were contradicted by downloaded upstream gsap-core.js definitions.
The 'pure helpers' description is too broad because shuffle mutates. Normalization is not clamping, and distribute amount is not a universal amount/target-count step formula.

Four docs URLs returned 404; upstream source excerpts resolved the API decisions. Installed-version compatibility remains to be checked during actual implementation; no GSAP installation or workflow execution occurred.

principles: Zusammenhängende Motion über benannte Timeline-Positionen, Überlappungen und kontrollierbare Playheads modellieren. Scrub-Sequenzen mit linearer Progression planen; numerischer scrub-Wert bedeutet Aufholverzögerung.

Falls Lenis tatsächlich erforderlich und vorhanden ist: genau einen Taktgeber nutzen, lenis.raf mit Sekunden→Millisekunden-Umrechnung antreiben und ScrollTrigger.update an Lenis-Scrollereignisse koppeln. Doppelte rAF-Schleifen vermeiden.

Lenis- und Locomotive-Integration anhand der konkreten Version und des wirklichen Scrollcontainers unterscheiden. Innere native Scrollflächen bei Bedarf ausnehmen; Ticker-Callbacks als benannte Referenzen entfernen und eigene Instanzen zerstören.

Für Reduced Motion natives Scrollen und einen vollständigen statischen Inhaltszustand anbieten; nur Lenis abzuschalten genügt nicht, wenn Pinning und räumliche Scrub-Animationen unverändert weiterlaufen.

Motion-Zustände für QA reproduzierbar machen: ein optionaler Testparameter kann den passenden Playhead auf eine validierte Zeit setzen und pausieren. Start, Übergangsmitte, Ende und Schleifennaht als tatsächlich betrachtete Screenshots erfassen.

Ein Ready-Signal erst nach geladenen Fonts, decodierten Bildern, abgeschlossener Layoutmessung und angewandtem Seek setzen. Die Quellvorlage liefert die Idee, aber noch keinen vollständigen Asset-Readiness-Nachweis.

Pinning in transformierten Vorfahren und entfernte DOM-Nodes als konkrete Fehlerursachen prüfen; Kontext-Cleanup statt globalem Kill über alle ScrollTrigger einsetzen. ScrollTrigger.batch bündelt Callback-Arbeit, seine Triggeranzahl nicht ungeprüft als reduziert darstellen.
conflicts: Die Behauptung alle Bonusplugins seien seit 3.12 kostenlos ist zeitlich falsch: die gelesene GSAP-Mitteilung verortet dies bei 3.13 am 29.04.2025.

Die Lenis-Referenz erklärt fast jedes Scrollproblem durch zwei Schleifen. Das ist zu absolut; Layoutänderungen, Vorfahrentransforms und versionsspezifische Scrollcontainer sind eigenständige Ursachen. lagSmoothing(0) verändert globales Verhalten und ist keine ungeprüfte Standardkorrektur.
Die Anker-Skizze verhindert native Navigation, ohne Hash/History, Fokus, Modifier-Keys oder fehlende Ziele vollständig zu behandeln. Semantische Links und deren Verhalten erhalten.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — motion performance and deterministic visual checks
principles: Investigate layout, paint and composition separately. Prefer transform for movement and opacity for fades when they preserve the intended layout and content; confirm the actual bottleneck with a performance trace.

For changing shadow strength, keep a static shadow on a pointer-transparent pseudo-element and animate its opacity; inspect clipping, stacking and memory rather than animating a large blur region blindly.

For reordering, measure all initial rects, mutate the real layout, measure final rects, apply the inverse transform and animate to identity. Preserve final DOM order and check nested text for scale distortion.
Batch geometry reads before style writes to avoid repeated synchronous reflow. Schedule scroll-driven transforms once per animation frame and avoid per-element measurement in a hot loop.

For content expansion, feature-detect interpolate-size where appropriate or use a 0fr-to-1fr grid with min-height:0 and overflow containment. Coordinate hidden content semantics/focus with the disclosure state.
Apply will-change only for a demonstrated preparation need and remove it when no longer useful. Inspect layer count and memory as well as dropped frames.

For animation QA, expose a deterministic time or paused WAAPI/CSS state and capture start/middle/end. Separately profile live playback; a frozen screenshot proves appearance, not frame-rate performance.
conflicts: Transform/opacity are favorable properties, not a 60/120fps guarantee or permission to animate freely. JavaScript, paint invalidation, blending, layer size and hardware still matter.

The source calls grid-track interpolation compositor-friendly and also requires zero Layout/Paint per frame. Grid/height interpolation changes layout; permit bounded measured layout animation instead of promising compositor-only expansion.

FLIP with scale does not automatically avoid stretched child text; the supplied snippet scales the entire element. Handle child scale correction or choose translation-only/alternate treatment where needed.
Reject one standalone HTML file, CDN dependencies, fixed screenshot helpers and a universal ban on other CSS properties as Web output requirements. Use the project runtime and actual browser tools.
Global tiny-duration reduced-motion hacks and animationend-dependent correctness are not a robust state model. Final state must remain correct if motion is skipped, interrupted or unsupported.
entries.reason: Concrete browser-cost, FLIP, shadow-layer and reproducible-capture tactics fit the core playbook after correcting oversimplified compositing claims. Full profiling/pattern support was read.

entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; DESIGN.md motion inventory; motion/accessibility reference; existing Scrollcraft reduced-motion adapter
principles: Inventory each effect by purpose and motion risk: remove large translations, zoom, parallax, 3D spin, scroll pinning and autoplay drift under reduced motion; preserve information and clear state feedback.

For a small nonessential displacement, consider a brief opacity transition or an immediate state change; define the reduced variant per component instead of assuming every animation has one safe duration.
Keep initial HTML/CSS visibly usable and opt elaborate motion into prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. Failure to initialize JS must not strand essential content hidden.
Apply the preference to JS, canvas/WebGL and scroll engines as well as CSS; listen for live preference changes and tear down RAF loops, controls, listeners and style mutations.

With GSAP use scoped matchMedia/context setup and reversion; with Lenis cancel RAF, destroy the instance and restore native scrolling. Use an existing shared motion controller rather than parallel loops.
Supply usable pause/stop controls for applicable continuing autoplay content independently of OS preference; preserve access to all carousel/story content when motion is stopped.
Verify normal and reduced states at equivalent moments, plus live toggling and final-state completion; emulate CSS media preferences as well as any JS debug flag.
Use deterministic seeking only as an isolated test harness; test actual time progression and interaction as well, because a frozen frame cannot prove cleanup or motion safety.
conflicts: The universal !important 0.01ms reset overrides the later non-important tiered duration declarations; the presented CSS does not implement its stated hierarchy reliably.

'Tier 3 always keep', all spinners are essential, and instantaneous changes are more disorienting are overgeneralizations. Preserve feedback, not an obligatory animation; static text/progress may be suitable.

The prose advises SSR default false while the sample initializes from client matchMedia; this can mismatch hydration and start unwanted motion. Use a stable SSR snapshot and a conservative static initial state.

0.01ms does not guarantee every end event will fire; cancelation, no property change, display changes or teardown may bypass completion. Do not make business-state completion depend only on a CSS event.
patterns.md's generic controller lacks disposal of its MediaQueryList listener; the marquee media rule may keep animation paused after the button says Play. Test actual state/UI agreement.
WCAG 2.3.3 is AAA and C39 is a technique, not whole-site certification. The >5s summary omits criterion conditions/exceptions; make no compliance claim from this skill or its screenshots.
Reject mandatory standalone HTML/CDN output and a new helper-tool workflow; adapt to the existing website and Scrollcraft modules.

entries.destination: UI craft/motion playbook: state feedback, native CSS transitions and bounded interactive islands
principles: Give immediate press feedback and keep routine response motion short; 100–250ms is a useful starting range, with quicker exits than entrances when the task benefits.
Preserve object continuity through loading, success and error states rather than swapping unrelated surfaces. The animation must represent actual application state.

Use native CSS @starting-style for initial entry and explicitly include display/overlay in discrete transition lists for dialogs/popovers; provide instant functional fallback at the actual browser support floor.
When React motion is already appropriate, stable keys and a persistent AnimatePresence owner enable exits; choose sync, wait or popLayout for real overlap needs, not by habit.
Use layout/consistent layoutId for reorder/shared-element continuity only where needed; inspect text/radius distortion and prefer position-only animation or explicit correction for children.
Avoid React state for per-frame pointer/scroll values, and avoid layout measurement on hundreds of static nodes. Use lifecycle cleanup and measured property ownership.
Capture deterministic idle, focus, pressed, open, error and settled result states; observe the transition as well as screenshots, test repeated input and reduced-motion behaviour.
For intrinsic-size accordions, test interpolate-size support or a grid-track fallback with real content and minimum-size handling; use proper disclosure semantics and functional keyboard controls.
conflicts: The short main CSS sample sets allow-discrete but omits display from the transition list; the delegated recipe supplies the needed explicit display/overlay transitions. Do not copy the incomplete sample as an exit solution.
Transform/opacity are preferred, not universally GPU-only or zero-cost; height, colour, stroke and necessary layout changes can be justified and measured.
Do not globally overwrite every animation with 0.01ms without checking delays, resting styles and functional event coupling. Scoped reduced-motion treatment must keep feedback visible.

The lightbox, reorder, toggle and like examples are animation sketches with incomplete accessibility and error handling. A clickable img or pointer drag alone is not a complete accessible interaction.
No forced React/CDN/standalone-demo build or dependency switch. A working demo is not proof of integration in the real site.

entries.destination: Motion appendix: optional native page transitions, existing application routers and transition QA
principles: Prefer progressive native View Transitions for simple cross-page continuity when supported; keep normal navigation functional without them.
For shared elements use the same logical view-transition-name across source/destination and ensure each name is unique within a captured page.

A presence-based exit needs a persistent owner, a changing keyed child and retained outgoing content; inspect lifecycle/context ownership when exit is skipped or the departing page flashes destination data.
Choose overlapping crossfade versus exit-then-enter deliberately. Serial exit can make navigation feel slow; durations around 200–400ms are a starting range to test, not a gate.
Verify source, actual intermediate transition and destination, including back/forward, rapid navigation, old-content preservation, reduced motion and layout stability.
Use deterministic state/phase controls for screenshots and a full end-to-end router check; a standalone two-view prototype can settle motion shape but cannot verify framework lifecycle integration.

entries.destination: SVG motion recipes; deterministic screenshot QA
principles: Use pathLength=1 to normalize draw-on stroke dash math without measurement; use getTotalLength in the path's own user units when actual length matters. Split compound subpaths for sequential drawing.
Morph compatible command structures directly; use MorphSVG/Flubber only when mismatched geometry or quality requires it. Verify endpoint shape, path direction and intermediate twisting.
Use transform-box and transform-origin intentionally for SVG icon rotations. For path following, align coordinate systems and decide whether orientation follows the tangent.
Choose CSS for simple declarative effects, self-contained SMIL where its support fits, WAAPI for controlled native motion and existing GSAP for coordinated/scrubbed effects.
Preserve viewBox, animated IDs/classes, hidden animated nodes and separate paths during SVGO optimization; namespace IDs for repeated inline assets and verify external references after optimization.
Provide a deterministic seek/pause harness for the selected driver and inspect start, midpoint and endpoint screenshots for clipping, stale dashoffset, flashing and morph seams.
Under reduced motion expose the final drawn state and remove decorative loops. Bound/filter-test expensive gradient, blur and displacement effects instead of assuming vector animation is cheap.
conflicts: The GSAP free-as-of-3.12 statement is not reliable version/licensing guidance; verify current installed/plugin terms when implementing. CSS d/offset-path/SMIL support is target-dependent.
A standalone HTML artifact is useful for an isolated vector probe, not a mandatory deliverable or CDN requirement for every SVG component.

Do not remove dimensions without preserving layout space, and do not run prefixIds without updating external CSS/JS references. The sample Flubber value transform recreates the interpolator per update; cache it when implementing.
Legacy-browser and ID-resolution simplifications in the supporting doc are not universal compatibility guarantees.

Reject mandatory glass-pill navigation, 700ms transition-all, hidden-on-load/800ms blurred reveals and a compulsory word-by-word tagline section. They can delay content and need real reduced-motion, keyboard and no-JS behaviour.
Reject invented realistic identities, organic fake figures and compulsory guarantees/free plans/cancel-anytime claims. Risk reversal must reflect the real offer.
Do not force 3 steps, 6–12 FAQ items, mandatory section counts or short-copy templates. Search pages must answer their intent completely.

A non-indexed path is not an indexing directive; robots blocking alone can also prevent discovery of noindex. Decide noindex per page and verify rendered/crawlable output. FAQ markup does not guarantee rich results or AI visibility.
The absolute scroll-listener ban conflicts with the source's own RAF-throttled listener alternative. Choose the simplest measured implementation without provider or framework switches.

entries.destination: Motion opportunity review within DESIGN.md / UI craft
principles: Inspect feedback gaps, abruptly appearing/disappearing content, unclear trigger-to-panel relationships, group entrances, gesture discontinuities and rare completion moments as separate motion candidates.
For each candidate record current behavior and source location, user frequency, concrete purpose, proposed properties/timing and expected effect on task completion.
Keep reading and acting on information stable; decorative tracking belongs only where it helps the brief and does not move functional data.
Rank useful opportunities by impact and reuse existing motion tokens; record meaningful rejected candidates and their reason when this explains restraint.
Carry reduced-motion and pointer gating into proposed recipes and verify uncertainty about feel in the rendered interface before treating the recommendation as settled.
conflicts: Reject mandatory 5–7 suggestions and 2–5 rejections, exact curve-only recipes, absolute keyboard/frequency prohibitions and a second forced plan/handoff after an already authorized implementation.

The source contradicts itself with a 400ms toast example against its general UI budget; treat speed ranges as reference defaults. A hold-to-confirm affordance is not automatically better or accessible for destructive actions.

entries.destination: Library decision table under stack/component-islands adapters
principles: Start from the required capability and inspect existing dependencies/versions. Keep a working incumbent library; a curated preference alone is not a migration reason.
Consider Base UI for complex headless React primitives, cmdk for command palettes, Sonner for toasts and input-otp for verification inputs only when those interactions are actually needed.
Use CSS transitions for simple hover/fade. Evaluate Motion for springs/layout/exit/gestures and NumberFlow for digit transitions only when the added behaviour justifies its runtime.
Distinguish streaming charts from static/comparison charts, and canvas/3D effects from ordinary component interaction; choose compatible actual source with a truthful data and accessibility contract.

Consider dnd-kit for a real drag interaction with alternatives, and virtualisation for measured large-list problems. Do not replace useful pagination on indexable content just because an app-oriented list library exists.

Keep state local unless genuinely shared; clsx can simplify conditional classes and cva fits a real variant API when the stack supports it. Next-specific theme tools are not general Astro requirements.

Record purpose, version, source/licence, static-renderability, hydration boundary and state/keyboard QA for adopted library components; static shadcn rendering or an interactive Astro React island are valid routes.
conflicts: Reject closed-list mandates, default competitor replacement, automatic installation and a library for every feature. No assumption that the listed sites/packages are installed or currently compatible.
Accessible library marketing does not prove the integrated component is accessible; test labels, focus, portals, states and overrides.
Libraries such as Recharts, cmdk, zustand and Next themes do not justify a whole React application. A whole app requires actual complexity and shared interaction/state needs.
Curated homepages are ancillary discovery links not independently inspected API references in this batch; verify exact docs/types when a component is selected.

entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; references/inspiration.md direction comparison; optional prototype harness
principles: When a real design uncertainty remains, compare variants that differ on named axes such as layout, density, interaction model or motion; tint changes are not distinct directions.
Keep context, realistic content and project tokens stable across variants so the comparison measures the intended design difference.
Render one variant at full usable scale with its real neighbors; verify each interaction and motion state before judging the design.
Use an isolated route/file with no production imports; integrate only the selected direction and remove experimental chrome according to the agreed artifact ownership.
Make switching immediate, expose descriptive variant names/tradeoffs and a reproducible URL selection; keyboard shortcuts must not consume input-field editing.
Document what each direction gains and costs, then update DESIGN.md with the actual decision and supporting evidence. A live picker is useful when interaction or timing materially changes the choice.
conflicts: Reject a mandatory one-component scope, fixed 3-to-5 variant quota, exact picker aesthetics and automatic user-choice stop when the existing task already authorizes autonomous design selection.
PICKER.md's 28px controls, fixed z-index, dark glass and no safe-area handling are not universal production-quality UI. The harness may cover content and needs contextual QA.
Picker code returns without rendering for an out-of-range v parameter and does not fully handle cleanup, shortcut defaults or modifiers; do not copy it verbatim as reliable infrastructure.
Prototype names/numbers must be marked as mock data and never become fabricated production testimonials, statistics or proof.
Transform-only, sub-300ms and entrance easing prescriptions are defaults, not unconditional animation correctness rules.
entries.reason: Good divergence and fair-comparison technique when uncertainty warrants it; retain the existing autonomous owner and project scope.
