entries.destination: references/screenshots.md: evidence/coverage and consolidated review; references/ui-playbook.md: domain craft
principles: Resolve the actual screen/flow/state scope, stack and project conventions before reviewing. Report inspected versus uninspected domains explicitly; a static pass cannot establish runtime focus, contrast or wrapping.

Review accessibility, layout, writing, typography, colors and UI/motion, then consolidate one ranked result. One root cause gets one finding with all confirmed locations and its owning rule; a shared-token fix can outrank a leaf fix of equal severity.

Rank task blockers, misleading actions, inaccessible paths, obscured controls, unrecoverable errors and motion-only state changes above polish. Never average away a serious defect because unrelated dimensions look good.
Prefer removing needless UI, using native behavior and reusing existing tokens before introducing a new abstraction. Make the recommendation in the project's actual styling idiom.

The accessibility owner distinguishes 24×24 CSS-pixel WCAG 2.2 AA target sizing with exceptions from a 44px touch goal, preserves forced-colors focus, allows paste, and separates native disabled from focusable-but-inert aria-disabled.

Use a stable polite status region for nonurgent repeated updates, field-associated descriptions for validation and alerts for urgent untied errors. Preserve visible names, background inertness and focus restoration in overlays.

The layout owner adds visible disclosure/scroll cues, shared alignment edges, logical properties, safe areas, content-driven breakpoints, pseudo-localization and controls protected from clipping at narrow widths and zoom.

The typography owner adds real font files/styles, semantic type roles, unitless line height, context-appropriate measure, balanced headings, reachable truncated content, tabular numbers and bidi isolation. Inspect actual loaded faces and real string lengths.

The color owner requires semantic-role usage and measurements against the actual composited background in each supported theme. A border token borrowed as text is a future failure even if its present hex happens to match.

The UI owner adds concentric radius reasoning, optical icon alignment, precise transition properties, targeted will-change, restrained high-frequency feedback and slowed animation inspection to find discontinuities.
Retest affected states after fixes and link evidence to the actual revision. A check unavailable in the environment is Not verified, not an invented failure or an implied pass.
conflicts: Reject the 15-finding cap as a work limit and the forced handoff asking the user to invoke another review command. Use the authorized Compound scope and preserve all consequential findings.

Domain documents contain preferences presented as exact rules: 2× spacing, 0.96 press scale, zero bounce, fixed icon blur and root font smoothing. Use only when the selected design and rendering warrant them.
One-color-one-meaning within 15 degrees, all-neutral interactive elements being misleading, and one filled action per view are overly universal. Brand hierarchy and redundant affordances govern.

Review-only nonmutation is appropriate for a review request, not a ban on fixing issues in an authorized build. A source saying leave colors alone does not require another approval when fixes are already commissioned.
The source's exact style values and screenshot-independent computed-value phrasing cannot substitute for actual rendered measurement or standards verification.
entries.reason: Useful consolidated evidence and ownership model plus substantial delegated craft. All six domain owners were read (better-writing is also assigned here) and the output-format reference was read. Ancillary deep recipes are inventoried separately.

source.description: Run a holistic interface review across accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color, and visual polish.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — semantic controls, focus, forms, motion and resilient content; references/screenshots.md — explicit verification coverage
principles: Prefer native buttons, links, forms, dialog/disclosure behavior and visible labels. Give complex widgets the complete APG keyboard model; site navigation is not an application menu merely because it has links.

Preserve or deliberately replace the browser focus indicator. Verify the whole custom perimeter across every adjacent surface and relevant state, including forced colors; sticky bars must not obscure the focused control.

Keep natural tab order, use roving tabindex within appropriate composite widgets, trap modal focus with an inert background and restore it on close. Choose initial focus by the task, with a safe action for destructive confirmations.

Apply WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 as 24×24 CSS px or a documented exception; 44px touch and 40px desktop are usability goals where appropriate. Expand actual buttons/labels rather than replaced inputs, and prevent overlapping targets.

Use persistent labels, appropriate type/inputmode/autocomplete and accessible names containing visible labels. Keep paste/password-manager support. Native disabled and aria-disabled have different focus, form and activation behavior.

Allow an incomplete submission to reveal actionable errors; prevent repeat in-flight submissions without erasing the label. Link inline errors with aria-describedby, mark aria-invalid and focus the first invalid field or a suitable multi-error summary.

Choose one announcement mechanism by purpose: focus when moving into the relevant content, described-by for a control-specific message, stable polite status for routine updates and alert only for urgent untied errors. Do not steal focus for toasts.

Design a static/reduced-spatial-motion path, visible controls for applicable autoplaying content, and persistent errors/actions rather than fleeting toasts. Keep state feedback understandable when motion is skipped.
Use meaningful headings/landmarks, skip navigation and scroll-margin for anchors. Test text at 200% and reflow at 320 CSS px, allowing true two-dimensional content to scroll within its own region.
Walk the complete keyboard path and a target screen-reader/browser combination separately from automated checks. Report unrun checks as not verified; group findings by root cause and user impact.
conflicts: Reject fixed exact recipe values as universal conformance rules. Single h1/no skipped levels are useful structural conventions, not standalone WCAG failures without applicable evidence.

The source says leave failing colors unchanged unless separately asked; an authorized accessibility fix already includes necessary color repair within the design contract. Do not add a redundant permission gate.
Its code does not by itself fully implement custom modal trapping, scroll lock or accessible dialog naming. overscroll-behavior:contain alone is not full background scroll locking.

The motion fallback relies on tiny durations to preserve end events; prefer explicit state completion and cancellation. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in textarea is an optional product shortcut, not native default behavior. Never indiscriminately trim passwords or other intentionally whitespace-sensitive inputs.

Review verdicts apply only to inspected flows and criteria; an Approve word or automated scan does not certify WCAG compliance. Native media exceptions, contrast exemptions and input-purpose applicability still require context.
entries.reason: The most directly reusable accessibility source in the batch. All six delegated documents were read, including their distinctions between conformance and larger usability targets.

source.description: Review and improve focus states, keyboard support, ARIA, forms, screen readers, hit areas, and motion accessibility.

entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; DESIGN.md layout/responsive contract; UI craft reference; screenshots.md stress cases
principles: Express grouping through proximity first, background containers when a unit needs a visible surface and separators for dense data; make inter-group spacing clearly larger than intra-group spacing.
Align related content to shared leading edges and use a consistent indentation step; align numerical columns to the trailing edge while preserving meaningful reading order.
Distinguish controls from static content using an underline, border, background or established control zone; avoid noninteractive badges that look identical to buttons.
Use logical inline properties and text-align:start for direction-dependent geometry. Test the mirrored layout where supported and keep digit order intact.
Make hidden content discoverable through a peeking next item, explicit count-bearing disclosure or another established cue; clamped essential text needs an accessible route to the full value.
Keep controls and text within layout/safe-area margins while allowing intended media bleed; ensure sticky headers/action rows do not cover focused controls or important content.
Set breakpoints where actual content stops fitting, use container queries for reusable components and test extremes plus the boundary widths.
Allow text containers to grow and rows to wrap; test pseudo-localization, long German labels, zoom and keyboard-induced viewport changes instead of assuming one percentage of string expansion.
Report each root cause with all affected locations, before/after behavior and user impact; distinguish inspected widths from not-verified cases.
conflicts: 2x grouping gaps and 12/24/16px recipes are starting points, not universal compliance or brand laws; preserve proven compact density and approved tokens.
A visible radius on every inset button and always-short first views are aesthetic/content choices; useful service/SEO content must not be cut or hidden to satisfy them.
The reference's nowrap button example can still overflow in very narrow containers; content-aware wrapping or a suitable alternative is necessary.
RTL sample combines logical placement with a physical safe-area-right value; use the correct physical inset for the final placement.
'Approve if no HIGH' cannot certify unsupported widths or all accessibility; preserve the actual evidence boundary.
entries.reason: One of the strongest direct additions: concrete, mostly stack-neutral layout mechanics and stress tests fit HTML/custom CSS immediately.

source.description: Improve interface structure through grouping, alignment, reading order, progressive disclosure, and adaptive responsive layouts.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md: UX writing contracts; references/dependencies.md: copywriting ownership
principles: Read neighboring copy, localization conventions and product vocabulary first. Keep one voice and stable terminology across labels, toasts, menus and steps; vary tone with success, routine work, errors and destructive consequences.
Name button actions with a useful verb and object. A destructive confirmation should still be answerable from Delete project and Cancel even when the body is skipped.
Write links that identify their destination outside the surrounding paragraph. Repeated Learn more links need a topic-specific accessible name.
Label settings for the enabled state, avoid double negatives, and link directly to the relevant setting instead of describing a navigation maze.
An error should state the next useful action beside the failed field without blame. Preserve entered data; recurring errors may call for redesign or a better hint before the failure.

Distinguish first-use empty state from no-results: explain the purpose and creation action for the former; identify the query/filter and a way out for the latter. Do not hide persistent instructions in a state that vanishes once data exists.
Use placeholders only as format examples; keep visible labels. Localize whole templates with proper pluralization instead of concatenating translated fragments around a variable.
Check the label against the actual invoked action and preserve one flow vocabulary. Use device-neutral verbs when the same interface serves pointer and touch.
conflicts: Its example Use only letters for your name must not become an invented validation rule; real names may contain spaces, punctuation and non-Latin characters. Copy must reflect a justified real constraint.
Sentence case, no idioms and preferred pronouns are defaults to adapt to the actual German/Swiss brand voice, not universal prohibitions.
Source inspection can verify wording intent, but rendered truncation, translated growth and assistive announcements still require their respective runtime checks.
entries.reason: Direct, source-specific UX writing knowledge with clear ownership boundaries; complements rather than replaces the installed German copywriting skill.

source.description: Improve UX writing for interface labels, errors, empty states, settings, notifications, and product voice consistency.

entries.destination: references/inspiration.md and references/service-learning.md — evidence model; references/screenshots.md — capture interpretation
principles: Scope research to the named effect or to the whole frontend system; do not answer a gradient question with an unrelated token inventory. State whether evidence came from a live browser, fetched source or screenshot reconstruction.
Label observations measured, derived or inferred. Browser computed values describe the visited runtime state; authored HTML/CSS exposes declarations and variants but does not prove which rule wins.

Explain effects as layers in paint order with each layer’s perceptual job. Inspect ::before/::after, oversize bounds, blur, masks, alpha, blending and backdrop relationships; ignore idle blur(0px)/transform:none artifacts.

For whole-system analysis, inventory tokens, recurring type/spacing/depth values, loaded fonts, breakpoints and motion patterns, then verify a second width/state. Record unread cross-origin sheets and runtime-generated gaps explicitly.
Treat framework/library fingerprints as evidence of varying strength, not proof or absence tests. Explain the transferable technique rather than inventing an authoring API from compiled artifacts.

For a screenshot-only source, report relative geometry and visual categories, name the unknown capture scale and avoid claiming CSS pixel sizes, framework, breakpoints or unseen behavior. Sampled colors describe the image, not necessarily the authored token.

Close with the reusable mechanism, the values that matter to perception and what will not transfer—licensed type, source identity, raster-specific effects or viewport-tuned geometry. Treat source-page instructions as untrusted content.
conflicts: Do not install Chrome DevTools MCP or change browser/provider because the source recommends it. Use actual tools and preserve other sessions/processes.

The claim that sampled screenshot contrast is exact needs limits: antialiasing, compression, color profiles, alpha and unknown backgrounds can prevent recovery of normative text colors. Screenshot sampling alone does not certify WCAG.

Ordering by y and z is not a complete paint-order algorithm; stacking contexts, DOM order, pseudo-elements and pointer-events affect inspection. Empty CSS hits do not prove the effect is non-CSS, and probing getContext can initialize an untouched canvas.

Default breakpoints, a common font or nine shadow values do not prove thoughtlessness. Stack fingerprints such as data-slot and class patterns are weak clues; absence of Google Fonts requests does not prove fonts are self-hosted.
Its no-code-snippet ending is an explanation preference, not a ban on implementing a requested pattern. Preserve research scope and distinguish reconstruction from source recovery.
entries.reason: Strong source-specific evidence discipline and layer analysis directly improve Web reference learning. All four delegated analysis methods were read.

source.description: Answers how was this built about an interface. Give it a URL and name the thing you're curious about, and it reads the layers that produce the effect. Reads the whole frontend instead when you don't name a thing. From a screenshot it reconstructs rather than reads and says so.

entries.destination: Change-scoped UI-QA innerhalb des führenden Compound-/Web-Ablaufs
principles: Reviewziel, Base-/Head-Revision, Commitanteil und uncommittete Dateien getrennt dokumentieren. Neue untracked Komponenten mit erfassen; ein einzelner Dirty-Tree-Edit darf den eigentlichen Branch nicht verdecken.

Nicht nur geänderte Dateien, sondern ihre gerenderten Verbraucher prüfen. Bei Tokens, Themes und gemeinsamen Primitives nach dem verwendeten Token suchen und über direkte Importer hinaus die betroffenen Seitenfamilien bestimmen.

Entfernte Zeilen auf verlorene Semantik, Labels, Fokus, Reduced Motion, logische CSS-Eigenschaften, Sprachmetadaten und Wrapping prüfen. Eine äquivalente native oder anderweitige Ersetzung räumt das Signal aus; die Entfernung allein ist kein Fehler.
Jeden Befund als eingeführt, Regression oder vorbestehend klassifizieren und am tatsächlichen Review-Ref belegen. Fehlerauswirkung und Verursachung sind getrennte Informationen.

Die formulierte Absicht gegen alle notwendigen Zustände halten: Hover, Fokus, aktiv, disabled, loading, selected, leer, Fehler und schmale Ansicht. Unvollständige Varianten- oder Übersetzungsumstellungen auch dann erfassen, wenn der Happy Path funktioniert.

Systemische Ursachen einmal am Token oder gemeinsamen Bauteil melden und sämtliche bestätigten Verbraucher zuordnen. Befund enthält Ort, Istzustand, Korrektur, Nutzerauswirkung und beobachtete Verifikation.
Quellcode- und visuelle Belege getrennt halten. Tatsächliche Pixel für visuelle Behauptungen inspizieren; fehlende Runtime-Prüfung sichtbar als nicht verifiziert ausweisen.

Ein reiner Reviewauftrag verändert keine Nutzerdaten oder Arbeitskopie. Für gerenderte Baselines isolierte Checkouts bzw. vorhandene verlässliche Builds verwenden, ohne den aktiven parallelen Workspace umzuschalten.
conflicts: Starre Grenzen von fünf Verbrauchern, drei Altbefunden oder 15 Gesamtbefunden sowie automatisches Verengen auf einen Flow widersprechen der beauftragten Abdeckung und Qualitätspriorität. Reale Abdeckung benennen, keine künstliche Sparquote.

Nicht stoppen, nur weil better-interface oder einzelne better-* Skills fehlen; den vorhandenen führenden Ablauf verwenden und konkrete Methodenlücken benennen. Keine zweite konkurrierende Review-Steuerung starten.
Rendered verification ist im Original nur opt-in. Für beauftragte Web-Bauten bleibt die vorhandene Browser-/Screenshot-QA verbindlich.
Das pauschale Approve bei ausschliesslich vorbestehenden Problemen ist kein Website-Releaseurteil: kritische Altfehler können weiterhin den vereinbarten Nutzerweg blockieren.
Auth-/Toolfehler bei PR-Ermittlung nicht als gesichertes 'keine PR vorhanden' ausgeben. Die Quelle legt diese ungenaue Zusammenfassung nahe; korrekt ist 'nicht ermittelbar'.
entries.reason: Sehr brauchbare Ergänzung für nachvollziehbare UI-Regressionsreviews; Scope-, Evidence- und Ursachenmodell übernehmen, fremde Orchestrierung und künstliche Limits verwerfen.

source.description: Interface review of a change rather than a screen: uncommitted work, the current branch, or a pull request. Covers interface quality, not correctness, tests, or security.

entries.destination: Gezielte Richtungsentscheidungen in DESIGN.md; optionale Variantenprobe im realen Seitenkontext
principles: Varianten als unterschiedliche Antworten auf eine explizite Hauptachse planen: Struktur, Dichte, Betonung, Typografie oder Stimme. Sekundärentscheidungen daraus ableiten, damit Unterschiede zuordenbar bleiben.
Richtungen nach ihrer Eigenschaft benennen und vor dem Bau erklären, wann sie nützen und welche Kosten entstehen. Reine Tönungswechsel liefern selten eine echte strukturelle Entscheidung.

Jede Variante mit gleicher inhaltlicher Aufgabe, realistischen Mengen und denselben Accessibility-Mindestanforderungen prüfen. Fehlende Namen, Fokus, Tastaturzugang oder unzugängliches Clipping sind keine ästhetischen Tradeoffs.
Jeweils eine Variante in voller Grösse auf der wirklichen Seite mit benachbarten Komponenten zeigen. Kontext, Hintergrund, schmale/breite Ansicht und Nutzungsfrequenz beeinflussen die Wahl.
Ein URL-Parameter kann Varianten reproduzierbar adressieren; ein als Prüfsteuerung erkennbarer Picker wechselt ohne störende Animation und zeigt den aktiven Wert zugänglich an.

Vor dem Vergleich jede Variante tatsächlich rendern und Interaktionen prüfen. Nach Auswahl die gewählte Richtung sauber integrieren und alternative Implementierungen bzw. Harness nach dem vereinbarten Lebenszyklus entfernen.
conflicts: Drei Varianten, maximal fünf und immer nur ein kleines UI-Stück sind keine universellen Limits. Anzahl und Umfang folgen der offenen Entscheidung, nicht einem Sparbudget.

Das Verbot einer eigenen Empfehlung und zwingendes Stoppen bis zur Nutzerwahl passen nicht zu bereits autorisierter autonomer Umsetzung. Bindende Geschmacksvorgaben respektieren, sonst begründet entscheiden.
Die Pflichtpalette des Pickers und Z-Index 2147483647 sind keine Produktdesignregeln. Picker darf Inhalt nicht verdecken; Tastaturshortcuts dürfen Eingabefelder und andere Controls nicht übernehmen.

Die Aussage Harness dürfe nichts aus Produktion importieren widerspricht teilweise echter Kontext-/Komponentenwiederverwendung. Entscheidend ist die einseitige Abhängigkeit: Produktion darf keine Prüf-Fiksturen benötigen.
entries.reason: Sinnvoll, wenn eine konkrete Designentscheidung offen ist; kein zusätzliches Pflicht-Brainstorming vor klarer Implementierung.

entries.destination: Web UI/error-copy rules + PRODUCT.md vocabulary; installed copywriting remains primary for marketing
principles: For instructional UI and documentation, put the condition before the command and give one actionable step at a time; define an unfamiliar necessary term at first use.
Keep code, identifiers, commands, paths, quoted errors, proper names and known facts unchanged when simplifying prose.
Use specific state/cause/recovery structure for errors; name a cause only when known and give a concrete recovery action appropriate to the user.
Maintain consistent concept names through a flow and break ambiguous noun chains into explicit relationships. Preserve meaningful distinctions rather than treating every synonym as interchangeable.
Delete empty claims such as seamless, powerful or gracefully handles; replace them with observable behavior when evidence exists.
Separate factual/procedural text from persuasive brand writing. STE-inspired plain language can improve support/help text without governing marketing voice.

If formal ASD-STE100 compliance is actually requested, consult the official standard/dictionary and specialist review; the local word-swaps are the author’s suggestions and the strict index is explicitly incomplete.
conflicts: Five-sentence chat cap, bans on lists/headings/contractions, American spelling and hard 20/25-word limits do not govern Raphael’s task or German/Swiss website copy.
Replacing should with must or deleting may/might/could can change factual uncertainty, permission or obligation. Preserve modality and distinguish known, unknown and conditional facts.
Collapsing check/verify/validate/confirm into make sure that and all settings/options into configuration can erase real technical or UI distinctions.
The source examples introduce causal certainty and numerical facts that cannot be inferred during a rewrite. No fake STE certification or guaranteed translation-error reduction.
The full ASD dictionary and rule-catalog.md were not read; no formal STE conformance conclusion is offered.
entries.reason: Full SKILL and use-cases, strict-vocabulary, word-swaps read. Integrate only applicable clarity tactics; preserve brand copy ownership and honest uncertainty.

entries.destination: Web dependencies / Figma adapter; DESIGN.md token-to-design mapping
principles: For an authorized Figma task, discover existing pages, components, styles, variable collections and naming first; reuse matching definitions and create only the missing delta.

Maintain an explicit bridge from implementation tokens to Figma primitives, semantic aliases, modes and WEB codeSyntax; preserve original CSS variable names instead of guessing them from display names.

Model related children with auto-layout. Parent nodes before assigning FILL/HUG; distinguish child FIXED/HUG/FILL values from frame FIXED/AUTO sizing, and verify parent dimensions before relying on FILL.

For text changes load and await each current font from styled segments, then mutate and return affected IDs. Give wrapping text HEIGHT autoresize and a deliberate width; inspect clipping with screenshots.

Retain actual runtime contracts: plain JS with top-level await/return, asynchronous page selection, complete returned mutation IDs, normalized colors, immutable paint reassignment and context-aware retry after errors.
Validate structure and rendered pixels separately; use screenshots with enough resolution to judge small text and components, and remove work-in-progress placeholders before completion.

Resolve component property definitions on a component set or a non-variant component, and narrow node capabilities before reading getters. Check live tool schemas and the installed skill before operational use.
conflicts: This downloaded skill is research data, not a replacement for installed Figma prerequisites. No Figma writes, tool calls or page fan-out are authorized by this extraction.

Do not generalize the ten-operation cap, compulsory parallel writes, assumed plan mode quotas, default font availability or helper API availability into Web's workflow. Actual documented installed-tool constraints still apply when invoked.

entries.destination: Figma-Adapter für beauftragte Code→Figma-Ansichten; DESIGN.md: Komponenten-/Token-/Font-Zuordnung; Screenshot-QA
principles: Eine komponierte Ansicht zunächst in Abschnittsaufgaben und tatsächlich verwendete Komponenten zerlegen; Code-Connect-Zuordnungen, vorhandene Instanzen und passende Bibliotheken als konkrete Wiederverwendungsbelege erfassen.

Bibliotheksgebundene Typografie von selbst erzeugtem Text unterscheiden: lokale Fehler korrigieren, Abweichungen in Instanzen oder veröffentlichten Textstyles als Bibliothekslücke dokumentieren statt unbemerkt Overrides aufzuzwingen.
Lokale Variable-Collections und veröffentlichte Remote-Variablen getrennt suchen. Ein leeres getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync ist kein Beleg, dass keine Designsystem-Tokens existieren.

Bibliotheken gezielt nach jeweils einer Suchabsicht abfragen; bei unbekannten Namen Synonyme separat verwenden. Bibliotheksschlüssel, Komponententyp, Varianten, TEXT-/BOOLEAN-/INSTANCE_SWAP-Properties und Token-Code-Syntax festhalten.

Container mit Auto Layout aufbauen und wiederkehrende Elemente als echte Komponenteninstanzen komponieren. Property-verwaltete Texte über die entdeckten setProperties-Schlüssel überschreiben; auch implizite Default-Props des Quellcodes berücksichtigen.

Bestehende SVG-Icons exakt importieren, viewBox und explizite Abmessungen angeben und currentColor bewusst auflösen oder binden. Icons nicht aus gedrehten Linien rekonstruieren; austauschbare Icons über INSTANCE_SWAP statt Variantenexplosion modellieren.

Farben, Abstände und Radien an vorhandene Variablen binden, Text-/Effektstyles wiederverwenden und die echten CSS-Variablennamen in Code-Syntax erhalten. Rückgabewerte von Paint-Bindungen neu zuweisen.

Gesamtansicht und lesbare Einzelabschnitte prüfen: Clipping, Überlagerungen, Platzhaltertexte, falsche Varianten, Fontsubstitution und leere Bildflächen. Nach Korrekturen betroffene Ansichten erneut prüfen.

Bei verfügbarer, beauftragter Browser→Figma-Erfassung Bildfüllungen über tatsächliche imageHash-Zuordnungen übertragen und Ausschnitt/Position prüfen. Temporäre eigene Referenznodes erst entfernen, wenn die Übertragung nachweislich vollständig ist.

Bei realer Figma-Nutzung installierte Skill-/Tool-Voraussetzungen erhalten: richtige Datei und Editorart, geladene Fonts, zulässige APIs, Node-IDs, Moduskontext und Fehlerrückmeldung safeToRetryWithoutCanvasRead beachten.
conflicts: Figma-Ausgabe, parallele Capture-Erzeugung und starr vorgeschriebene Suchreihenfolgen sind keine Web-Baupflicht. Toolbehauptungen des Research-Snapshots nicht mit der tatsächlich installierten Schnittstelle gleichsetzen.

Pixel-perfect ist eine Absicht, kein Ergebnisbeleg. Erfolgreiche Scripts oder Metadaten ersetzen keine visuelle Prüfung; Browser-Capture liefert ohne Prüfung ebenfalls keine garantierte Übereinstimmung.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md token/source mapping; library integration; installed Figma skill routing
principles: Inventory authoritative token files, CSS custom properties, theme config and component APIs alongside existing Figma collections, modes, styles and components; classify new, matching, conflicting and Figma-only items.

Preserve two identities: human-readable Figma names and exact code identifiers. Record code token, raw/resolved value, collection, semantic role, type and mode; use the actual CSS variable reference rather than deriving fictitious names.

Bind semantic roles to primitives where the existing system benefits from aliasing; keep theme modes coherent and bind component values to those semantics. Represent composite typography and shadows through appropriate styles.

Evaluate reuse by property API, token compatibility and ownership. Reuse matching assets, wrap a visually suitable component behind a compatible API, and rebuild only when a meaningful incompatibility warrants it.

Separate content, boolean visibility and icon swaps from visual variant axes; extract independently stateful repeating subcomponents to avoid variant explosion. Verify actual hover, focus, pressed, disabled and loading behavior instead of checking counts alone.
Document tokens with bound swatches, actual type specimens, spacing bars, radius/elevation examples and exact code names; include component purpose and usage guidance.
Combine structural verification of variant axes/property bindings with screenshots of size/state differences, text, grid labels and component bounds.

For optional Figma work, maintain exact returned IDs and pending validations in a durable ledger; inspect after partial failures and clean only owned exact IDs. Verify Code Connect mappings and snippets against actual code when that integration is requested.
conflicts: Reject universal 20–100+ calls, fixed phase/checklist IDs, a cover/foundations page before a single component, the hard 30-variant split threshold, and mandatory approval after each component. Match task scale and prior authorization.

Discovery recommends parallel use_figma reads while the main file forbids all parallel use_figma calls; component reference asks approval while the main file says continue. Installed specialist tool instructions govern actual execution.

Discovery includes bare CSS code syntax despite the var() rule; token bulk mapping can prefix an already --prefixed code name again. Sample variants omit distinct hover styling; example icon frames are not swappable instances. Treat examples as unverified implementation recipes.
Naming/collection architecture and theme counts are defaults, not universal requirements. Do not force light/dark modes, token layers, React, Tailwind or publication to satisfy Figma documentation.

Code Connect can require a published library and available server features; a mapping request does not silently authorize publication. Figma plan limits and API details must be checked in the installed specialist/current tools.

entries.destination: Web accessibility/component contracts; installed Figma specialist for rendering
principles: Document each component's accessible name, native element/role, value, description, state and keyboard behavior per meaningful state; keep these properties separate instead of stuffing them all into the name.

Classify visible parts before specifying interaction: a field label and hint describe the input, a decorative icon is hidden from AT, and a trailing clear/password button remains an independently named action.

Describe keyboard tab sequence, composite-widget arrow navigation, semantic grouping and screen-reader reading sequence separately. Record conditional controls only in states and slot configurations where they actually exist.
Group purely visual states when their accessible semantics are identical; keep distinct entries for changed selection models, error, read-only, loading, or changed interactive controls.

For Figma handoff, keep the authored component Markdown as the source of truth; render matching variants, real slot contents and actual labels. Preserve stable source-node identifiers separately from human part names.
Validate that every documented interaction target has a corresponding preview target and annotation; unresolved target geometry is a handoff defect, not an acceptable silent omission.
Treat proposed announcement strings as expected behavior until tested with the named browser/screen-reader combination.
conflicts: Do not adopt mandatory Figma annotation output, provider configuration, template imports, no-questions/abort-only execution contract or three-iteration repair cap into Web.

The supporting agent conflates tab stops, semantic containers and AT reading stops. A tablist does not universally add an extra Tab stop; a static heading is not automatically keyboard-focusable; 'two grouping questions imply a focus stop' is invalid.
Reject the blanket rule that disabled controls always leave focus order: native disabled and aria-disabled differ; aria-disabled does not itself disable interaction or change tabindex.
Tooltip content is not universally a live region; use the actual tooltip/description pattern. Live-region content can also contain independently focusable actions.
The ARIA reference's accessible-name priority is oversimplified, aria-flowto is not a general reading-order override, and deprecated drag ARIA must not become a recommended implementation.
Forced identical stops on iOS, Android and Web can be wrong. Native-platform references were not read; no native-platform implementation claims are made.
entries.reason: The primary file is a 57,981-byte renderer, not an accessibility authoring authority. Its traceable per-state handoff model is useful after correcting the substantive supporting reference's focus-model errors.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md component anatomy; optional Figma documentation reference
principles: Document a component as a composition plus meaningful child anatomies: distinguish fixed subcomponents, optional boolean-controlled children, editable text, composable slots, layout containers and decorative structure.
For each slot record its purpose, accepted/preferred component families, default content and visibility control; describe what it does rather than merely counting children.
Choose a structurally rich representative variant when the default omits distinct parts; do not mistake color/size/theme variation for additional anatomy.
Preserve designer-facing wrapper names while retaining underlying component identity; include skipped wrappers when they own layout, fills, borders or effects.
Record hidden-by-default and mutually exclusive states separately from the expanded annotation artwork. Use real component properties to expose states when possible.
Group consecutive equivalent instances with counts, create one useful child anatomy per component family, and link only to sections that actually exist.
Measure annotation bounds again after revealing children or populating slots; check marker collisions, clipping, correspondence to table rows and text readability in screenshots.
Carry the source spec path and source hash into derived documentation so later drift can be detected.
conflicts: The uSpec render-meta/template/MCP-provider contract is specific to this producer; it is not a prerequisite for Web work. Reject unconditional Figma writes, no-question/no-stop commands, fixed fonts/colors/dimensions and the three-iteration cap as canonical rules.

The linked anatomy instructions still describe old live extraction fields and index-based boolean resolution; the main SKILL now seeds render-meta and binds names. Do not copy the two interfaces as a coherent implementation.

The renderer iterates child indexes after composition deduplication, which can misassociate later bounds; child artwork unhides before recording visibility. Preserve original identity and visibility rather than copying these scripts blindly.
Showing all hidden descendants together can display mutually exclusive states that never coexist in production; annotation artwork is not proof of valid runtime behavior.
entries.reason: Useful optional component-spec craft, especially slots and states; the 86KB Figma rendering implementation belongs to a specialist, not the HTML-first Web entrypoint.

entries.destination: Web copywriting adapter; DESIGN.md terminology, state and localization contract
principles: Review complete visitor tasks and adjacent states, not isolated strings. Record audience, task, moment, available action, terminology and the evidence surface before changing wording.

Inventory orientation, actions, inputs, feedback, recovery, assistance, state, decisions and dynamic data. Name the actual outcome in buttons and links; distinguish save, send, queue, publish, delete, archive and close.
For errors state what happened, what is affected and a recovery the system really supports. Do not suggest retry when it cannot help or promise a support response time without evidence.

Separate first use, valid zero data, no search results, filtered empty, permission limitation, loading failure and unavailable content. Do not hide persistent guidance solely in a disappearing empty state.

Keep stable voice but calibrate tone to stakes: calm actionable errors, measured waiting, explicit consequential decisions. Maintain one noun per object and one verb per recurring action while preserving functional distinctions.
Edit canonical copy/catalogs or source components; preserve keys, interpolation tokens, ICU plural/select branches, rich-text tags, escaping, semantic attributes and analytics/test identifiers.

Use complete translatable strings rather than concatenated fragments. Check locale expansion, grammatical variants, RTL/mixed-direction content, actual font coverage, wrapping, zoom and touch/keyboard equivalents for help.
Keep visible labels aligned with accessible names for voice input; do not infer names, focus order, announcements or screen-reader output from a screenshot.

For research claims distinguish observed, reported, inferred, proposed and verified. Match tests to the decision: comprehension, task success or recovery; subjective preference and conversion alone do not establish UX quality.

Add a terminology decision record with concept, preferred/rejected terms, functional distinction, evidence, affected surfaces and exceptions; verify changed copy in the rendered state before claiming implementation is checked.
conflicts: Do not convert this source's review/approval transitions into repeated permission gates for an already authorized implementation. Maintain the actual requested review versus edit scope.
Do not shorten away consequences or retrofit unsupported product behavior, testimonials, guarantees, legal rules or conversion claims. Pseudo-localization is not native-language approval.
Keep marketing persuasion under Raphael's copywriting voice rules; this source supplies interface semantics and evidence practices, not a competing global voice.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md: semantische Abstandsrollen; Layout-Craft und Token-Reconciliation
principles: Die sichtbare Gruppierung zuerst als Page → Section → Card → Inhalt → Inline-Beziehung beschreiben. Räumlich enger zusammengehörige Elemente sollen typischerweise näher stehen als voneinander unabhängige Gruppen.

Bestehende Spacing-Tokens und Namenskonventionen verwenden. Bei fehlendem System eine nachvollziehbare Skala entwickeln und Padding von Containerrahmen sowie Gap zwischen Geschwistern getrennt dokumentieren.

Von einer sinnvollen inneren Basis aus nach aussen abstimmen; die Quelle zeigt dafür beispielsweise 8 → 12 → 16 → 24 → 32. Als visuell zu prüfendes Ausgangsmuster behandeln, nicht als mathematisches Gesetz.

Abstände möglichst an gemeinsame Variablen binden und die Werte pro Hierarchieebene mit begründeten Ausnahmen festhalten. Kontextabhängige Komponentenabstände nicht durch pauschale tiefenabhängige Overrides beschädigen.
Bei stark verschachtelten Bereichen den Gesamtplatzbedarf prüfen und erforderlichenfalls Hierarchie oder Skala vereinfachen, statt jede Ebene blind zu multiplizieren.

Bestehende Inkonsistenzen systematisch von inneren Gruppierungen aus prüfen. Die wahrnehmbare Trennung ist der Zweck; zusätzliche Divider sind nicht nötig, wenn Abstände die Beziehung bereits verständlich machen.

4-/8px-Raster, 4px-Minimum und 48-/64px-Maximum sind mögliche Projektskalen, keine universellen Grenzen für responsive Websites, grosse Sektionen oder optische Korrekturen.
Nicht allein wegen fehlender Figma-Variablen neue Collections anlegen oder zusätzliche Bestätigung verlangen. Im HTML-first-Projekt ist die bestehende CSS-Tokenquelle massgeblich.

entries.destination: references/scrollcraft.md — optional multi-scene camera chain and seeking/QA tactics; GPT Image module remains authoritative
principles: Choose camera architecture from the story: a realistic walkthrough can chain each leg from the preceding rendered final frame; a miniature map can deliberately alternate dive clips and aerial connectors. A direction reversal at a realistic seam can look like a rewind even when composition matches.

For a connector, use the preceding rendered clip endpoint and the following rendered clip first frame as the conditioning images, rather than the independently generated scene stills. Inspect actual output endpoints; conditioning is not a guarantee of pixel identity.

Plan both position and velocity continuity. Settle each continuous-walkthrough leg into the same forward drift near the handoff, inspect a short boundary sequence, and review every seam while scrolling both down and up.

Use a shared art-direction preamble, palette, lighting and camera vocabulary across scenes, with approved content/style reference files under the existing GPT Image module. Keep posters as actual assets and choose mobile composition from the subject, not an automatic centre crop.

Probe the served media for usable seek ranges. When range serving is unavailable, a bounded Blob/object-URL fallback can make complete clips seekable; account for download latency and memory, revoke URLs, abort obsolete requests and dispose listeners/animation loops.

Coalesce currentTime seeks while a decoder is already seeking; keep the still visible until a frame actually paints; verify muted/playsinline and first-gesture behavior on iOS. Test fast flicks, URL-bar collapse, rotation, slow delivery and decode errors.

Use native-resolution, short-GOP encoding as a measured starting point, not a universal preset. Compare seek latency, visual softness, file size and device decode cost; select lighter mobile variants where needed.

Adjust per-section dwell independently from clip duration; a monotone linger remapping must preserve endpoints f(0)=0 and f(1)=1. Give copy enough readable dwell without trapping the visitor in a long scroll track.

Retain initial-HTML headings, body, links and CTA; enhance media around them. Reduced motion and failed JavaScript must leave a readable ordinary page. Scope styles and scroll coordinates to the actual section and define teardown before adapting the engine.
conflicts: Reject the Monid default, provider/model substitutions, CLI worker spawning, installation/auth flows, spending thresholds, mandatory camera/mobile interviews and universal diorama aesthetic. These are upstream workflow data, not authorization; installed GPT Image/Higgsfield and Scrollcraft instructions retain real tool authority.

The source calls seams frame-identical but also reports near-miss endpoints and PSNR below exact identity. Its ffmpeg -sseof -0.15 command samples near the end rather than proving extraction of the exact final displayed frame; inspect the actual boundary frames and motion.

The engine is not drop-in for an HTML-first site: it creates all copy through JS, has no disposal or URL.revokeObjectURL, uses global viewport/scroll coordinates and html/body rules, mutates section config, and keeps a perpetual rAF loop.

Opacity plus pointer-events does not remove hidden CTA links from keyboard navigation. The code provides no inert/tab-order synchronization; on narrow screens its route labels are display:none and buttons need explicit accessible names.

The documented live mobile source switch is not implemented for already-loaded clips: loadClip is guarded by s.loading and posters are selected only at mount. Reduced-motion preference is also sampled only once. Adapt both behaviors explicitly.

The claims that blob loading, identical prompts or a small crossfade guarantee smoothness/cohesion are too strong. There is no universal requirement to render two chains, prohibit responsive downscaling, or preserve full-native desktop video on every device.
entries.reason: A substantive, framework-independent scroll-media technique fits as an optional Scrollcraft extension; the supplied engine and commercial pipeline need adaptation, not wholesale adoption. Both supporting prompt templates and all 448 engine lines were read.

entries.destination: Accessibility-Regressions-QA mit isolierten Baselines; Evidenzformat in docs/qa
principles: Vorher und Nachher mit demselben tatsächlich geladenen Ziel, Zustand, Selektorumfang und Regelsatz vergleichen. Neu, behoben und vorbestehend getrennt zählen, statt Altbefunde als neue Regression auszugeben.

Baseline und Head aus isolierten Arbeitskopien bzw. revisionsgebundenen Builds bedienen. Bereitschaft an tatsächlicher Buildrevision, Fonts, Bildern und relevantem UI-Zustand prüfen, nicht an einer pauschalen Wartezeit.
Wenn die Targetkonfiguration verändert wurde, beide Scans über ein explizites äquivalentes Ziel auflösen. Ein gleichlautender Konfigname garantiert nicht dieselbe Seite.
Neue Befunde mit originalem Selektor, reproduzierbarer Interaktion, DOM-/Accessibility-Tree-Fakt und konkreter Korrektur dokumentieren. Datei/Zeile nur nennen, wenn eine echte Zuordnung vorliegt.
Auswirkung und Belegbasis getrennt bewerten: reproduzierbarer Fakt, interpretative Einschätzung und noch erforderlicher AT-/Nutzertest sind unterschiedliche Evidenzarten.

Scan, zustandsübergreifenden Audit, Remediation und Regressionstest unterscheiden. Bei grösseren DOM-Änderungen Selektordrift berücksichtigen und zusätzlich den aktuellen vollständigen Zustand prüfen.
Nicht geprüfte Kriterien und Seiten als offen bzw. ausserhalb des Umfangs dokumentieren; vorhandene Keyboard-/Browser- und Assistive-Technology-Prüfungen ergänzen automatisierte Regeln.
Nach beauftragter Korrektur denselben betroffenen Zustand erneut prüfen. Prozess-/Browserinstanzen nur dann abbauen, wenn sie der eigenen Aufgabe gehören.

sleep 2 ist kein verlässlicher HMR-/Build-Ready-Nachweis. Ein vorhandener Selektor kann auch aus einer alten Buildrevision stammen.

entries.destination: Web references/screenshots.md / accessibility QA evidence and specialist adapter
principles: State whether the work is a one-page automated scan, a set of browser-driven checks, or a scoped multi-page audit; name pages, states and assistive-technology coverage.
Ground every finding in an observed selector and concrete fact (for example measured contrast or missing accessible name). Add file:line only when real source mapping supplies it.
Separate severity from evidence basis: an observed deterministic violation, a supported interpretive concern and a test needing real assistive technology are different claims.
When a conclusion combines an observed fact with human interpretation, retain the fact but do not present the broader judgment as mechanically proven.

For critical flows and rich controls, map the actual keyboard/ARIA contract and exercise reachable states. The accessibility tree is useful machine evidence, not a substitute for actual announcements or AT-user experience.
Mark unexercised, inaccessible or uncertain criteria as undetermined and report relevant scope gaps. Do not average away a failure or count unknowns as passes.
Use scope → route/state exploration → representative evaluation → criterion-specific reporting for audits, while preserving canonical Web’s all-delivered-route desktop/mobile QA coverage.
After a mechanical remediation, rerun the affected check and journey; keep baseline/current findings separate. Prepare precise AT test steps when that evidence remains unavailable.
conflicts: No claim of WCAG compliance from an automated scan, DOM tree, semantic locator or screenshot. The cited 57%/80% automation figures are not verified universal coverage estimates.
The methodology evidence-budget and stop-after-one-screenshot prescriptions conflict with Raphael’s quality priority. Gather what an unresolved consequential question needs.
No forced AccessLint install, --latest CLI, browser teardown --all or tool/provider switch. Reuse actual available specialist tools and stop only processes owned by the task.
The source contradictory locate-only versus apply-fixes wording must not expand a review scope. Real content evidence can support alt/label fixes; a blanket TODO is not an acceptable completed build.
No synthetic persona claims of AT testing; human judgment, browser mechanics and lived experience must remain separately labeled.

entries.destination: Web accessibility reference; DESIGN.md state contracts; browser QA evidence
principles: Run available rendered audits and inspect their failing nodes, then inspect the accessibility tree and exercise the affected keyboard flow. Retest the same state after a fix; distinguish automated from manual coverage.

Prefer native buttons, links, inputs and modal dialog behavior; ensure names, roles, states, visible labels, field instructions and actual activation agree. Do not add duplicate Enter/Space handlers to native buttons.

Use meaningful alt for informative assets, empty alt for decoration, text equivalents for complex charts, and captions/transcripts appropriate to media content. Keep real text outside GPT Image raster assets.

Check text contrast at 4.5:1, large text at 3:1 and applicable non-text controls at 3:1. Correct the source's units: large text begins at 18pt (24 CSS px) or 14pt bold (about 18.67 CSS px), with font/context caveats; do not round failing ratios upward.
Test skip navigation, logical focus order, visible focus, modal exit/return and focus visibility under sticky bars. Use measured header/footer offsets for scroll margins rather than copying 80/60px.

Apply WCAG 2.2 target-size and dragging checks with their exceptions: 24 CSS px AA minimum/spacing rules, with larger comfortable targets where useful; provide a single-pointer alternative to dragging as well as keyboard operation.

Associate error text and invalid state with the input; distinguish a field error from a system failure, preserve entered values, and announce significant state changes without excessive alerts or double focus jumps.

Cover consistent help placement, avoidance of redundant entry, password-manager/paste assistance, 200% text resize, 320 CSS px reflow, user text spacing, high contrast and reduced motion. Record which assistive technologies were actually used.
conflicts: The main contrast table substitutes px for pt and its sample hex-ratio annotations are approximate/inaccurate; use actual computed colors and the W3C source, not comments as measured evidence.

The supplied modal trap omits empty/hidden/disabled/dynamically changing focusables, listener cleanup and focus restoration; the error example focuses a field then a possibly non-focusable summary. These are illustrative snippets, not production-ready accessibility implementations.
A global 0.01ms motion reset does not handle JS-driven scroll media or prove accessible motion. Use state-aware fallbacks so content remains visible and functional.
Do not infer legal compliance, full WCAG conformance or screen-reader correctness from Lighthouse 100, screenshots or partial checklists. Do not run the source's global axe installation.
entries.reason: Directly strengthens HTML-first implementation and evidence-led QA, with material source defects corrected and compliance claims withheld.

entries.destination: Web references/stack.md + QA/security subsection of dependencies.md
principles: Check deployed HTTPS, mixed content, response headers, console/network failures and relevant dependency risks alongside source inspection. A Lighthouse Best Practices result is only one diagnostic input.
Use semantic valid HTML with unique IDs, meaningful landmarks, correctly nested lists and no nested interactive controls; set doctype, charset early and a viewport that preserves zoom.

Use feature detection and supports queries instead of user-agent branching. Keep polyfills targeted to supported browsers, preferably bundled/self-hosted rather than loading uncontrolled third-party code.

Prefer textContent for untrusted text and a maintained sanitizer when HTML is genuinely needed. Roll out CSP and Trusted Types against actual sink usage and browser support; do not treat the framework as a sanitizer.

Pin third-party assets and use valid SRI where response CORS and immutable delivery permit it. Generate any nonce freshly per response; verify the actual delivered policy before calling protection enabled.
Use deferred/module scripts where appropriate, passive listeners when no preventDefault is required, and cleanup/AbortController for listeners tied to component lifetimes.
Request powerful browser permissions in a meaningful user action with an understandable purpose. Configure Permissions-Policy as an HTTP response header with the real feature needs.

Handle failures with useful recovery and operational diagnostics. Decide production sourcemap publication/access intentionally; removing a sourceMappingURL alone does not protect a publicly served map.
conflicts: The main SKILL Permissions-Policy meta examples are ineffective; use the response header shown in SECURITY.md.
SECURITY.md falsely says structuredClone drops __proto__ and functions. A local language check preserves the own __proto__ key and throws DataCloneError for a function; cloning is not sanitization.

The Trusted Types example creates a default policy, which can automatically convert raw strings at sinks. Its unconditional claim that assigning a raw string now throws is false when that default policy handles it.
Do not copy the fixed abc123 nonce, enable HSTS includeSubDomains/preload without deployment prerequisites, or interpret hidden-source-map as access control.

No automatic npm audit fix/update, mandatory telemetry vendor, arbitrary source-map ban or proof of safety from a clean scanner. Date-sensitive Trusted Types baseline claims need actual browser compatibility checks.
The source event delegation matches only the direct event target; real nested icons/labels may require closest() with a container-boundary check. Error boundaries and React examples are conditional.
entries.reason: Both the full SKILL and delegated SECURITY.md read. Integrate deployment-evidenced practices with explicit corrections to unsafe/inaccurate examples.

entries.destination: Web performance QA / references/screenshots.md + stack.md + seo-pages.md evidence limits
principles: Record URL/origin scope, device, window, sample and p75 for field LCP/INP/CLS. Good thresholds are LCP ≤2.5s, INP ≤200ms and CLS ≤0.1; missing field data is unavailable, never passing.

Keep CrUX (typically 28-day aggregate), first-party RUM, controlled lab traces, Lighthouse and source hypotheses distinct. A local observer is one session; no immediate field improvement follows from a fresh deployment.

Measure the same route/state and conditions before/after: browser/tool version, CSS viewport, CPU/network profile, cache, auth, consent and experiment state. For headline decisions use repeated equivalent runs and report central value and variability.

Decompose LCP into TTFB, resource discovery delay, resource transfer and render delay; fix the dominant measured part. Place important content and discoverable image URLs in initial HTML; prioritize the real LCP resource and preload only if discovery remains late.

Resize/compress responsive images and reserve intrinsic space. Font delivery and measured fallback metrics can affect both LCP and CLS; do not blindly copy another font pair’s size-adjust/ascent/descent values.

Decompose slow interactions into input delay, handler processing and presentation delay. Attribute contention to actual first/third-party tasks before changing handlers or applying framework memoization.

Yield between chunks using an available scheduler with fallback, or use a worker for appropriate computation; choose chunk boundaries by measured time rather than assuming 100 items is cheap. Confirm visible feedback actually paints before remaining work.
Trace the initiator of layout shifts, not just the node that moved. Reserve realistic media/embed/async slots and test banners, validation, consent, long localization and post-load states.

Use speculation rules only as a measured progressive navigation enhancement: scope likely safe routes, exclude side-effectful endpoints, handle prerender activation, and measure wasted bytes/server work as well as latency.

If production RUM is authorized, reuse the existing pipeline, prefer lifecycle-correct web-vitals reporting, minimize/sanitize payloads, record release and sampling, aggregate route templates and form factors, and avoid user text/query strings.

Use raw metric and trace evidence for performance conclusions. Screenshots cannot prove performance, a Lighthouse score cannot prove field outcomes, and CWV improvements do not guarantee search rankings.
conflicts: Critical CSS <14KB, TTFB <800ms, font-display:swap and adding speculation rules are not universal release gates. Apply the relevant measured fix and preserve CSP/no-JS behavior.
The top-level SKILL loosely lists svg as an LCP candidate; the detailed reference correctly distinguishes an image inside svg. Generic inline SVG shapes are not a blanket LCP candidate.

Framework quick fixes are incomplete/version-sensitive: Image fill still needs a sized parent, ssr:false may harm essential content, useTransition does not eliminate arbitrary CPU work, and inline CSS-load handlers may violate CSP.
The React Router/Next/Vue examples do not authorize a whole React migration. Astro static HTML and bounded actual React islands remain the default-compatible integration paths.
Source descriptions of specific DevTools MCP capabilities/eagerness timings must be checked against tools and browser versions actually available; no forced provider/tool route.

RUM privacy and live collection need the real project contract; even location.pathname can contain identifying data and should be normalized. Generic numerical SEO savings or ranking claims are rejected.
entries.reason: Full SKILL plus MEASUREMENT, LCP, INP, CLS and RUM references read. Strong direct evidence methodology with scoped optimization tactics, preserving all SEO-route and image/motion contracts.

entries.destination: Performance-/SEO-QA; DESIGN.md: messbare Ressourcen- und Medienverträge; bestehende Screenshot-Evidenz ergänzen
principles: Messbefunde in Feldwerte, einzelne Browser-/Laborsitzungen und statische Codehypothesen trennen. Fehlende CrUX-Daten als nicht verfügbar ausweisen; Origin-Daten nicht als Beweis für eine einzelne URL darstellen.

Vorher/Nachher mit gleichem finalem Pfad, Zustand, Tool-/Browserversion, Viewport, CPU-/Netzprofil, Cache, Authentifizierung und Consent vergleichen. Bei entscheidenden Labormetriken mehrere gleichartige Navigationen und Median plus Streuung angeben.

Reale p75-Werte für LCP, INP und CLS zur Priorisierung nutzen; im Trace LCP-Entdeckung, Dokumentlatenz, Renderblocking, Drittanbieter und Main-Thread-Arbeit als Ursachen untersuchen. TBT bleibt Laborproxy und ist kein Feld-INP.
Nur gemessene Engpässe optimieren. Ressourcenbudgets für Seitentyp, Nutzergeräte und Netze festlegen; Quellwerte wie 1,5 MB Gesamtgewicht sind Startbeispiele, keine universellen Releasegrenzen.

Wahrscheinliche LCP-Bilder früh im HTML auffindbar, passend dimensioniert und eager laden; fetchpriority gezielt setzen. Unterhalb des ersten Sichtbereichs lazy laden und srcset/sizes, Seitenverhältnis und Format gegen reale Darstellungsgrössen prüfen.
Preloads und Preconnects nur bei nachgewiesen spätem Entdecken bzw. benötigten Origins ergänzen. Unnötige Hochprioritätsressourcen können mit LCP konkurrieren.

JavaScript nach Feature oder schwerem Widget aufteilen und nicht benötigte Drittanbieter hinter einer funktionierenden, zugänglichen Fassade laden. Das passt zu statischem HTML und begrenzter Island-Hydrierung.

Fonts mit tatsächlich benötigten Glyphen/Gewichten und funktionierenden Fallbacks ausliefern; Layoutmetriken beim Fontwechsel prüfen. Bei langlebigem Asset-Caching gehashte Dateinamen und nachvollziehbare Invalidierung verwenden.

DOM-Messungen vor Schreiboperationen bündeln, Animationen am Rendering-Takt ausrichten und teure Listen nur bei gemessenem Bedarf optimieren. Dynamische Importkosten und Laufzeitkosten getrennt messen.

Optionales RUM in vorhandene autorisierte Telemetrie einordnen: web-vitals-Lifecycle, Releasekennung, Routentemplates, Stichprobe, Zeitraum und p75 statt Durchschnitt dokumentieren; keine Querystrings, Forminhalte oder vollständige DOM-Fragmente erfassen.

Early Hints, Speculation Rules und View Transitions als optionale, unterstützungsabhängige Verbesserungen behandeln. Trefferquote, zusätzliche Transfers, Serverkosten, Analytics-Auslösung und Reduced Motion prüfen; Felderfolg nach Deployment bleibt bis zu neuen Nutzerdaten offen.
conflicts: Das responsive Hero-Beispiel verwendet loading:lazy und widerspricht dem späteren LCP-Beispiel. LCP niemals pauschal lazy laden; decoding:sync ist ebenfalls keine allgemeine Bestleistungsgarantie.
content-visibility:auto ist keine DOM-Virtualisierung. Mehr als 100 Items ist kein universeller Schwellenwert; SEO-Inhalte nicht ohne prüfbaren Rendering-/Crawlability-Vertrag aus dem DOM entfernen.
Die Cache-first-Service-Worker-Skizze ist keine vollständige Cache-/Update-/Fehlerstrategie; nicht routinemässig hinzufügen. API-Caching muss Daten- und Nutzerkontext berücksichtigen.
Debounce eines Scrollhandlers ist nicht automatisch die richtige Lösung für laufende visuelle Scrollreaktionen. Ebenso vermeiden View Transitions nicht automatisch jede Render- oder Layoutarbeit.
Browseranteile, Baseline-Jahreszahlen und Kompressionsgewinne sind zeit-/kontextabhängige Angaben. Keine aktuellen Support-, SEO- oder Conversiongarantien daraus ableiten.
DevTools-MCP-spezifische Routingregeln gelten nur für dessen tatsächlich vorhandene Tools. Fehlende Feld-/Trace-Werkzeuge sind keine Pflichtinstallation und kein Grund, unabhängige Arbeit zu stoppen.
Neue Telemetrieanbieter oder Datenflüsse werden durch Recherche nicht autorisiert. Die Nutzerpräferenz verbietet künstliche Sparbudgets; sinnvolle zusätzliche Messungen bleiben möglich.

entries.destination: SEO page-map/technical QA; metadata and schema checks in ui-playbook
principles: Check rendered metadata and semantics with available tools, then independently inspect HTTP status/redirects, robots controls, sitemap coverage, canonicals and source HTML; Lighthouse is a technical subset, not ranking evidence.

Use accurate distinct page titles and descriptions, natural topics and meaningful link text. Treat 50–60/150–160 characters as rough lint proxies; review visible width and query-dependent rewriting instead of fixed limits.

Include canonical indexable URLs in the sitemap and use truthful lastmod dates; keep resources needed for rendering crawlable. Make links real anchors and provide indexable content before browser-only enhancements.

Correct the source pagination example using the fetched Google guidance: each page needs its own URL and canonical; link sequential pages with anchor hrefs. Google no longer uses rel=next/prev for pagination, and button-only load-more does not expose subsequent content to its crawler.

Use stable identifiers and absolute URLs in JSON-LD that describes visible, verified content; validate syntax and separately check current feature eligibility. Never invent aggregate ratings, offer values or organisation details.

Keep heading hierarchy unambiguous without declaring multiple h1 elements an automatic failure. Supply appropriate html lang and reciprocal, page-specific alternates when multilingual pages actually exist.
Provide descriptive or empty decorative alt text as appropriate, explicit image dimensions, responsive modern sources and below-fold lazy loading; do not lazy-load critical hero/LCP imagery.

Separate search crawling, training permissions and user-directed retrieval by documented agent. llms.txt remains optional/consumer-specific; WebMCP is a scoped integration, not a rankings or AI-citation shortcut.
conflicts: The source header label security headers for SEO trust signals is unsupported: choose security headers for actual security needs, not a claimed ranking boost. Robots Disallow is not access control.
Reject canonicalising all pagination to page one and the implication that rel=prev/next solves current Google pagination; primary Google reference read and saved.

Reject universal <75-character URL restrictions, blanket parameter avoidance, fixed tap-size/font-size pass criteria and automatic nofollow paired with noindex; assess the actual page and applicable requirements.
Do not promise rankings, rich results, search indexing, AI ingestion/citation or field CWV from lab checks. Do not claim source crawler tables or optional tooling were independently reverified here.
No automatic Search Console submission, new external integrations or publishing; actual tool availability and authorisation remain intact.

entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; DESIGN.md semantic tokens/art direction; existing-stack UnoCSS adapter; redesign safeguards
principles: State the design reading from page kind, real audience, reference observations and existing brand before selecting variance, motion and density. Treat dials as descriptions of deliberate choices.
Treat semantic tokens as a stable interface: centralize surface, text, action, status, layout and named-depth families; use the equivalent CSS custom properties/classes in HTML projects.

When UnoCSS already exists, keep extractable literal class strings, verify shortcut/modifier behavior and use the project's generation conventions; do not assume dynamically assembled class names will be generated.
Specify nested radius relationships, optical icon alignment, subtle image-edge treatment and purposeful flat/elevated surfaces. Judge actual pixels instead of applying every decorative treatment.

Use interruptible property-specific transitions for repeated state changes, avoid transition:all, keep changing numeric widths stable with tabular figures and reserve monospace for technical metadata.
Vary section composition according to content jobs; repeated equal-card grids or image/text alternation should be a deliberate page-family pattern rather than an automatic template.

For redesigns inventory brand tokens, functional content, navigation, routes and SEO baseline; evolve typography/spacing first when they solve the brief, and track intentional changes to URLs, forms and proof.
Reject decorative telemetry, unverified statistics and imitation product screenshots; use actual component previews, licensed real assets or clearly identified mock material.
conflicts: Reject UnoCSS-first as a site-wide requirement, compulsory dual themes, marketing dial defaults, one-accent/no-white/no-black rules, dash bans and automatic serif/Inter exclusions.
Low-opacity text tokens (op30/op25) and 10px micro text can fail readability; semantic naming is not a contrast measurement. title alone is not an accessible full-value reveal.
The 'mobile-safe' shell uses h-screen/w-screen, fixed large left padding and overflow clipping; it is not automatically safe on mobile browser chrome or RTL layouts.
Micro-interaction rules conflict with other sources (100ms staggers versus 50ms, 40px targets versus 44px, shadows versus borders). Resolve by task, measured motion and actual target geometry.
Reduced motion is incorrectly limited to motion beyond hover/active or a dial above 3; any relevant nonessential motion must respect the chosen accessibility contract.
The '70% value at 40% risk' redesign estimate and strongest-AI-tell claims lack evidence; exclude them. Do not generate believable fake names/numbers as real business proof.
Pure-black shadow starter examples conflict with later no-black-shadow advice; retain brand-appropriate, measured tokens rather than copying a contradictory palette.
entries.reason: Integrate token semantics, brief-reading, craft and migration awareness; keep UnoCSS implementation details conditional and strip aesthetic mandates.

entries.destination: Figma motion adapter and UI playbook: faithful design-to-code motion; installed Figma specialist retains tool calls and runtime contracts
principles: Treat static design context as structure and motion context as animated-node inventory and values; join exact node IDs first, then fallback backing-component IDs, preserving per-instance scope.

Walk every animated node even when static output uses plain paragraphs, divs or images. Reuse generated timing, keyframes, easing and per-element transform origins; do not infer animation from JSX tags or sibling order.
Use timeline cohorts to drive related nodes through one shared duration/loop lifecycle; factor identical snippets into constants or parameterized components without changing their authored values.

Keep static layout transforms separate from animated transforms. Preserve wrapper/static-transform/inner nesting and subtract an already-applied base rotation from absolute animation values to avoid double rotation.
Keep static display:contents wrappers layout-transparent. An animated group needs a real box with equivalent scene bounds; recheck child coordinates and the static frame after inserting that box.

For path-level motion inline the actual SVG, retain viewBox, defs, geometry and wrapper layout, then animate the matching path. Use pathLength=1 when dash values are normalized; whole-object motion can remain on the existing wrapper.
Preserve HOLD as step-end, apply zero-duration final states statically, and inspect exported SVG bytes for baked t=0 invisibility that parent opacity cannot undo.

Use emitted CSS keyframes for HTML/vanilla and the existing motion stack for compatible islands. Observe one entire loop, including nested pivots and appearance timing, before spreading a pattern to many nodes.

Keep feature-limit evidence tied to the actual tool response: Smart Animate, masks, shaders and partial path trims may need explicit adaptation or an inspected media fallback. Reduced motion must retain visible meaningful content and correct state.
conflicts: The installed Figma specialist, not this research copy, owns real get_design_context/get_motion_context instructions and any exact lint-message requirements. A missing tool cannot be invented; this extraction performed no Figma calls.
Do not turn recommendations for particles, springs or scroll effects into mandatory libraries or a replacement for Scrollcraft. CSS is appropriate for simple glass and stroke drawing.

The gotcha claiming RGB red-to-blue necessarily becomes grey and that color-interpolation-filters controls general Motion interpolation is unreliable. Choose/measure the actual interpolation implementation; do not copy that fix.
A parent opacity of 1 cannot repair opacity=0 baked into an SVG child; remove or reassign the baked animated property at its true owner. The suggested parent-only fallback is insufficient.
Do not generalize the tentative rotation-pivot sign workaround; verify coordinates and a full loop. Preserve static groups unless the group itself animates.

Fallback claims that video is always accurate, animated WebP/APNG is inherently lower bandwidth, or SMIL is deprecated-ish are not reliable guarantees. Verify actual export contents, size and browser support.

Source references disagree on wrapper-only SVG inlining and on whether unsupported features permit approximation. Prefer the smallest correct motion target and actual specialist/runtime contract; record fidelity loss explicitly.
entries.reason: Highly useful when the project contains authored Figma motion; all six delegated deep dives were fetched and read. Tool-specific procedure remains with the installed specialist rather than being copied into generic Web.

Record visible change, trigger, target and resulting state. Distinguish click, hover, keyboard, scroll, timer and unknown trigger rather than guessing from cursor proximity.
Place markers only on clearly visible targets/results; retain inferred/uncertain flags and suppress misleading confident markers. Store normalized coordinates as machine metadata, not visible copy.
Keep timestamps, source frames, dimensions, image quality and annotation text in a local manifest before producing the storyboard.

For an authorized Figma handoff, retain node IDs, upload/image hashes and verification status so failed uploads can resume without duplicate pages; verify nonblank images and marker alignment in the resulting canvas.
conflicts: Figma output is conditional; recording analysis can feed DESIGN.md and browser QA directly. Do not create a Design file or upload recording assets merely because this source prescribes it.
Reject pip --break-system-packages, mandatory provider capabilities and fixed 5–15-moment limits. Scout sampling does not prove a short transition was absent.
A static storyboard documents observed states, not a working interaction or full behavioral validation. Keep the existing watch/video analysis and installed Figma tool instructions.
entries.reason: The main document contains the full decision method; executable frame/upload helpers were recorded as ancillary and were not executed.

entries.destination: references/ui-playbook.md — optional ASCII visual module with semantic fallback
principles: Use a brightness-to-glyph ramp with deliberate foreground/background polarity; measure actual monospace cell width and line height and derive rows = columns × sourceAspect × cellAspect to avoid vertical stretch.

Use one pre/textContent string for a modest monochrome field and canvas for larger or per-glyph-color output; avoid thousands of changing DOM spans. Benchmark grid size and refresh rate on the actual device.
Downsample image/video once into a small offscreen canvas and read the whole pixel buffer once per source frame. Wait for dimensions/fonts to settle and handle cross-origin pixel-access failures.
With Three.js AsciiEffect, append its DOM target, render through effect.render and keep camera/effect dimensions synchronized. Controls should bind to the actual interactive target.

Inject time and seed randomness for deterministic screenshots of multiple moments; define the time unit explicitly. Freeze or stop nonessential loops for reduced motion/offscreen states and keep meaningful content outside the character field.
conflicts: ASCII is a conditional visual language, not inherently lightweight at every grid size. Per-frame text replacement or canvas pixel readback can be expensive; terminal ANSI delivery is outside this Web consolidation.

The luminance formula applies weights to gamma-encoded channels; it is a stylized brightness approximation, not WCAG relative luminance. Ramp labels/counts are inconsistent; verify polarity with a known black-to-white image.
The complete Three.js sample adds PointLight.position.set(...), which returns a Vector3 rather than a light, to scene.add. The prose also names nonexistent getImageContext. Do not copy either defect.
The seek example mixes descriptions of seconds with millisecond samples; normalize units. The examples omit loading/error/disposal and meaningful accessibility treatment.
Reject the required standalone/CDN output and green terminal aesthetic. Adapt only if the reference, brand and visitor task justify it.
entries.reason: A useful specialist visual recipe for selected technical/creative brands, with specific sampling and reproducibility lessons. Full rendering support was read; no animation was built.
