Covers generative ASCII fields, image/video/3D-to-ASCII, and animated character art for both web and terminal.

entries.destination: Web optional material/effect recipes + references/screenshots.md; existing motion/GPT Image/Scrollcraft retained
principles: Use glass only when the chosen visual direction calls for layered translucency. Its useful visual controls are backdrop frost, alpha fill, lit edge and elevation; demonstrate it over actual varied content.

A masked pseudo-element can draw a specular rim independently of text; a very faint grain layer can reduce visible gradient banding when that artifact actually exists. Decorative layers must not intercept input.
Separate readability from material: put a stable scrim or sufficient solid fill behind text and measure contrast against the worst relevant region/frame of the actual backdrop.
Provide solid readable fallbacks for reduced transparency and missing backdrop-filter support; reduced motion must stop sweep/refraction as well as transitions. Test the fallback as rendered.
Limit large and nested blur surfaces; prefer movement/opacity of a static effect layer to continuously changing blur radius, shadow geometry or turbulence. Measure on representative hardware.
Treat SVG displacement as distortion of SourceGraphic, not proof of correct background lens refraction. Keep readable content on a stable separate layer and inspect the actual result.

For deterministic QA, expose state and time controls, pin CSS animation currentTime and SVG SMIL time after readiness, and compare rest/hover/entry plus start/mid/end frames. Combine contact-sheet context with readable details.
For a standalone effect study, HTML/CSS plus optional inline SVG can be sufficient; integrate the approved effect into the actual project rather than forcing a separate application framework.
conflicts: Do not require glass, four decorative ingredients, grain, a 20px radius or a busy backdrop across all website surfaces. Reduced-transparency fallback may and should be fully opaque.

Animating box-shadow/background is paint work, not universally cheap. translateZ(0) does not guarantee improvement, nested blur is not established as universally quadratic, and fixed blur/count limits are heuristics.
The sweep example animates left continuously; replace with a measured transform-based implementation when used. The SKILL reduced-motion snippet misses the CSS sweep while the full recipe handles it.
The initial contrast test names the brightest background only; that is relevant for light text, whereas dark text can fail on darker regions. Test the worst actual text/background pairing.

The freeze harness alone does not create matching forced-hover CSS and can miss animations not created yet or target the wrong SVG. A query-class fallback test is not proof of OS media-query integration.
The linked skill-local scripts/README.md returns 404. Equivalent repository-root scripts/README.md was found, retrieved and read; actual helper shell scripts remain unread and unexecuted.
entries.reason: Main SKILL, full glass recipe and recovered toolkit README read. Useful conditional effect and deterministic motion QA material, not a new default aesthetic or provider.

principles: Inventory existing motion across CSS, inline styles, component variants and keyframes using five dimensions: duration, distance, scale, blur and easing. Classify the interaction's purpose before assigning a token; leave unmatched uses alone rather than snapping to the nearest number.

Make dismissal prompt and quieter than entry; remove gratuitous exit travel/blur and avoid delayed closes. Reversible operations such as tabs, text swaps and accordions can share a symmetric duration.

For infrequent sequences, start around 40ms stagger or 80ms for a few large items; bound the total waiting time, using the actual last-item delay of (count-1)*offset plus the animation duration when judging completion.
Use delays for intent filtering or deliberate sequencing, not as compensation for slow animation. Check hover-in and return separately while preserving prompt feedback.
Map adopted values into existing semantic custom properties; tune only the affected motion values. Record rationale and verify full-speed use, interruption and reduced-motion/static feedback.
conflicts: Reject confirmation-before-every-edit, automatic token-file installation, Refine-panel assumptions and a mandatory companion installation.
Do not force the source scale, default smooth-out curve, blur addition or strong bouncing hover-out on all brands. Frequent interactions may be instant.
Reduced-motion and performance hygiene are described as future expansion in the source; they must come from the existing Web contract, not be claimed as implemented by this skill.
The source's offset×count shorthand overstates the last start delay; distinguish start staggering from total sequence duration.
entries.reason: Adds a practical semantic motion-audit model and open/close/stagger decisions without requiring a library or global visual style.

source.description: Polish and refine existing motion against the transitions.dev motion-token scale — duration, distance, scale, blur, easing, and when each token applies.

entries.destination: references/ui-skills.md routing; references/ui-playbook.md relevant tactics; existing-complex-React-app adapter; form/pending-state notes; SSR evidence contract
principles: Use data mode only for an existing or justified complex React application with route-level loaders/actions; it does not replace HTML routes for ordinary service pages.
Represent search/filter state with GET form parameters so the result is linkable; choose navigation-producing Form submissions for actual navigations and fetchers for bounded inline mutations.
Distinguish idle, submitting and revalidating/loading states at the relevant scope; preserve user input and provide meaningful local errors and completion feedback.
Derive optimistic display from the pending submission plus authoritative data only for reversible/predictable operations; implement failure, retry and concurrency behavior explicitly.
For manual SSR, keep shared route definitions, query via createStaticHandler, handle Response redirects, render StaticRouterProvider and hydrate with compatible serialized data.
Deliver the real initial document, extracted CSS, correct statuses, route metadata and crawlable links; verify HTML before hydration rather than equating createBrowserRouter with server rendering.
conflicts: The client createBrowserRouter action examples call db directly; browser-side actions require a real server/API boundary and must not expose database code or secrets.

The claim that failed optimistic mutations always revalidate and roll back automatically is too broad; behavior depends on action/error/revalidation semantics and actual version. Test explicit failure paths.
The sample 'automatic' optimistic state can remain stale if pending data is not scoped to the lifecycle; rapid repeated submissions and failed responses need explicit verification.
SSR examples return default 200 for nonredirect error contexts and reference /client.tsx directly; production integration needs correct HTTP status propagation and built assets.
Manual SSR instructions oversimplify server/client loader separation; shared route modules must not pull server-only capabilities into the client bundle.
Reject default fetcher/optimistic behavior for every mutation and new React/SSR infrastructure without application complexity. Screenshots cannot certify SEO or crawlability.
entries.reason: Useful for preserving a viable React app and improving real form states, conditional on genuine application scope; not a default Web stack.

source.description: Build React applications using React Router data mode with createBrowserRouter, loaders, actions, Form, useFetcher, and pending or optimistic UI.

entries.destination: Web app-only routing adapter; native-link and URL-state principles
principles: Use BrowserRouter declarative mode only inside an actual React application whose complexity justifies it; static service pages and simple Astro islands retain real document routes.
Within that app use nested routes and Outlet for shared layouts, index routes for parent defaults, dynamic params for identifiers and an explicit unmatched-route experience.
Use Link/NavLink for navigational controls so users retain keyboard, context-menu, middle-click and bookmark behavior; reserve imperative navigation for completed operations or actual redirects.
Preserve unrelated query parameters and multi-value filters when updating URL state; use replacement history for incremental typing when appropriate so Back does not replay each keystroke.
Represent pagination with links and stable query URLs; validate missing/malformed params and clarify route-relative versus path-relative navigation.
Test direct deep links, refresh, Back/Forward, active navigation, input labels and query preservation; separately verify HTTP statuses and initial HTML for any indexable route.
conflicts: The ban on native internal anchors is specific to its SPA preference and is rejected for HTML-first websites and cross-island/page navigation.
The reference's claim that a root NavLink remains active everywhere without end is inaccurate for current React Router root special handling; do not propagate it as a defect rule.
Examples overwrite unrelated search params and omit input labels despite later preservation guidance. parseInt plus isNaN is not strict validation of a complete numeric identifier.

preventScrollReset depends on the appropriate scroll-restoration integration; a declarative BrowserRouter alone does not supply framework/data-router loaders or actions, initial HTML, HTTP 404s or SEO guarantees.
entries.reason: Retains good link/URL-state behavior for a justified application while preventing React Router from displacing the site's indexable HTML routes.

source.description: Build React applications using React Router declarative mode with BrowserRouter, Routes, Link, NavLink, and URL or search params without loaders or actions.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md: Motion-Tokens und Zustandsverträge; UI-Craft-/Library-Adapter; Motion-QA
principles: Motion nach Zweck ordnen: Zustandswechsel, Eintritt/Austritt, räumliche Beziehung oder direkte Rückmeldung. Häufigkeit und verzögerte Bedienbarkeit bei der Entscheidung berücksichtigen; ständig wiederholte Dekoration eher entfernen.

Eintritt, Austritt und Änderungen sichtbarer Elemente als getrennte Motion-Rollen dokumentieren. Die Quellwerte 150/100 ms für Popover und 300/200 ms für Sheets dienen als abstimmbare Beispiele; grosse Distanzen anders behandeln als kleine Zustandswechsel.

Positionierte Overlays vom Trigger aus transformieren und ihre Einflugrichtung an der tatsächlichen Seite ausrichten. Bei Base UI dessen transform-origin-Variable nutzen, in nativer Umsetzung die entsprechende Geometrie selbst korrekt bestimmen.
Für interaktive Zustandsänderungen explizite CSS-Transition-Properties statt transition-all einsetzen; schnelle Richtungswechsel müssen eine laufende Bewegung sauber auf den neuen Zustand umlenken.

Press-Feedback behutsam nach Kontrollgrösse abstimmen und nur bei no-preference aktivieren. Hover-Effekte auf hover-fähige Eingabegeräte beschränken; Pseudoelemente ausdrücklich in Reduced-Motion-Regeln einbeziehen.
Will-change nur für tatsächlich animierende Elemente und während des relevanten Zeitraums setzen. Transform/Opacity bevorzugen, aber reale Renderkosten im Browser prüfen.

Bei tatsächlicher Verwendung von Vaul oder Sonner deren Motion-Props und Lebenszyklus nutzen; keine zweite konkurrierende Animation um die Bibliothekskomponente legen. Tooltips in einer Gruppe können nach der ersten bewussten Aktivierung ohne wiederholte Verzögerung reagieren.

Gesten bei begründetem Bedarf mit Pointer Capture, einer aktiven Pointer-ID, Widerstand an Grenzen und klarer Abgrenzung zum Inhaltsscrollen bauen. Tastaturbedienung und persistente Zustandsanzeige separat erhalten.

Reduced Motion als wirklichen Endzustand entwerfen: sichtbare Inhalte, bedienbare Controls und nachvollziehbarer Status müssen auch ohne Slide, Scale oder Keyframes bestehen. In QA auch Pseudoelemente und schnelle Open/Close-Wechsel prüfen.
conflicts: Die exakt kopierbaren Tailwind-/Base-UI-Klassen verlangen konkrete Tokens, Varianten und Animationspakete. Nicht als frameworkfreies CSS ausgeben und keine Tailwind-/React-Migration daraus ableiten; tatsächliche shadcn-Bausteine dürfen statisch oder als interaktive Astro-React-Islands eingebunden werden.

Interne Widersprüche: niemals ease-in vs ease-in-quart beim Austritt; nur Transform/Opacity/clip-path vs Breite, Höhe, Margin, Farbe und Schatten in eigenen Beispielen; unter 300 ms vs 350–500 ms für bestimmte Komponenten.

clip-path ist nicht universell garantiert compositor-only; CSS-Variablen sind nicht grundsätzlich verboten und Keyframes nicht grundsätzlich ununterbrechbar. Solche Performanceaussagen als messabhängig behandeln.

Pauschal keine tastaturausgelöste Animation, Mindestskalierungen und Pflicht-Custom-Easings sind Produktpräferenzen, keine Accessibility- oder Qualitätsgesetze. Rückmeldung darf Tastaturnutzenden nicht verloren gehen.
Einige kopierte Overlay-/Checkbox-Snippets enthalten trotz Checkliste keine vollständige Reduced-Motion-Abdeckung. Keine Konformität aus der Klassenliste behaupten.
entries.reason: Konkrete, weitgehend in natives CSS übertragbare Interaktionsmuster. Bibliotheksdetails, Zahlen und Performanceabsolutismen werden klar vom allgemeinen Motion-Vertrag getrennt.

source.description: Prototyper UI animation conventions for writing, reviewing, or debugging transition code, overlay enter/exit, press feedback, and prefers-reduced-motion.

entries.destination: Component-islands/library migration adapter; apply only to a requested Radix migration
principles: Inspect the existing package manager, installed versions, components.json and wrapper/consumer dependency graph; establish build/typecheck baseline and distinguish pre-existing failures.
Compare each wrapper with its exact stock origin, using the recorded style verbatim. Preserve custom text, icon, token and behavioural changes when adopting a corresponding Base UI wrapper.

For progressive migration keep old/new wrappers side by side and move consumers in dependency order; only change global style/dependencies after remaining consumers permit it. Detect existing partial migration from source instead of restarting.

Map asChild to render and positionable overlays from Portal/Content to Portal/Positioner/Popup. If a wrapper declares align/side/offset props, destructure and forward them to Positioner; a type-correct fallthrough onto Popup silently breaks placement.

Review consumer value and callback contracts: Accordion/ToggleGroup arrays, Select nullable values, Checkbox indeterminate boolean, Slider commit rename, initial/final focus and menu activation/dismissal differences.

Rewrite state selectors, transform-origin/anchor-size variables and entry/exit transitions by actual rendered attributes. :disabled styling can stop working when the replacement root is a span or exposes aria-disabled/data-disabled.

Sweep even clean three-way merges for stale Radix imports, registry placeholders and wrong consumer props. Verify keyboard/typeahead, focus return, hover timing, visual alignment and submitted values in the browser.

Keep unrelated cmdk/vaul/sonner/input-otp/calendar/chart wrappers out of a Radix-only migration. Legacy styles with no Base counterpart need source-preserving transforms rather than an unrequested style change.
conflicts: No automatic migration, latest-CLI execution, installation, clean-tree stop gate, component-per-commit rule or whole-site React conversion. HTML-first static rendering and interactive Astro React islands remain allowed.

Source tables target @base-ui/react 1.6.0 and include unresolved TODOs; verify installed type declarations and live registry before transforming an uncertain part. Root files resolved the initial assumed references/ 404s.
wrapper-shapes.md gives conflicting ContextMenu submenu offsets (-3 example versus +4 correction); do not copy literal alignment constants without current evidence.
Flag behaviour deltas, but the source prohibition on restoring them does not override an authorised behaviour-preserving migration. Do not silently remove focus/dismissal features with no equivalent.
Golden registry output is not automatically correct: the source itself notes dead disabled classes and merge residue. No claimed complete migration from build success alone.

entries.destination: Installed Apple web-app/browser-quirk adapter; touch/safe-area QA
principles: Route iPhone/iPad Home Screen separately from macOS Add to Dock. Preserve existing auth, manifest, scrolling and product decisions unless the requested installed-app symptom requires change.

For edge-to-edge iOS controls use a base dimension plus safe-area inset; zero is valid. Mirror inset values once if needed, but never hide the interface while waiting for a positive inset or treat computed 0px as readiness.
Preserve pinch zoom and body-text selection. Scope touch suppression, long-press changes and tap-highlight removal to controls with an intentional replacement interaction and visible feedback.

Keep focused input, dismissal and scrolling reachable when the keyboard opens. For a reproduced viewport defect inspect visualViewport and scrollingElement, initialise synchronisation on open and remove listeners/cancel pending frames on close.

Validate installation assets by anonymous HTTP response, type and dimensions; sign-in redirects can break icon selection. Keep a common icon artwork source and check installed appearance separately after fresh installation.

Inspect actual emitted head tags/manifest and applicable platform icon formats. iOS startup-image prerequisites and Mac manifest icons have different contracts; optional startup assets are not required for every website.

When browser controls are hidden, supply a usable back/out path and verify internal, external and authentication navigation. Detect display-mode appropriately rather than assuming iOS navigator.standalone exists on Mac.

Separate documented platform behaviour, dated device observations and community workarounds. Record OS/build/browser/orientation/install state for appearance checks; desktop emulation cannot prove installed safe-area, tint or splash behaviour.
conflicts: No universal 100vh/100dvh replacement, forced app scroll root, fixed 64px iPad padding, translucent/glass styling, install hint or manifest requirement.

Version-specific 26.x sampling thresholds and workarounds are inherited source observations, not newly tested results. Reproduce the symptom and check current platform documentation before adopting them.
No service-worker/offline/push expansion, authentication/storage migration or iOS asset generation for Mac-only work.
The conformance checklist is a product recipe checklist, not WCAG certification. Actual hardware limitations must be reported as unverified, not replaced with synthetic device claims.
External URLs in sources.md were inventoried as ancillary, not independently reread; the private production experience cannot be independently retrieved.

entries.destination: Web complex-interaction/architecture handoff diagrams; existing visualization specialist
principles: When a website change is difficult to explain, diagram responsibilities, runtimes and system boundaries with unchanged direct neighbors that establish impact.
Use distinct architecture and ordered data-flow views; add a narrower child view only when it contributes information rather than mirroring folders or duplicating its parent.
Choose one principal relationship to emphasize; add a sequence only when temporal order matters.
Attach actual source/revision references to diagram entities and validate referential integrity among edges, flow participants, view selections and walkthrough steps.
Describe a walkthrough step as a concrete behavior change with a consequence; group consecutive steps on the same view to avoid unnecessary camera travel.
Keep persistent interpretation corrections separate from regenerated diagrams and detect corrections whose selectors no longer match.
conflicts: Do not auto-install a CLI, use external inference providers, publish a public prlens.dev canvas, alter .gitignore, or attach/comment on PRs from a diagram request without matching authorization.
Animated SVG, dark theme, numerical view/step quotas and mandatory walkthroughs are renderer conventions, not Web design requirements.
Diagram/schema validity does not verify implementation behavior, accessibility, security or change correctness; comprehension and code review remain distinct.
Preserve source diagrams and evidence when useful; do not adopt blanket 'never commit any generated artifact' as a Web rule.
entries.reason: Conditional value for complex component islands, forms and integrations; ordinary service pages do not need an additional architecture-diagram pipeline.

entries.destination: DESIGN.md/handoff explanation aids and optional local visual decision artifacts
principles: Choose the smallest representation that clarifies the question: pseudocode for logic, a call tree for execution, a shallow file tree for ownership and a component tree for UI/state boundaries.
Use a diff when an existing shape changes and enough surrounding context remains to establish ownership/order; show the whole block when most of it is new or readers need a copyable target.
For a visual comparison too dense for a diagram, create one focused responsive artifact with real labels/data and the project's type, spacing and colours.
Place each visual beside the short explanation it supports and omit unrelated nodes, calls and implementation detail.
conflicts: This is a communication aid, not a website implementation or quality-review workflow. A diagram does not replace route coverage, browser inspection or actual interaction testing.

Do not execute the source's Bash(open ...) literally or invent an application-launch tool. Use the host's supported artifact/rendering mechanism, including an installed visualization specialist when appropriate.
No need to generate a separate HTML artifact when a concise explanation or existing evidence already answers the question.
entries.reason: Self-contained, practical mapping from explanation need to artifact shape; retain as an optional handoff technique rather than adding another mandatory output.

source.description: Help the user understand the current topic visually with concise diagrams, code-shape sketches, Mermaid flows, diffs, and focused HTML artifacts.

entries.destination: ui-skills/ui-playbook: data-visualisation patterns; DESIGN.md data-encoding contract
principles: Choose a chart from the actual data shape and reader task: comparison, time series, composition, distribution, hierarchy or record paths; separately assess label capacity and expected reading time. Familiar bars/lines are valid first choices for quick service-page evidence.

Define what position, length, area, luminance and each repeated unit mean before selecting geometry. Preserve zero-based bar-length comparisons; use square-root radius scaling for area-encoded circles, and let a treemap layout encode area directly from nonnegative weights.

Distinguish a true 100% composition from independently answered multi-select percentages; a dot representing one percentage point must not be presented as a real individual. Explain rounding and denominators without inventing records.

Give each chart an evidence-supported takeaway, units, time range, legend and real source. A second chart must answer a different question; report composition should follow the commissioned narrative rather than the number of columns in a dataset.

Define semantic chart colour roles alongside the site tokens: background, text, muted text, grid, data, emphasis, ordinal ramp or categories. Keep category meanings stable and redundant through labels/shape/position; recheck contrast after role changes.

Use a real hover/pin interaction only when a mark represents inspectable data. For dense paths enlarge the hit area separately from the visible stroke; Web adaptation must add equivalent keyboard/touch access and a textual/table route to important values.

Use deterministic fixtures for repeatable screenshot QA. If adopting a template, record its exact gallery file, chart title and rendering block, replace all demo data and inspect the actual implementation rather than claiming reuse from a visual resemblance.

The fetched basics gallery demonstrates countable rung bars and a two-level treemap with full-path/value/share tooltip; preserve those encoding ideas while adapting responsive layout, readable labels and interaction semantics to Web.
conflicts: Reject mandatory Lupi-before-Basics-before-Glance ranking, minimum-three-candidate proofs, per-page chart quotas, forced template non-repetition and exact family geometry as general Web gates.

Reject fixed Inter/Mono/preset-only aesthetics, bans on brand colour or >6-category colour, and arbitrary 24px radii. A coherent semantic palette can support several chart roles without using one preset.

Reject 5.5/6.5px SVG label minima and hover-only overflow handling. mono-tokens.js has low-contrast muted/source colours, click-only replay and fixed two-column CSS; its reduced-motion CSS does not prove JS/ECharts animation is disabled.

The prose requires no bounce while mono-tokens.js uses scale(0) pop overshoot. The gallery also duplicates tokens and lacks the main token stylesheet reduced-motion block in its opening CSS. Source instructions are not proof of accessible implementation.
The source labels paired series as causal; chart co-movement alone cannot establish causality. No statistical, geographical-compliance or conversion claim is imported.
Creator attribution prompt is not a workflow requirement; check actual licence obligations before copying source/assets. Main tables disagree on catalogue numbering/counts, so use exact titles/files.

entries.destination: UI playbook: hierarchy, spacing, typography, surfaces and image presentation; DESIGN.md token rationale
principles: Choose a small, purposeful spacing/type/opacity/elevation vocabulary; compare a candidate value with its immediate smaller and larger neighbours instead of accumulating near-identical one-off values.
Build a real functional unit at a constrained width before letting it spread across a large canvas. Start generous with whitespace, then tighten according to the task's intended density.
Establish hierarchy with weight and contrast as well as size. When the primary element cannot stand out, reduce competing emphasis rather than making it ever larger.

Give groups more outside space than inside space. Keep data labels where users scan by label and always preserve accessible names for controls; visual heading size remains separate from semantic heading structure.
Use fixed or bounded widths for sidebars, forms and content with an optimal measure; scale headlines and small UI independently across viewports and align mixed-size text on baselines.

Distinguish decorative dividers from functional control boundaries in tokens. Normal text needs 4.5:1 for WCAG AA; large text means 24px regular or about 18.67px bold, and required non-text boundaries need 3:1.
For quiet status treatments, try dark semantic text on a pale tint instead of a saturated fill with white text. Measure every actual foreground/surface pair, including raised surfaces in dark mode.

Model elevation using contact and cast shadows with distinct blur/offset: contact darkens near the surface and fades with elevation. Put combined shadows in one comma-separated declaration; raised/inset highlights must be lighter than the actual surface.

Handle images at their intended display scale: crop a meaningful screenshot region rather than shrinking a whole desktop interface, choose an optical favicon variant, and use consistent image containers with subtle edge separation.
When text overlays photos, manage the image's local contrast or add a scrim and inspect all responsive crops. Use the symptom-to-fix table diagnostically, then verify the actual pixels.
conflicts: Adopt constrained scales, not the exact mandatory number lists, universal HSL notation, two weights, single radius, no-black rule or a ban on em/clamp. Existing tokens and accessible fluid typography remain valid.
The main scale omits 1px yet says it covers borders; the supporting token file correctly has a separate border scale. Keep function-specific tokens rather than mechanically snapping hairlines to 4px.

HSL hue rotation and perceptual brightness formulas are design heuristics, not WCAG luminance calculations. OKLCH may be useful for new systems; changing a stable existing notation is not automatically an improvement.

Labels are not optional for form accessibility. Do not hide useful page titles, distinguish charts solely by lightness, make links discoverable only on hover or replace native controls merely to look less default.

Reject claims that popular fonts, five weights, blue/gold colour stereotypes or professional stock always beat authentic client photography. Brand fit and the GPT Image provenance module govern imagery.

The token file's self-described contrast verification is evidence about its declared starter pairs, not proof for edited values, translucent composition or the completed website. Remeasure and inspect relevant states.
Do not silently cut agreed features to the smallest version or delete functionality to satisfy the source's short-cycle advice.
entries.reason: Concrete hierarchy, optical alignment, shadow geometry and symptom-specific tactics transfer directly to HTML/custom CSS; all three delegated references and the complete token asset were read.

source.description: Design and improve user interfaces using Refactoring UI rules for constrained spacing, type, color, shadow scales, hierarchy, and depth.
